chapters.title: Chapter 351: Kai’s Shop
paragraphs: The notification didn’t end yet as Traceless received more.
[ Warning: Some tested poisons may cause severe pain, temporary paralysis, hallucinations, organ damage, or loss of consciousness. ]

[ Warning: Although the poisons used in the experiment are not classified as immediately lethal under normal testing conditions, serious complications may occur depending on the subject’s resistance. ]
[ Mission Reward upon Completion: 1 Skill Point, 1,200 Experience Points, 5 Gold ]
Traceless’s expression became slightly strange.
’Temporary paralysis? Hallucinations? Organ damage?’
He stared at the notification for a moment.
Furthermore, the antidotes provided couldn’t completely eliminate the danger either.
That was definitely a red flag!
Thankfully, this was just a game, and even if he really died, then he would just respawn after 24 hours!
However, he was concerned if the debuff would continue to haunt him...
’It’s dangerous, but I have four different advantages.’Levi muttered.
Furthermore, he would have access to antidotes and emergency treatment. Even if they can’t fully cure him, his Gene Skills should be strong enough to negate the other negative effects.
’If I can survive it, I’ll get another Skill Point.’
That was what mattered most.
One Skill Point could significantly improve one of his skills, and unlike ordinary Experience Points or credits, Skill Points were much harder to obtain.
Traceless looked at the two missions again.
One required him to spar with a noble child for four hours a day over five days.
The other required him to participate in at least three poison tests over seven days.
’One is easy, and the other is dangerous.’
Traceless’s lips slowly curled into a smile.
’But both are worth it.’
Traceless was already thinking about which abilities he wanted to improve.
His Spirit Barrier was still at Level 0, and he had only recently acquired it. Increasing its level would obviously make it more reliable during dangerous battles.
At the same time, there were several other skills that could benefit from additional levels.
’I’ll decide after I get the Skill Points.’
For now, there was no reason to rush.
He had just arrived in Leonine Town, and he had already found two missions that could provide exactly what he wanted.
More importantly, both missions lasted several days, which meant that he could use his time efficiently.
He could spend four hours each day sparring with the noble child, while the poison testing would only happen according to the researcher’s schedule.
That left him with plenty of time to explore the city, search for other missions, and perhaps even hunt powerful monsters outside Leonine Town.
Traceless couldn’t help but feel satisfied.
’Katrina was right.’
Leonine Town really did have better opportunities.

He had only just arrived, yet he had already obtained a Rare Item Chest, discovered two special missions with Skill Point rewards, and found a place where he could potentially improve his strength much faster than he could in Reverie Town.
Traceless looked toward the bustling Adventurers’ Guild.
For some reason, he felt that his journey in Perfect World was finally beginning to enter a new stage.
’Let’s see how much stronger I can become here.’
For the next several days, Kai’s life became surprisingly busy.

He would spend most of his time inside Perfect World, but every few hours, he would log out to check on the situation in Cameron City before returning to his room and putting on the Neural Gear once again.
The first thing he always did after logging out was check the World Chat and Guild Chat...
The second thing was usually asking Farrah about the shop.
"How are things?"
Farrah would always give him the same answer.
"Busy."
Kai initially thought she was exaggerating.
Then he stepped outside his room and saw the line of people waiting in front of the shop.
He stared at it for several seconds.
’Ah.’
Apparently, she wasn’t exaggerating.
Kai’s Shop, his shop, had become increasingly popular throughout Cameron City.

At first, it had only been a small shop selling strange items that survivors occasionally found useful. Most people who came in were simply curious because they had heard rumors about the shop’s unusual products.
However, after several weeks, word had begun spreading.
The shop always had something useful, the products were reliable, and the prices were reasonable.
And, most importantly, the owner somehow managed to restock items that other shops could no longer obtain.
Farrah had also become quite skilled at managing the store.
She had learned which products were in constant demand and which ones should only be brought out occasionally.
The fire extinguishers were among the most popular.
After all, fires were a constant danger in a city filled with temporary shelters, generators, electrical equipment, and improvised cooking areas.
The calming incense sets were also surprisingly popular.
Many survivors suffered from anxiety and stress after living through the apocalypse, and although incense couldn’t solve their problems, some people found that the familiar scent helped them relax.
Then there were the field tents, insulated sleeping bags, heavy-duty flashlights, thermal blankets, and heavy-duty raincoats.
Those products were especially popular among people who frequently traveled outside the city.
Farrah had quickly realized that she couldn’t sell everything at once.
If she emptied the shop’s inventory every day, people would eventually begin asking questions about where the products came from.
Instead, she began rotating the merchandise.
Sometimes, a customer would walk into the shop and find exactly what they expected.
Other times, they would discover something that hadn’t been available for several days.
That simple strategy made the shop feel as though it had a constantly changing inventory.
The food section was even more popular.
Canned goods disappeared quickly.
Instant noodles were almost impossible to keep in stock.
Granola bars were purchased by travelers and hunters who needed something convenient to carry.
Tea bags became popular among older survivors, while mayonnaise somehow became a surprisingly valuable item.
Kai had initially found that strange, but then, Farrah explained it to him.
"People miss normal food."
Kai could only nod.
That was something he understood.
In the apocalypse, even something as simple as adding mayonnaise to a meal could make a person feel like they were living normally again.
The shop also occasionally brought back older products like, folding bicycles, helmets, dried fruits and nuts, coffee sachets, wristwatches, water gallons, and finally, stainless steel tumblers.
All of them had come from Kai’s infinite gift pack talent!
Those items were never displayed at the same time.
Instead, Farrah would quietly bring them out when she thought the timing was appropriate.
It had created an interesting situation.
Some customers had started visiting the shop regularly.
One particular man, a middle-aged survivor named Gordon, had become a frequent customer.
He had purchased a folding bicycle during one of the shop’s earlier rotations and had apparently become quite attached to it.
Every few days, he would enter the shop and immediately ask the same question.
"Do you have anything new?"
"You were here yesterday." Farrah muttered as she gave him a tired look.
"I know."
"And the day before that."
"I know."
"So why are you asking?"
Gordon smiled proudly.
"Because you might have received something new today."
Farrah had no answer to that.
One afternoon, Gordon came into the shop again.
He looked around carefully before approaching the counter.
"Any coffee?"
Farrah shook her head.
"Not today."
"Tea?"
"Yes."
"How much?"
"Three boxes."
Gordon’s expression immediately became serious.
"I’ll take all of them."
Farrah raised an eyebrow.
"All three?"
"Yes."
"Why?"
Farrah sighed before placing the tea on the counter... "All yours."
"Nice..."
Gordon immediately paid... It was worth 600 Credits!
Outside this shop, Farrah could use those Credits to purchase three weeks of food!
But as Gordon was leaving, another customer entered.
The man was young, perhaps in his early twenties, and he immediately noticed the tea on Gordon’s hands.
"Wait."
Gordon stopped as soon as he heard this. The young man then looked at Farrah.
"Do you have more?"
Farrah thought for a moment before replying... "No."
"Are you sure?"
Farrah’s expression remained calm and she nodded.
The young man looked toward Gordon.
"How much did you pay for those?"
Gordon frowned.
"Why?"
"I want to buy them from you."
Gordon immediately tightened his grip around the boxes. There was no way he’d let that happen.
"No."
"I’ll pay more."
"Not possible."
"I’ll give you double."
Gordon looked offended and shook his head.
"Do you think I’m going to sell them after waiting three days to buy them?"
The young man frowned.
"It’s just tea."
Gordon stared at him.
"Then why are you offering double?"
The two men continued staring at each other until Farrah finally interrupted.
"Please leave."
The young man looked annoyed.
"I haven’t done anything."
"You’re blocking the entrance."
That finally ended the argument.
Gordon left with his tea while the young man reluctantly moved aside.
Farrah watched him go.
’Every day, there is something new.’
She had originally thought running a shop would be easy.
Now she understood why Kai had hired her.
However, the young man seemed problematic... she couldn’t help but worry a little.

chapters.title: Chapter 352: Cameron City
paragraphs: The situation surrounding Kai’s Shop gradually became more complicated as its reputation continued to spread throughout Cameron City.

At first, Farrah had thought that having more customers would only make her work more difficult, but she soon realized that the problem was not the number of people coming into the shop. The real problem was that other people had started paying attention to the business as well.
Kai’s Shop had originally been nothing more than a small store operating in a rented space belonging to the Aries Faction.
Because of its location, the shop had already enjoyed a certain degree of protection, but nobody had expected it to become this popular.
The products were simply too useful.

Every time Farrah managed to introduce a new item, people would quickly spread the information to their friends, and before long, more survivors would arrive to see whether they could purchase the same thing.

Some customers were only interested in food, while others came specifically looking for items that could help them survive outside the city. There were even people who visited regularly simply because they had become curious about what Kai’s Shop might sell next.
Naturally, the other factions could not ignore such a business forever.
One morning, Farrah noticed that something had changed when she looked outside the shop.
A new sign had appeared across the street.
She stared at it for several seconds before slowly turning toward the young man who had been helping her organize the shelves.
"Did someone open a new shop?"
The young man nodded.
"It opened this morning."
Farrah immediately frowned.

The shop across the street was significantly larger than Kai’s Shop, and unlike their small store, it had several shelves filled with different types of goods that were being sold at surprisingly low prices.
It didn’t take long for Farrah to understand what was happening.
"They’re trying to compete with us."
The young man looked toward the entrance.
"Is that a problem?"
Farrah remained silent for a moment.
Normally, she wouldn’t have cared.

Competition was not unusual, and Kai’s Shop had never relied on having no competitors. However, the situation was slightly different this time because the new shop was not simply selling any products...
They were selling the same products.

Flashlights, raincoats, sleeping bags, tents, canned food, instant noodles, and even some of the other supplies that Farrah had previously brought out during their merchandise rotations were now appearing across the street.
Furthermore, they were selling more than that...
"Seriously..."
Farrah’s expression became slightly strange.

The problem was that some of the products being sold by the new shop were even cheaper than theirs. Still, she couldn’t help but chuckle a little since she knew that they could never compete against Kai.
Kai could produce as many items as he could, and he had a wider range of products compared to what they had seen so far.
If Kai wanted, they would be able to sell more unique products that the others wouldn’t be able to copy at all.

’Still, they’re really quite resourceful. They actually have products similar to what Kai can produce. Wait... Is it another System Talent? But if that’s the case, they should’ve done it before... Maybe this is just their reserves?’
Farrah couldn’t help but wonder.
After all, it would be interesting if they really opened their vault just to mess with their shop.
In any case, this would certainly cause problems with their sale... Although she didn’t really care if the sale was weak, she still didn’t want to see their business being looked down upon...
However, despite having that thought, she couldn’t really do anything about it.
For ordinary survivors, their low price was naturally a very attractive offer.
By noon, several people who had originally intended to visit Kai’s Shop had already entered the new store instead.
Farrah stood behind the counter and watched the situation through the window.
"This is interesting... I guess Kai wouldn’t be bothered about this... So should we just ignore them?" She muttered to herself.
She wasn’t particularly worried about losing money.
However, their store’s popularity had already attracted too much attention, and Farrah understood that the sudden appearance of a competitor was probably not a coincidence.
The twelve factions controlled most of Cameron City’s resources, and although Aries and Libra were friendly toward Kai’s group, the other factions maintained a much more neutral attitude.
As for Cancer, Farrah had already heard enough rumors about them to know that they were not people she wanted to provoke.
She immediately contacted Kai.
It didn’t take long before he appeared in the shop.
Kai had just returned from Perfect World, and after hearing Farrah’s explanation, he immediately walked toward the window and looked at the store across the street.
"So they opened a shop here?"
"Yes."
"Are they causing trouble?"
"Not yet."
Farrah crossed her arms.
"But they’re clearly targeting us."
Kai didn’t immediately respond.
He studied the other shop carefully and noticed that several people were standing outside, handing out discounts and trying to attract customers.
"It looks like they’re trying to force us out through competition instead of directly attacking us."
"That’s what I think as well."
Kai nodded.
"Then let them."
Farrah looked at him with a smile. She expected that much, but she couldn’t help but ask, "You’re not worried?"
"Why would I be?"
Kai turned away from the window.
"If they’re selling ordinary supplies, we don’t have to fight them. We can simply sell something they don’t have."
Farrah immediately understood what he meant.
The other shop could copy their current products, but they had no idea where those products were coming from.
More importantly, they couldn’t copy everything.
Kai’s Shop still had access to an enormous variety of items that could never be obtained through ordinary means.
That afternoon, Farrah quietly changed the merchandise rotation.
The next customers who entered the shop were surprised to discover that the shelves no longer contained the same products that had been available in the morning.
Instead, Farrah placed several folding bicycles near the entrance, along with helmets and stainless steel tumblers.

A small section was also filled with dried fruits and nuts, coffee sachets, wristwatches, and several large water gallons... Furthermore, there was even a shelf filled with medicine or full medical kit!
Those items were the ones immediately purchased by the survivors. After that, the other products were also being sold!
"Wait, you sell these?"
One of the customers pointed toward the folding bicycles.
Farrah nodded.
"We have a limited supply."
The man’s eyes immediately brightened.
"How much?"
Before Farrah could answer, another customer who had been looking around the store suddenly rushed over.
"Wait a minute. You have coffee?"
The man’s voice was loud enough to attract everyone’s attention.
Farrah looked toward the shelf.
"Yes."
"How much?"
"One hundred Credits per pack... however, if you have C-Grade Cores, that would be better."
The man immediately grabbed several packs.
"I’ll take five."
The people around him immediately started looking toward the coffee.
Within minutes, the situation inside the shop became chaotic.

The customers who had originally been planning to buy canned goods suddenly began asking about the new products, and some of those who had visited the shop several times before were delighted to discover that Farrah had brought out items they had been searching for.
The new shop across the street could only watch as their own customers began crossing the road.
Just a day had passed and the competitor’s advantage had disappeared.
Farrah couldn’t help but smile.
Kai had been right.
There was no need to fight them.
As long as Kai’s Shop continued offering products that nobody else could obtain, the other shops could never completely replace them.
However, the situation did not end there.
Several days later, Farrah noticed that the same young man who had previously tried to buy Gordon’s tea was standing outside the shop again.
This time, he wasn’t alone... Three men were standing beside him.
Farrah immediately recognized the clothing they were wearing.
They belonged to one of the neutral factions.
She couldn’t determine exactly why they were there, but she knew better than to underestimate them.
The young man eventually entered the shop.
His eyes immediately moved around the room before settling on Farrah.
"I heard your shop has been selling some interesting things."
Farrah remained calm.
"We have many products."
"I can see that."
The man smiled.
"However, I think we should talk about where you obtain them."
The atmosphere inside the shop immediately changed as the other customers slowly stopped talking.
Still, Farrah’s expression remained unchanged.
"I’m afraid I don’t understand."
The young man smiled and continued.
"You suddenly have products that nobody else can obtain, yet you always seem to have more whenever people come looking for them. Don’t you think that’s a little suspicious?"
Farrah stared at him.
"Are you accusing us of something?"
"Of course not."
The man immediately shook his head.
"I’m simply curious. Apparently, some products in our vault had been missing..."

The other shop could copy their current products, but they had no idea where those products were coming from.
More importantly, they couldn’t copy everything.
Kai’s Shop still had access to an enormous variety of items that could never be obtained through ordinary means.
That afternoon, Farrah quietly changed the merchandise rotation.
The next customers who entered the shop were surprised to discover that the shelves no longer contained the same products that had been available in the morning.
Instead, Farrah placed several folding bicycles near the entrance, along with helmets and stainless steel tumblers.
A small section was also filled with dried fruits and nuts, coffee sachets, wristwatches, and several large water gallons...
Furthermore, there was even a shelf filled with medicine or full medical kit!
Those items were the ones immediately purchased by the survivors.
After that, the other products were also being sold!
"Wait, you sell these?"
One of the customers pointed toward the folding bicycles.
Farrah nodded.
"We have a limited supply."
The man’s eyes immediately brightened.
"How much?"
Before Farrah could answer, another customer who had been looking around the store suddenly rushed over.
"Wait a minute.
You have coffee?"
The man’s voice was loud enough to attract everyone’s attention.
Farrah looked toward the shelf.
"Yes."
"How much?"
"One hundred Credits per pack... however, if you have C-Grade Cores, that would be better."
The man immediately grabbed several packs.
"I’ll take five."
The people around him immediately started looking toward the coffee.
Within minutes, the situation inside the shop became chaotic.

The customers who had originally been planning to buy canned goods suddenly began asking about the new products, and some of those who had visited the shop several times before were delighted to discover that Farrah had brought out items they had been searching for.
The new shop across the street could only watch as their own customers began crossing the road.
Just a day had passed and the competitor’s advantage had disappeared.
Farrah couldn’t help but smile.
Kai had been right.
There was no need to fight them.
As long as Kai’s Shop continued offering products that nobody else could obtain, the other shops could never completely replace them.
However, the situation did not end there.
Several days later, Farrah noticed that the same young man who had previously tried to buy Gordon’s tea was standing outside the shop again.
This time, he wasn’t alone...
Three men were standing beside him.
Farrah immediately recognized the clothing they were wearing.
They belonged to one of the neutral factions.
She couldn’t determine exactly why they were there, but she knew better than to underestimate them.
The young man eventually entered the shop.
His eyes immediately moved around the room before settling on Farrah.
"I heard your shop has been selling some interesting things."
Farrah remained calm.
"We have many products."
"I can see that."
The man smiled.
"However, I think we should talk about where you obtain them."
The atmosphere inside the shop immediately changed as the other customers slowly stopped talking.
Still, Farrah’s expression remained unchanged.
"I’m afraid I don’t understand."
The young man smiled and continued.
"You suddenly have products that nobody else can obtain, yet you always seem to have more whenever people come looking for them.
Don’t you think that’s a little suspicious?"
Farrah stared at him.
"Are you accusing us of something?"
"Of course not."
The man immediately shook his head.
"I’m simply curious.
Apparently, some products in our vault had been missing..."

chapters.title: Chapter 353: The New Target
paragraphs: "I’m simply curious. Apparently, some products in our vault had been missing..."
Farrah’s expression didn’t change as he heard these words from the young man.
However, she immediately understood what the man was implying.

The atmosphere inside the shop had already become noticeably quieter. Several customers who had been browsing the shelves were now pretending to examine the products in front of them, although it was obvious that they were listening to the conversation.
Farrah calmly placed the item in her hands back onto the counter.
"Are you saying that we stole something from your faction?"
The young man’s smile widened slightly.
"I didn’t say that."
"Then what exactly are you saying?"
The man’s smile slowly faded.

He had probably expected Farrah to become nervous after hearing his accusation, but her reaction was completely different from what he had anticipated. She wasn’t angry, and she wasn’t frightened either. Instead, she simply looked at him with an expression that seemed almost bored.
That made the situation slightly more difficult.
The man glanced around the shop before looking back at her.
"I’m only saying that some of the products you’re selling appear to be similar to items that recently disappeared from our storage facilities."
Farrah tilted her head.
"Similar? Then what does that have to do with us?"
The young man paused.
Farrah immediately continued before he could answer.
"If your faction lost something, shouldn’t you investigate the people who had access to your storage facilities? Why are you coming here and questioning me?"
The man’s expression became slightly stiff.
Farrah could tell that she had hit the problem directly.

If the items had truly been stolen from their vault, then they should have evidence of the theft. They should know exactly what was missing and when it disappeared. Most importantly, they should have some idea of who could have accessed their storage.
Simply walking into Kai’s Shop and claiming that their products looked similar was meaningless.
The man didn’t seem particularly bothered, however.
"You’re right. We should investigate the matter properly."
"Then you should do that."
Farrah nodded.
The man’s eyebrows twitched.
He had clearly expected the conversation to go in a different direction.
"You don’t seem concerned."
"Should I be?"
The young man stared at her for several seconds.
Farrah calmly stared back.

The customers inside the shop had become increasingly uncomfortable, but nobody wanted to leave while the conversation was still happening. After all, everyone knew that the twelve factions controlled a significant portion of Cameron City’s resources.
Even the neutral factions were not people that ordinary survivors wanted to offend.
The young man finally let out a quiet laugh.
"You’re quite calm."
"If I became nervous every time someone came in and asked me a strange question, I wouldn’t be able to do business."
That answer caused several customers nearby to quietly chuckle.
The man’s expression darkened for a moment.
However, he quickly recovered.
"Perhaps I should explain myself more clearly."
"Please do."
The man stepped closer to the counter.

"Our faction recently discovered that several items were missing from one of our storage facilities. Among those items were emergency supplies, medical equipment, and several other products that are not particularly easy to obtain."
Farrah found this interesting as she listened carefully...
"Then, shortly afterward, those same types of products began appearing in your shop. Don’t you think that’s a strange coincidence?"
"Not particularly."
The man’s expression changed, "Why?"
"Because there are hundreds of thousands of survivors in Cameron City."
Farrah gestured toward the entrance.

"People are constantly moving supplies around. They trade with one another, they explore ruins, they search abandoned buildings, and they recover items from places that have been left untouched since the apocalypse began."
She looked directly at him.
"Why would you assume that the products in my shop came from your vault?"
The man didn’t immediately answer.
Farrah’s response was perfectly reasonable.
In fact, that was exactly the problem.
The man had no proof, and he was simply trying to see how she would react.
Farrah didn’t know exactly what they were planning, but she was certain of one thing.
They were trying to investigate them... They wanted to know the source of their endless products.
’Well... I guess it’s just a matter of time.’
They had already expected that some people would want to know about their secrets.
Still, the young man smiled again.

"Your shop is selling products that are becoming increasingly difficult to obtain. You have a steady supply, your prices are reasonable, and you somehow manage to introduce new products every few days."
His gaze swept across the shelves.
"That isn’t normal."
Farrah smiled.
"Neither is the apocalypse."
The man stared at her.
Farrah continued smiling.
"Perhaps our suppliers are simply better than yours."
A few customers immediately turned their heads away to hide their laughter.
The young man’s face became slightly unpleasant.
However, he didn’t lose his temper.
That was probably the reason he had been sent here in the first place.
He understood that openly causing trouble inside Aries Faction’s territory would be foolish.
Kai’s Shop was still operating under their protection.
As long as Farrah paid the rent and didn’t cause trouble, Aries had no reason to allow another faction to intimidate or harm one of their renters.
The young man knew this.
"I’ll probably come back."
"You’re welcome anytime. As long as you don’t disturb my customers."
The man’s smile disappeared slightly before he finally walked out.
The moment he left, the customers inside the shop immediately began talking among themselves.
Farrah waited until the door closed before finally releasing a quiet breath...
Meanwhile, Temet could only frown as he left the shop...

He had not been acting on his own. He was a member of the Cancer Faction, one of the twelve major factions that controlled Cameron City. Unlike outsiders who had to reach Level 40 and complete the required breakthrough before they could officially join a faction, Temet had been born into Cancer.
His parents were already members, which meant that his position within the faction had been established from birth despite being Level 29 only.
Nonetheless, because of that, Temet had been given an important task, to investigate Kai’s Shop.
At first, the task seemed simple.
However, several weeks had already passed since he began investigating the strange shop, and he still hadn’t discovered anything useful.
No matter how many products they purchased, the supplies simply kept coming.

There were times when certain items disappeared from the shelves for several days, but they always returned eventually. The shop might have a delay in its supply, but it never completely ran out of products.
Temet had even tried buying large quantities of the merchandise.
It made no difference.
The more they bought, the more convinced he became that Kai’s Shop had some kind of extraordinary supply chain.
Unfortunately, they couldn’t find it.
They had investigated the people working in the shop, followed some of the customers, and even tried tracing the products after purchasing them. However, everything eventually led to a dead end.
There were simply too many possibilities.

The supplies could have come from another city. They could have been recovered from abandoned facilities, exchanged with survivors outside Cameron City, or obtained through some hidden trading network.
Eventually, Temet was summoned to a private meeting.
Several elders of the Cancer Faction were already waiting inside.
"Still nothing?"
Temet lowered his head slightly.
"Nothing conclusive."
One of the elders frowned.
"Not even after all this time?"
Another elder slowly tapped his fingers against the table.
"Then there is only one possibility."
Temet looked up.
"Conversion Node."
The words immediately attracted everyone’s attention.
Temet’s expression changed slightly.
The Conversion Node was a device capable of transferring certain items obtained or traded within the VR world into reality. It was extremely valuable, but it had several restrictions.
Normally, it was used for special items such as gene enhancements, blueprints, consumables, or crafted equipment.
One of the elders slowly shook his head.
"I don’t believe it."
"Why not?"
"Look at what they’re selling."
He gestured toward the reports.
"Instant noodles. Water gallons. Folding bicycles. Sleeping bags. Flashlights. Raincoats. Stainless steel tumblers. Even canned food."
His expression became increasingly skeptical.
"Those aren’t the types of items that can normally be materialized through a Conversion Node."
Another elder nodded.
"Even if it were possible, the energy required to transfer such a massive quantity of ordinary goods would be absurd. They would need an enormous supply of cores just to maintain their inventory."
Temet remained silent.
That was exactly the problem.
The Conversion Node was the only explanation that made sense, yet it also didn’t make sense at all.
If Kai’s Shop was truly using one, then they had somehow overcome restrictions that even the elders considered impossible.
And if they hadn’t...
Then where were the products coming from?
After a long silence, one of the elders finally spoke.
"Regardless of the source, we cannot continue investigating from the outside."
Temet looked toward him.
The elder’s eyes narrowed.
"Capture Kai."
Temet’s expression immediately became serious.

chapters.title: Chapter 354: Claire and the Codebreakers
paragraphs: The elders of the Cancer Faction eventually decided that there was no point in continuing their investigation from a distance.
If they couldn't discover where Kai's Shop was obtaining its endless supply of products, then they would simply have to capture Kai himself and force him to reveal the truth.
"How many people should we send?"
One of the elders asked.
"Five should be enough."
Another elder replied after a moment of consideration.
"Everyone must be at least Level 60."

Temet, who was standing nearby, immediately understood their reasoning. There was no need to mobilize a large force against someone who had yet to reach Level 40, especially when the Cancer Faction had several Level 60 survivors who could easily handle someone of Kai's supposed strength.

As for Level 70 survivors, the elders weren't willing to mobilize them for such a simple operation, while the handful of Level 80 experts within the faction were even more precious. Moving someone of that level required considerable resources, and there was simply no reason to use one of their strongest combatants to deal with a person who was believed to be below Level 40.
"Once the opportunity appears, capture him and bring him back."
One of the elders finally ordered.
However, Temet's expression became slightly strange.
"There is one problem."
The elders looked at him.
"Kai doesn't leave the shop."
"What do you mean?"
"Exactly what I said. We've been observing him for some time now, and he has never left the building."

Temet had already investigated the matter thoroughly, but the result remained the same. Kai would occasionally leave his quarters and enter the shop, where he would act as the cashier for a while before returning to his room. Aside from that, he never went anywhere.
He didn't visit another faction, or meet any merchants. As a matter of fact, he didn't leave the city.
As far as Temet could tell, Kai simply remained inside the shop every day.
The elders exchanged confused looks.
"Are you saying that he has been staying there this entire time?"
"Yes."
"Then how is he obtaining the supplies?"
"We still don't know."
The answer caused the room to fall silent.

That was precisely what made Kai's Shop so strange. No matter how long they watched, they couldn't find anyone delivering the products, yet the supplies continued to appear. Even when the Cancer Faction deliberately purchased large quantities of merchandise, the shop would eventually restock again.
There could be delays, but the supply never completely stopped.
Temet had begun to suspect that Kai might have realized he was being watched.
Perhaps that was why he refused to leave.
One of the elders slowly narrowed his eyes.
"Then perhaps he knows."
Temet's expression changed.
"You mean he knows we're watching him?"
"It's possible."
The elder leaned back in his chair.
"Regardless, it doesn't matter. If he refuses to leave, then we'll simply wait."
The elders had already made their decision.
The moment Kai finally left the protection of the Aries Faction, they would make their move.
"Keep watching him," one of them ordered. "If he gets involved in the next raid, then we'll use our chance."
Temet nodded.
The next raid would take place outside the city.
And unlike Kai's Shop, the battlefield would not be under the protection of the Aries Faction.
That was where they would finally have their opportunity.
Meanwhile, completely unaware of their plans, or perhaps knowing far more than they realized, Kai continued staying inside his room.
He had no reason to leave.
After all, he was currently having far too much fun playing Perfect World.
Codebreakers Shelter.
Claire tightened the straps of her advanced camouflage gear before stepping out of the shelter.

The equipment covered her whole body, allowing her to blend into the surrounding environment whenever necessary, while the various weapons attached to her gear made it clear that she wasn't simply going outside for a casual walk. She had already checked everything twice before leaving, but she still took one final look at the weapons secured around her waist.
After all, they were heading into an abandoned shelter.
Nobody knew what they would find there or what had happened to the people who had once lived there either.
"Are you ready?"
Claire turned around.
Ralph was standing a few meters behind her, wearing his own combat equipment while carrying a rifle...
"I've been ready for five minutes."
Ralph smiled.
"Then you should have said something."
"I did."
"You said, 'Wait a moment.'"
"That was five minutes ago."
Ralph couldn't argue with that.
Claire shook her head before looking at the third member of their group.
Amer was standing slightly behind them.
Compared to Claire and Ralph, he looked almost out of place.
He had never been considered a powerful survivor before.

In fact, until recently, Amer had been little more than an ordinary young man in his twenties who helped with various chores around the shelter. He had spent much of his time assisting in the kitchen, carrying supplies, preparing meals, and doing whatever other work was necessary.
Nobody had expected him to suddenly become a combatant.
Still, the Codebreakers Shelter had obtained a Status Crystal that could be used to check the progress of local survivors.
Amer had been one of the first people to use it.
The result had surprised everyone.
[ Name: Amer ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 15 ]
[ Physique Rating: D ]
[ Active Skills: Silent Dash Lv3 ]
[ Passive Skills: Spirit Sense Lv2, Dexterity Flow Lv2 ]
Amer had initially been shocked by his own status.
Claire had been even more surprised.
The young man who had previously spent most of his days working in the kitchen had actually awakened abilities that were extremely suitable for combat.

His Silent Dash allowed him to channel Spirit Energy into his legs and suddenly move up to five meters, ignoring terrain obstacles in the process. His Spirit Sense allowed him to detect subtle movements and potential threats, while Dexterity Flow improved his coordination and agility.
Amer wasn't particularly strong yet, but he had the potential to become much stronger.
"Don't worry so much."
Amer suddenly spoke.
Claire looked at him.
"I'm not worried."
"You've been looking at me for some time..."
"Because you're making me nervous."
Claire sighed.
"You're going to an abandoned shelter for the first time, and you're smiling like you're going on a picnic."
"I've never been outside with people this strong before."
Amer looked toward Ralph.
Then he looked at Claire.
"Besides, I want to see what it's like."
Ralph chuckled.
"Just remember that the things outside don't care how excited you are."
Amer's smile disappeared slightly.
"I'll remember that."
Claire glanced toward the massive gates of Codebreakers Shelter.

The shelter was already far more secure than it had been when they first established it, and thanks to Kai's resources, they had access to equipment that most survivors could only dream of possessing.
Food wasn't a major concern anymore and weapons weren't as difficult to obtain.
Even medical supplies and other necessities were available in reasonable quantities.
However, Kai's Infinite Gift Packs couldn't provide everything.
There were still resources they needed that simply didn't appear often enough.

Certain construction materials were difficult to acquire. Specialized machinery was almost impossible to find. Some types of electronic equipment, replacement parts, and industrial supplies were equally valuable.
That was why they were here.
According to the information they had gathered, the shelter had been abandoned for several months.
Nobody knew why.
There were rumors that the people living there had been forced to evacuate after a powerful A.I. units appeared nearby.
Others believed that the shelter had been attacked.
Whatever the truth was, the place had remained untouched for a long time.
That made it worth investigating.
"Let's go."
Claire finally stepped forward.
The three of them left the shelter together.
The moment they passed through the gates, Amer's expression became noticeably more serious.
He immediately activated Spirit Sense.
"What do you sense?"
"Nothing."
Amer frowned.
"That's the problem."
Ralph immediately raised his rifle while Claire's eyes narrowed.
Ralph's Sharpshooter Focus Talent was already active.
His perception had become far more precise than that of an ordinary survivor, allowing him to notice details that most people would completely overlook.
A moment later, something moved behind one of the broken windows.
Amer instinctively activated Silent Dash.
Claire immediately grabbed his shoulder.
"Don't."
Amer froze.
"Why?"
"Because you don't know what you're looking at."
Claire slowly pulled out one of her weapons.
Ralph adjusted his position.
A few seconds passed... then something suddenly jumped from the building.
Amer nearly activated Silent Dash again, but Claire stopped him.
The creature landed heavily on the street.
It was a mutated dog.
Ralph fired immediately.
The shot struck its head and the mutated creature collapsed before it could even react.
Amer stared at the corpse.
"That's it?"
Claire glanced at him.
"Did you expect something stronger?"
"No."
Amer looked disappointed.
"I thought it would be more exciting."
Claire immediately regretted bringing him.

"We still don't know."
The answer caused the room to fall silent.
That was precisely what made Kai's Shop so strange.
No matter how long they watched, they couldn't find anyone delivering the products, yet the supplies continued to appear.
Even when the Cancer Faction deliberately purchased large quantities of merchandise, the shop would eventually restock again.
There could be delays, but the supply never completely stopped.
Temet had begun to suspect that Kai might have realized he was being watched.
Perhaps that was why he refused to leave.
One of the elders slowly narrowed his eyes.
"Then perhaps he knows."
Temet's expression changed.
"You mean he knows we're watching him?"
"It's possible."
The elder leaned back in his chair.
"Regardless, it doesn't matter.
If he refuses to leave, then we'll simply wait."
The elders had already made their decision.
The moment Kai finally left the protection of the Aries Faction, they would make their move.
"Keep watching him," one of them ordered.
"If he gets involved in the next raid, then we'll use our chance."
Temet nodded.
The next raid would take place outside the city.
And unlike Kai's Shop, the battlefield would not be under the protection of the Aries Faction.
That was where they would finally have their opportunity.
Meanwhile, completely unaware of their plans, or perhaps knowing far more than they realized, Kai continued staying inside his room.
He had no reason to leave.
After all, he was currently having far too much fun playing Perfect World.
Codebreakers Shelter.
Claire tightened the straps of her advanced camouflage gear before stepping out of the shelter.

The equipment covered her whole body, allowing her to blend into the surrounding environment whenever necessary, while the various weapons attached to her gear made it clear that she wasn't simply going outside for a casual walk.
She had already checked everything twice before leaving, but she still took one final look at the weapons secured around her waist.
After all, they were heading into an abandoned shelter.
Nobody knew what they would find there or what had happened to the people who had once lived there either.
"Are you ready?"
Claire turned around.
Ralph was standing a few meters behind her, wearing his own combat equipment while carrying a rifle...
"I've been ready for five minutes."
Ralph smiled.
"Then you should have said something."
"I did."
"You said, 'Wait a moment.'"
"That was five minutes ago."
Ralph couldn't argue with that.
Claire shook her head before looking at the third member of their group.
Amer was standing slightly behind them.
Compared to Claire and Ralph, he looked almost out of place.
He had never been considered a powerful survivor before.
In fact, until recently, Amer had been little more than an ordinary young man in his twenties who helped with various chores around the shelter.
He had spent much of his time assisting in the kitchen, carrying supplies, preparing meals, and doing whatever other work was necessary.
Nobody had expected him to suddenly become a combatant.
Still, the Codebreakers Shelter had obtained a Status Crystal that could be used to check the progress of local survivors.
Amer had been one of the first people to use it.
The result had surprised everyone.
[ Name: Amer ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 15 ]
[ Physique Rating: D ]
[ Active Skills: Silent Dash Lv3 ]
[ Passive Skills: Spirit Sense Lv2, Dexterity Flow Lv2 ]
Amer had initially been shocked by his own status.
Claire had been even more surprised.
The young man who had previously spent most of his days working in the kitchen had actually awakened abilities that were extremely suitable for combat.
His Silent Dash allowed him to channel Spirit Energy into his legs and suddenly move up to five meters, ignoring terrain obstacles in the process.
His Spirit Sense allowed him to detect subtle movements and potential threats, while Dexterity Flow improved his coordination and agility.
Amer wasn't particularly strong yet, but he had the potential to become much stronger.
"Don't worry so much."
Amer suddenly spoke.
Claire looked at him.
"I'm not worried."
"You've been looking at me for some time..."
"Because you're making me nervous."
Claire sighed.
"You're going to an abandoned shelter for the first time, and you're smiling like you're going on a picnic."
"I've never been outside with people this strong before."
Amer looked toward Ralph.
Then he looked at Claire.
"Besides, I want to see what it's like."
Ralph chuckled.
"Just remember that the things outside don't care how excited you are."
Amer's smile disappeared slightly.
"I'll remember that."
Claire glanced toward the massive gates of Codebreakers Shelter.

The shelter was already far more secure than it had been when they first established it, and thanks to Kai's resources, they had access to equipment that most survivors could only dream of possessing.
Food wasn't a major concern anymore and weapons weren't as difficult to obtain.
Even medical supplies and other necessities were available in reasonable quantities.
However, Kai's Infinite Gift Packs couldn't provide everything.
There were still resources they needed that simply didn't appear often enough.
Certain construction materials were difficult to acquire.
Specialized machinery was almost impossible to find.
Some types of electronic equipment, replacement parts, and industrial supplies were equally valuable.
That was why they were here.
According to the information they had gathered, the shelter had been abandoned for several months.
Nobody knew why.
There were rumors that the people living there had been forced to evacuate after a powerful A.I. units appeared nearby.
Others believed that the shelter had been attacked.
Whatever the truth was, the place had remained untouched for a long time.
That made it worth investigating.
"Let's go."
Claire finally stepped forward.
The three of them left the shelter together.
The moment they passed through the gates, Amer's expression became noticeably more serious.
He immediately activated Spirit Sense.
"What do you sense?"
"Nothing."
Amer frowned.
"That's the problem."
Ralph immediately raised his rifle while Claire's eyes narrowed.
Ralph's Sharpshooter Focus Talent was already active.
His perception had become far more precise than that of an ordinary survivor, allowing him to notice details that most people would completely overlook.
A moment later, something moved behind one of the broken windows.
Amer instinctively activated Silent Dash.
Claire immediately grabbed his shoulder.
"Don't."
Amer froze.
"Why?"
"Because you don't know what you're looking at."
Claire slowly pulled out one of her weapons.
Ralph adjusted his position.
A few seconds passed... then something suddenly jumped from the building.
Amer nearly activated Silent Dash again, but Claire stopped him.
The creature landed heavily on the street.
It was a mutated dog.
Ralph fired immediately.
The shot struck its head and the mutated creature collapsed before it could even react.
Amer stared at the corpse.
"That's it?"
Claire glanced at him.
"Did you expect something stronger?"
"No."
Amer looked disappointed.
"I thought it would be more exciting."
Claire immediately regretted bringing him.

chapters.title: Chapter 355: The Army
paragraphs: Claire immediately raised her hand, signaling the other two to stop.
Ralph lowered his rifle slightly, while Amer looked around in confusion.
"What is it?" Amer asked quietly.
Claire didn’t answer immediately.
Her eyes were fixed on the interior of the abandoned shelter.

The place had clearly been looted before. Broken furniture was scattered everywhere, cabinets and doors had been smashed open, and most of the easily accessible supplies had already disappeared. At first glance, it looked like there was nothing left worth taking.
However, Claire wasn’t looking at any of those things.
Instead, she was looking at something only she could see... It was the Spirit tied to her talent, Fifth Sin...
Its form constantly shifted like flowing smoke, yet its outline somehow resembled a man draped in an elegant robe...
The spirit slowly drifted toward the back of the room before stopping beside a cracked concrete wall.
"There."
The voice echoed directly inside Claire’s mind.
"So you found something again."
The invisible spirit didn’t answer immediately.
Instead, one translucent hand reached toward the wall.
"Wealth does not disappear. It merely waits for someone worthy to claim it."
Claire had heard those words countless times already.
Ever since awakening the Fifth Sin Talent, the mysterious spirit had always been beside her.
Neither Kai nor Mei could see it...
As far as everyone else was concerned, Claire occasionally spoke to herself for no apparent reason.
Only Claire knew that the spirit truly existed.
She walked toward the damaged wall before knocking on it lightly with her knuckles.
"...Hollow."
Ralph immediately understood.
"You think there’s something behind it?"
"I know there is."
Without wasting another second, Ralph retrieved a heavy pry bar from his backpack while Amer hurried over to help.
It took several minutes of careful work before a section of the cracked concrete finally gave way.
Behind it was a small maintenance room.
Apparently, whoever had abandoned the shelter had deliberately concealed the entrance before leaving.
Amer’s eyes widened.
"There really was a hidden room..."
Unlike the looted offices outside, this room remained almost untouched.
Metal shelves lined the walls from top to bottom.
Several sealed crates were stacked neatly in one corner, while dozens of waterproof containers remained unopened despite the passage of time.
Ralph immediately walked toward the nearest crate before carefully opening it.
His eyebrows rose as he saw the contents.
"...Generator parts."
With that said, he continued, the second crate contained industrial batteries.
The third was filled with electrical wiring, precision tools, replacement circuits, and various electronic components.
Amer stared blankly at everything in front of him.
"These... these are worth a fortune."
Claire slowly nodded.
Many people would overlook supplies like these because they weren’t immediately useful for combat.
However, rebuilding civilization required far more than food and weapons.
Shelters needed electricity... Other water purification systems needed replacement parts.
Defensive walls required machinery to maintain.
Every single crate inside this room represented resources that would become increasingly valuable as time passed.
Meanwhile, the spirit floated silently between the shelves.
Its movements became noticeably more graceful than before.
"Claim them."
Claire couldn’t help but smile.
"I know... But we can’t take them all, okay?"
The spirit’s soft laughter echoed inside her mind but it didn’t speak anymore.
So, Claire knew that it was already fine.
The moment she placed her hand on the nearest crate, a faint golden light spread across its surface.
The entire container disappeared without warning.
Amer blinked several times.
"...Where did it go?"
Another crate vanished... then another.
One after another, half of the valuable resource inside the hidden room disappeared into thin air.
Amer looked completely dumbfounded.
"I... I know you have a storage ability, but seeing it happen is still unbelievable."
Claire merely smiled without offering an explanation.
"Alright... I’ll be taking them all for now but I’ll take the half with me. In any case, I didn’t take any of the cores we’ve looted so far."
’And... It’s not really a storage ability.’
Claire added in her mind as she knew what was truly happening.
None of those supplies were actually inside her own storage.
They had all been entrusted to the spirit.
It was somewhere within an enormous dimensional vault that only the mysterious entity could access, countless treasures had already begun piling up.
Every resource she claimed expanded that hidden domain.
And as its wealth increased... so did the spirit’s power.
Claire felt a familiar warmth spread throughout her body.
Spirit Energy circulated through her meridians more smoothly than before, while her physical strength increased ever so slightly.
It wasn’t a dramatic transformation.
The improvement was subtle.
But she had experienced it enough times to recognize it immediately.
Well, the richer the spirit became... the stronger she became as well.
Claire looked at the invisible figure with curiosity.
"You really are Greed..."
The spirit remained silent for several seconds.
Then another quiet laugh echoed inside her mind.
"Names are merely labels created by mortals. Call me whatever you wish. As long as you continue gathering wealth... I shall continue making you stronger."
Claire shook her head helplessly before turning toward Ralph and Amer.
"Let’s continue searching."
She glanced once more at the now-empty storage room before smiling to herself.
If even one forgotten shelter could hide resources like these...
Then perhaps the wasteland still contained far more treasures than anyone had imagined.
The three of them continued searching through the abandoned shelter, moving deeper into the ruined buildings as they checked each room for anything that might still be useful.

After discovering the hidden maintenance room, their expectations had increased considerably. If one of the most obvious areas had been hiding such valuable resources, there was always a chance that other supplies had been overlooked as well.
Amer, in particular, had become much more enthusiastic.
He carefully searched through overturned cabinets and opened drawers that hadn’t already been completely destroyed, while Ralph checked the larger rooms and storage areas.
Claire moved between them, occasionally stopping whenever the spirit of Greed drew her attention toward something that had escaped the notice of the others.
Unfortunately, most of what they found was either useless or too damaged to be worth taking.

Several old computers had been stripped of their valuable components. A few pieces of machinery had been left behind, but they were so badly damaged that repairing them would likely require more resources than simply finding replacements elsewhere.
They had already been searching for nearly half an hour when Amer suddenly stopped.
His expression changed.
"Wait."
Claire immediately turned toward him.
"What is it?"
Amer didn’t answer.
His eyes slowly moved toward the entrance of the shelter.
A moment later, Ralph also noticed the change in his expression.
"What did you sense?"
"Something."
Amer activated Spirit Sense to its full extent.
His face gradually became more serious.
"There are... things approaching."
Claire’s expression immediately hardened.
"How many?"
"I don’t know yet."
Amer closed his eyes.
The Spirit Energy within his body circulated rapidly as he concentrated, allowing his senses to spread farther than before.
Then his eyes suddenly opened.
"Not far."
Ralph immediately raised his rifle.
"Mutated beasts?"
"No. They’re machines."
Claire’s expression changed.
"Everyone, hide."
There was no hesitation in her voice.
Ralph and Amer instantly followed her instructions.

They moved deeper into the abandoned shelter, quickly searching for a place where they could conceal themselves without exposing their positions. Claire eventually found a partially collapsed section of the building where several concrete walls had fallen over one another, creating a narrow space large enough for the three of them to hide.
They immediately moved behind the rubble.
Claire activated her advanced camouflage gear.

A faint shimmer passed over her body as the equipment adjusted itself to the surrounding environment. The technology was far more sophisticated than anything ordinary survivors could obtain, and it didn’t simply distort their appearance.
It also suppressed their heat signatures.
Ralph and Amer activated their own camouflage equipment as well.
Within moments, the three of them became almost impossible to detect with ordinary sensors.
Claire carefully peeked through a narrow gap between the broken concrete.
She couldn’t see anything yet.
But she could hear them.
A faint mechanical sound gradually grew louder in the distance.
It was the sound of countless metal feet moving across the ground.
Clank. Clank. Clank.
The noise continued approaching, and Amer’s expression became tense.
He instinctively reached toward the jammer attached to his equipment.
Claire immediately grabbed his wrist.
"Don’t."
Amer froze.
"Why?"
"The jammer. If you activate it now, they’ll know something is here."
Amer immediately understood.
The jammer was useful because it could interfere with the detection systems of the A.I. army, but activating it wasn’t something they could do without consequences.
The device required a considerable amount of power to operate.
That meant activating it would create an energy signature.
Under normal circumstances, they could activate the jammer before the enemy arrived and use it to conceal their presence.
But now...
It was already too late.
The enemy was too close.
If they suddenly activated a powerful electronic device in the middle of the A.I. army’s search range, there was a good chance their sensors would immediately notice the disturbance.
However, just as they finished speaking, the massive foot of a Tyrant Mech suddenly landed directly in front of their hiding place!

chapters.title: Chapter 356: The Product
paragraphs: Crash!
The three of them remained completely motionless.
Even after the Tyrant Mech’s enormous foot landed only a few meters away, none of them dared to breathe too loudly.
Claire could even hear Amer swallowing nervously beside her.

The gigantic machine stood nearly eight meters tall, its dark alloy armor covered with countless scratches left behind by previous battles. Thick hydraulic limbs supported its massive frame while several weapon systems remained folded against its back, ready to deploy at any moment.
It wasn’t alone.
One after another, more Tyrant Mechs marched past the abandoned shelter.
Their heavy footsteps shook the cracked concrete beneath Claire’s knees, causing fine dust to fall from the damaged ceiling.
Clank... Clank... Clank...

Mixed among them were dozens of smaller combat machines. Spider-like scouts rapidly climbed across ruined buildings while humanoid assault units marched in perfect formation without making a single unnecessary movement.
Above them, surveillance drones continuously circled through the sky.
None of the machines spoke...
They simply advanced like a single enormous organism moving toward an unknown destination.
Amer’s fingers unconsciously tightened around the handle of his weapon.
Claire immediately shook her head ever so slightly.
’Bro... Don’t get us killed...’
Against an army of that size, even Level 60 survivors would think twice before engaging.
Fortunately, the camouflage equipment continued functioning perfectly.
Several drones even hovered directly above the ruined shelter before flying away without showing the slightest reaction.
Only after nearly fifteen minutes did the endless stream of machines finally begin to disappear into the distance.
The heavy footsteps gradually became quieter.
The drones also slowly vanished from the sky until only silence remained.
Still, Claire refused to move.
"Wait."
She whispered the word so softly that it was almost inaudible.
Another two minutes passed... then another.
Only after Amer confirmed that nothing remained within the range of his Spirit Sense did Claire finally allow herself to relax.
"They’re gone."
Ralph slowly lowered his rifle and released a long breath.
"I’ve never seen that many at once"
"Neither have I."
Claire looked toward the direction where the machines had disappeared.
The number wasn’t simply unusual... It was alarming.
An army of that size wasn’t dispatched for ordinary patrols.
Whether they were passing through the region or preparing for something much larger, it was information that couldn’t be ignored.
Claire immediately opened her System interface.
Without wasting another second, she entered the Guild Chat shared by the members of Codebreakers.
Her fingers quickly moved across the translucent panel...

[ Claire: Hey guys! Large A.I. army spotted approximately thirty kilometers northeast of Cameron City. At least dozens of Tyrant Mechs, hundreds of assault units, multiple scout drones. Direction uncertain, but they’re moving toward Cameron City’s general vicinity. Avoid the area until we know more. ]
The message was sent instantly.
Several seconds later, replies began appearing.
[ Farrah: Interesting. ]
Claire couldn’t help but chuckle after seeing the nonchalant response.
That was certainly the shortest response she had expected.
A moment later, another message appeared.
[ Farrah: Don’t worry. Cameron City isn’t an ordinary survivor settlement. If they’re really heading here, the twelve factions will notice them long before they arrive. ]
Claire nodded slightly, and she believed that was true.
Although the Codebreakers Shelter had grown considerably stronger over the past few weeks, Cameron City was still one of the largest surviving cities in the region.
Its defensive walls, surveillance network, and countless patrol teams would detect such an army sooner or later.
More importantly, every one of the twelve factions had their own scouts operating outside the city every single day.
It would be almost impossible for an army of this size to approach unnoticed.
Still... Claire wasn’t completely reassured.
An army capable of making her hide without daring to move wasn’t something she could simply dismiss.
Before she could continue thinking, another notification appeared.
[ Kai: Estimated direction? ]
Claire immediately replied.
[ Claire: Still uncertain. They passed our location without stopping. They may only be moving through the area, but Cameron City lies roughly along their route. ]
There was a brief pause.
Then Kai finally sent another message.
[ Kai: Understood. Are you guys completing some Guild Mission? Be careful. ]
Claire smiled slightly and replied to thank Kai as always. After all, the camouflage gear they used to avoid detection came from him.
After that, she closed the Guild Chat before looking toward Ralph and Amer.
"We’ll continue our task..."
Two days passed quietly.

During those two days, the Codebreakers Shelter became even busier than before. Construction never seemed to stop. From sunrise until late in the evening, the sounds of hammers striking steel, welding torches crackling, and heavy machinery operating echoed throughout the settlement.

More defensive walls were being reinforced, new buildings gradually rose from their foundations, and additional watchtowers appeared around the perimeter. Every day, the shelter looked a little larger than it had the day before.
At this time, however, several kilometers away, another merchant caravan was slowly making its way through the ruined roads.

Unlike Diego and Morales, whose caravans specialized in food supplies, weapons, and Gene Serums, this caravan transported something completely different. Their large transport trucks had been modified into reinforced trailers covered with steel cages instead of cargo containers. Every now and then, animal noises echoed from within them, making the entire caravan seem strangely out of place in the middle of the post-apocalyptic wasteland.
One of the younger merchants looked around with a puzzled expression before scratching his head.
"Diego said the shelter should be somewhere around here."
The older man riding beside him unfolded a weathered map and compared it with the navigation device mounted inside the vehicle.
"The coordinates are correct. Unless we’ve somehow taken the wrong road, we should already be standing right in front of it."
The younger merchant leaned out of the window and looked around once more.
There was nothing.

Broken highways stretched into the distance, ruined buildings stood abandoned on both sides of the road, and dense vegetation had reclaimed much of the surrounding area. No matter where he looked, there wasn’t the slightest sign that a large settlement existed nearby.
"Did they move?"
"I doubt it."
Just as the older merchant was beginning to question the map itself, several guards riding with the caravan immediately became alert.
"Someone’s coming."
Weapons were instinctively raised, although they weren’t aimed directly at the approaching figure.

A lone survivor calmly walked toward them from between the trees. He carried an assault rifle over one shoulder and wore equipment that immediately revealed he belonged to an organized settlement rather than an ordinary group of scavengers.
The moment he got close enough, he smiled.
"Merchants?"
The two merchants exchanged surprised glances.
"Edwin..."
"Boris..."
They introduced themselves.
"My name is Wallace. I knew it, you’re all going to our shelter, right?
Boris looked around once again before nodding.
"Where is your shelter, Wallace?"
"Just stay behind and follow me for now."

Although the instruction sounded strange, neither merchant questioned it. The trucks slowly moved forward behind Wallace until, after traveling only a short distance, the scenery in front of them suddenly distorted.
The air rippled like the surface of a lake.
Soon, they saw a massive hidden settlement.

sentences.text: Crash!
The three of them remained completely motionless.
Even after the Tyrant Mech’s enormous foot landed only a few meters away, none of them dared to breathe too loudly.
Claire could even hear Amer swallowing nervously beside her.
The gigantic machine stood nearly eight meters tall, its dark alloy armor covered with countless scratches left behind by previous battles.
Thick hydraulic limbs supported its massive frame while several weapon systems remained folded against its back, ready to deploy at any moment.
It wasn’t alone.
One after another, more Tyrant Mechs marched past the abandoned shelter.
Their heavy footsteps shook the cracked concrete beneath Claire’s knees, causing fine dust to fall from the damaged ceiling.
Clank...
Clank...
Clank...
Mixed among them were dozens of smaller combat machines.
Spider-like scouts rapidly climbed across ruined buildings while humanoid assault units marched in perfect formation without making a single unnecessary movement.
Above them, surveillance drones continuously circled through the sky.
None of the machines spoke...
They simply advanced like a single enormous organism moving toward an unknown destination.
Amer’s fingers unconsciously tightened around the handle of his weapon.
Claire immediately shook her head ever so slightly.
’Bro...
Don’t get us killed...’
Against an army of that size, even Level 60 survivors would think twice before engaging.
Fortunately, the camouflage equipment continued functioning perfectly.
Several drones even hovered directly above the ruined shelter before flying away without showing the slightest reaction.
Only after nearly fifteen minutes did the endless stream of machines finally begin to disappear into the distance.
The heavy footsteps gradually became quieter.
The drones also slowly vanished from the sky until only silence remained.
Still, Claire refused to move.
"Wait."
She whispered the word so softly that it was almost inaudible.
Another two minutes passed... then another.
Only after Amer confirmed that nothing remained within the range of his Spirit Sense did Claire finally allow herself to relax.
"They’re gone."
Ralph slowly lowered his rifle and released a long breath.
"I’ve never seen that many at once"
"Neither have I."
Claire looked toward the direction where the machines had disappeared.
The number wasn’t simply unusual...
It was alarming.
An army of that size wasn’t dispatched for ordinary patrols.
Whether they were passing through the region or preparing for something much larger, it was information that couldn’t be ignored.
Claire immediately opened her System interface.
Without wasting another second, she entered the Guild Chat shared by the members of Codebreakers.
Her fingers quickly moved across the translucent panel...
[ Claire: Hey guys!
Large A.I. army spotted approximately thirty kilometers northeast of Cameron City.
At least dozens of Tyrant Mechs, hundreds of assault units, multiple scout drones.
Direction uncertain, but they’re moving toward Cameron City’s general vicinity.
Avoid the area until we know more. ]
The message was sent instantly.
Several seconds later, replies began appearing.
[ Farrah: Interesting. ]
Claire couldn’t help but chuckle after seeing the nonchalant response.
That was certainly the shortest response she had expected.
A moment later, another message appeared.
[ Farrah: Don’t worry.
Cameron City isn’t an ordinary survivor settlement.
If they’re really heading here, the twelve factions will notice them long before they arrive. ]
Claire nodded slightly, and she believed that was true.
Although the Codebreakers Shelter had grown considerably stronger over the past few weeks, Cameron City was still one of the largest surviving cities in the region.
Its defensive walls, surveillance network, and countless patrol teams would detect such an army sooner or later.
More importantly, every one of the twelve factions had their own scouts operating outside the city every single day.
It would be almost impossible for an army of this size to approach unnoticed.
Still...
Claire wasn’t completely reassured.
An army capable of making her hide without daring to move wasn’t something she could simply dismiss.
Before she could continue thinking, another notification appeared.
[ Kai: Estimated direction? ]
Claire immediately replied.
[ Claire: Still uncertain.
They passed our location without stopping.
They may only be moving through the area, but Cameron City lies roughly along their route. ]
There was a brief pause.
Then Kai finally sent another message.
[ Kai: Understood.
Are you guys completing some Guild Mission?
Be careful. ]
Claire smiled slightly and replied to thank Kai as always.
After all, the camouflage gear they used to avoid detection came from him.
After that, she closed the Guild Chat before looking toward Ralph and Amer.
"We’ll continue our task..."

Construction never seemed to stop.
From sunrise until late in the evening, the sounds of hammers striking steel, welding torches crackling, and heavy machinery operating echoed throughout the settlement.
More defensive walls were being reinforced, new buildings gradually rose from their foundations, and additional watchtowers appeared around the perimeter.
Every day, the shelter looked a little larger than it had the day before.
