chapters.title: Chapter 357: Livestock Trading
paragraphs: "We believe that a settlement that learns how to raise livestock can continue feeding itself for years."
Wallace slowly nodded.
That was something he couldn’t disagree with.

The Codebreakers Shelter already had its own poultry grounds, and the chickens they had obtained previously had proven to be extremely valuable. Eggs were now a regular part of the shelter’s food supply, and they had even begun incubating some of them in an attempt to expand the flock.
However, what stood before him was on an entirely different scale.
With goats, sheep, rabbits, ducks, and cattle, the shelter could develop a proper livestock industry instead of relying entirely on a small poultry farm and Kai’s Food Gift Packs.
"We’re interested," Wallace finally said.
Edwin’s expression immediately brightened.
"I was hoping you would say that."
Boris pulled out a small tablet from inside his coat and began explaining the prices.
The transaction took some time.
After nearly half an hour of negotiation, the two sides finally settled on the deal.
The Codebreakers Shelter would purchase fifty laying hens, ten roosters, twenty ducks, twenty rabbits, ten goats, eight sheep, and four cattle.
The fifty hens and ten roosters would immediately expand the shelter’s existing poultry operation, while the ducks and rabbits would provide additional sources of eggs and meat.

The goats and sheep could eventually provide milk, meat, and wool, while the cattle represented the most valuable part of the transaction. Even if they were difficult to raise, four healthy cattle could eventually become the foundation of a much larger herd.
In total, the caravan was bringing 122 animals into the Codebreakers Shelter.
The two merchants were primarily interested in C-Grade Energy Cores.
Fortunately, that wasn’t a problem for Codebreakers.

Kai had provided the shelter with enough resources that paying for the livestock wouldn’t significantly affect their reserves, especially considering the long-term value of the animals. As a matter of fact, while Energy Cores could be absorbed by Foreign Survivors to grow stronger, there was also a limit to how many cores they could effectively use. Once a survivor reached a certain point, accumulating more cores was far less valuable than it had been during their early growth... After all, there was a limit to how much they could absorb per month.
After calculating the value of the animals, Edwin and Boris asked for five hundred and forty C-Grade Energy Cores for the entire shipment.
Althea, who had been called over to finalize the transaction, didn’t immediately agree.

She carefully inspected the list of animals and their condition before making her own calculations. After several minutes of discussion, she managed to negotiate the price down to five hundred and ten C-Grade Energy Cores.
Edwin and Boris exchanged a glance before finally accepting.
"Five hundred and ten," Edwin said. "For all 122 animals."
"Correct."
"Then we have a deal."
Althea nodded.
Soon, five hundred and ten C-Grade Energy Cores were transferred from the Codebreakers Shelter’s reserves to the merchants.
In return, Edwin and Boris handed over ownership of the livestock they had transported.
The transaction was finally complete.

For the merchants, it was an excellent deal. They had converted livestock that required constant food and care during their journey into a valuable supply of Energy Cores that could be used to strengthen their own people or traded with other settlements.
For Codebreakers, however, the value of the purchase went far beyond the Energy Cores they had spent.
They had just acquired the foundation of a proper livestock industry.
The only problem was that they now had to figure out how to take care of 122 new animals.
However, just as the agreement was about to be finalized, Boris suddenly glanced toward Althea.
"There is one more thing."
Althea looked at him.
"What is it?"
"We heard that your shelter possesses Gene Stimulants. Ahem... Diego mentioned it after he had visited your shelter."
Althea didn’t immediately answer.
She was the person responsible for managing the shelter’s supply of Gene Stimulants, and she understood exactly why the merchants were interested.
Gene Stimulants were extremely valuable.

Even the weaker versions could potentially help survivors strengthen their bodies and increase their chances of surviving in the wasteland. Unfortunately, most of the Gene Stimulants circulating among survivors came with dangerous side effects.
Some caused mutations... others damaged the body.
There were even cases where people died after using them.
The Gene Stimulants controlled by Codebreakers were completely different. They came from Kai’s Gift Packs.
Their quality was so high that the negative effects were almost nonexistent aside from some temporary weakness that could be easily negated with a higher vitality.
Of course, that didn’t mean Althea was willing to sell them without consideration.
"Why are you asking?"
Boris exchanged a glance with Edwin.
"We’ve been traveling between settlements for quite some time. We’ve seen plenty of Gene Stimulants but most of them aren’t worth the risk."
"That is an understatement," Boris added. "We’ve seen people lose their minds after taking them. Some developed temporary mutations, while others became too weak to even walk."
Althea remained silent.
"We heard yours are different."
"We’re willing to trade for them," Edwin said. "Energy cores, livestock, or other resources. We can discuss the price."
Althea considered the proposal.
The Codebreakers Shelter had no shortage of Gene Stimulants at the moment. Kai’s resources had given them access to a steady supply, and the shelter wasn’t using all of them immediately.
However, that didn’t mean they could sell them carelessly. After all, they wouldn’t want their own items to be in the hands of their enemy.
"How many do you want?"
Boris hesitated.
"A hundred if possible!"
But he immediately realized how eager he sounded and coughed lightly before straightening his expression.
"If the price is reasonable, of course. We have a number of settlements that are interested in reliable Gene Stimulants. If what Diego told us is true, your supply could be extremely valuable to us."
Althea glanced at Edwin.
The older merchant nodded.
"We are prepared to pay properly for them."
Althea thought for a moment before answering.
"Alright... In case you’re interested, we also have Spirit-Boosting Vials aside from Gene Stimulant Injectors."
The two were shocked as they heard this.
"How about this... One low-grade Gene Weapon for eighteen Gene Stimulants? If you have Gene Skill Crystals, we can give five Gene Stimulants and five Spirit-Boosting Vials..."

The two merchants stared at Althea as if they had suddenly forgotten how to speak. They had expected Gene Stimulants, and they had even been prepared to pay a considerable price for them. However, Spirit-Boosting Vials were something else entirely.
Edwin’s expression became noticeably more serious.
"You’re saying you can provide both Gene Stimulants and Spirit-Boosting Vials?"
"That’s what I said."

Boris swallowed quietly. His reaction was understandable. Spirit-Boosting Vials were far rarer than ordinary Gene Stimulants. While Gene Stimulants could strengthen the physical body, Spirit-Boosting Vials could directly enhance a survivor’s spiritual energy and improve their ability to control their powers.

In this apocalypse, where strength determined everything, the difference was enormous. A reliable Gene Stimulant could help an ordinary survivor become stronger, but a reliable Spirit-Boosting Vial could potentially allow an already powerful survivor to fight even stronger A.I. Soldiers.

The two merchants exchanged another glance, and this time their expressions were completely different. They were no longer looking at Althea as merchants negotiating a simple trade. Instead, they were looking at her as if they had just discovered that the Codebreakers Shelter possessed a treasure vault.
Edwin looked at Althea carefully.
"That doesn’t seem like a particularly favorable exchange for you."
Althea gave him a calm look.
"Then you don’t have to trade."
The blunt answer immediately silenced him.

He understood what Althea was doing. She wasn’t desperate to sell. That meant the Codebreakers Shelter already had enough resources to satisfy its own needs and was simply offering its excess supplies in exchange for things it considered valuable.
"Ahem... I mean... I believe we can come to an agreement."
He then called for one of the servants to bring a box from their wagon.
Inside were several transparent crystals, each containing a faint glow that seemed to move beneath its surface.
Althea’s eyes narrowed.
"Gene Skill Crystals."
"Five of them," Edwin said as he carefully placed the crystals on the table...

Althea didn’t immediately respond. She picked up the first crystal and examined it carefully before putting it down and inspecting the second. She repeated the process with the remaining three crystals, paying close attention to each one before finally returning her gaze to the merchants.
"Five Random Gene Skill Crystals... Low-Grade," she said.
"Twenty-five Gene Stimulants and another twenty-five Spirit-Boosting Vials."
"It might seem like they were spending a lot of Gene Stimulants and Spirit-Boosting Vials, but it had to be remembered that both were consumable items."

However, the Gene Skills that they could obtain from the crystals were all permanent. They were something that was already attached to their bodies unless they used them as a Fusion Material for a stronger Gene Skill.
Still, Edwin seemed to be probing more about what they could supply.
"Ahem... If you want, you can just give us half of it. In exchange, can we have one Atmospheric Water Generator instead?"

chapters.title: Chapter 358: Althea’s Trade and the Attack
paragraphs: Althea paused when she heard Edwin’s proposal.
"An Atmospheric Water Generator?"
Edwin immediately nodded.
"Yes. Just one unit."
Althea’s expression remained calm, but her mind was already considering the offer.
An Atmospheric Water Generator was certainly valuable. In fact, it was one of the most sought-after pieces of equipment in the entire wasteland.

The ability to produce clean water directly from the moisture in the air was practically a miracle in the apocalypse. Many shelters still relied on wells, rivers, underground reservoirs, or whatever water sources they could find. Those sources were not always safe, and even when they were, there was always the possibility that they would eventually run dry.
An Atmospheric Water Generator solved much of that problem.
It could provide a settlement with a reliable source of water without requiring them to constantly search for rivers or risk sending people into dangerous territory.
Because of that, almost every major shelter wanted one.
Even Cornelio Aries of the Aries Faction in Cameron City had shown considerable interest in obtaining Atmospheric Water Generators.
That was precisely why Kai had deliberately opened a large number of Superior-Grade Water Gift Packs.

After all, when something was so valuable that even the major factions of Cameron City were willing to pay a considerable price for it, there was no reason for Codebreakers to keep its supply limited.
Althea remembered the contents of the Superior-Grade Water Gift Pack.
[ Contents: Atmospheric Water Generator, Portable Desalination Unit, Fire Extinguisher, Gene Stimulant Injector, Spirit-Boosting Vial, and Stainless Steel Tumbler. ]
The contents of the Gift Pack were the reason Codebreakers had accumulated so many Atmospheric Water Generators in the first place.
Every time Kai opened one of those packs, the shelter received these items all at once.
As a result, their inventory of those three items had grown together.
Of course, the Portable Desalination Units were another matter.

They were useful in theory, but Codebreakers wasn’t located near the sea or any other large body of water. Transporting contaminated or seawater to the shelter simply to use the machines was not particularly practical.
Some had been kept in storage in case they became useful later.
Others had been dismantled and turned into spare parts or scrap metal... many of them had even disappeared from Claire’s hands.
As for the fire extinguishers and stainless steel tumblers... they were hardly worth mentioning.
The Atmospheric Water Generators, however, were completely different.
Those were treasures.
Althea slowly looked at Edwin.
"I don’t think you’re aware of how valuable it is."
"Ahem... Then what would you consider a fair exchange?"
"One Skill Fusion Crystal for one Atmospheric Water Generator. It’s our trade with another merchant. He had offered it, and we accepted that. Can you match it?"
The two merchants exchanged glances.
Edwin’s expression changed immediately.
"Skill Fusion Crystal? We don’t have those..."
Edwin’s expression immediately became awkward.
Boris also shook his head.
"We’ve heard of them, of course. But they’re not something merchants like us can simply carry around."
Althea wasn’t surprised. She had expected that possibility.

After all, Skill Fusion Crystals were extremely valuable, and even if Edwin and Boris had access to them through their connections, there was no guarantee they would be willing to use one to purchase an Atmospheric Water Generator.
However, Edwin didn’t immediately give up.
He seemed to think for a moment before looking toward Althea again.
"What about something else?"
"What do you have?"
"We have Gene Stabilizers."
Althea’s expression changed slightly.
"Gene Stabilizers?"
"Yes."
Boris nodded.
"They aren’t exactly common, but we’ve managed to obtain a small supply through our travels."
Althea didn’t immediately respond, so the two quickly explained what it was.
They couldn’t directly make someone stronger, but they could help stabilize the changes caused by Gene Enhancements and Stimulants and prevent the user’s body from becoming too unstable.
In some cases, they could even help a survivor whose body had already suffered from a failed Gene Enhancement recover from the worst of its effects.
"If mutations are still at the beginning stages, these Stabilizers can help."
That made them extremely valuable to anyone who regularly used Gene Stimulants.
However, Althea wasn’t immediately convinced.
"How many?"
Edwin’s expression relaxed slightly after realizing that she was at least interested.
"Six Gene Stabilizers for one Atmospheric Water Generator?"
"Yes... I think this is fair..."
"Six is too few."
Edwin’s smile disappeared.
"How many would you consider reasonable?"
"Twelve..."
"Twelve?"
Boris immediately frowned.
"That’s far too many."
"Then we don’t have a deal."
Althea’s response was calm.
She wasn’t trying to pressure them.
She simply didn’t need the trade badly enough to accept something she considered an unfavorable exchange.
Edwin fell silent, and after several seconds, he finally spoke.
"How about ten?"
Althea considered the offer for a moment before nodding.
"Fine."
Boris gave Edwin a helpless look. A single Gene Stabilizer could be used to trade for food that would last for a month after all.
Edwin noticed his gaze and shrugged.
"Do you have a better offer?"

Boris opened his mouth but quickly closed it again... He didn’t have a better solution after all... In any case, as long as they take care of the Atmospheric Water Generator and ensure that it won’t need so many repairs, they should be just fine.
Althea stood up.
"Then we’ll trade."
However, just as Edwin began to relax, Althea continued.
"One more thing."
The two merchants immediately became cautious.
"What?"
"These Gene Stabilizers you’re offering..."
Althea looked directly at Boris.
"I want to see them first."
Boris nodded.
"Of course."
He immediately called one of the merchants accompanying the caravan.
A few moments later, the man returned carrying a small metal case.
Boris opened it carefully.
Inside were several small vials filled with a dark blue liquid.
Althea leaned forward slightly.
She picked up one of the vials and examined it...
She didn’t have appraisal skill, so she couldn’t immediately see its exact properties. However, she could tell that it was valuable...
She then called for Victor to have it checked, and after confirming that it was real, she was finally satisfied.
"How many do you have in total?"
Edwin’s expression changed.
"You want to buy more? Ahem... After this first sale, we have thirty-three Gene Stabilizers left."
Althea wanted to obtain these items as well, but suddenly an alarm blared out! Soon, a scout shouted...
"Diggers! They’re coming from underground!"

chapters.title: Chapter 359: The Attack
paragraphs: A few hours earlier, the Codebreakers Shelter had already experienced something that should have been impossible.
For several days, Claire’s Illusion Device had successfully concealed the entire settlement from the outside world.
From a distance, the shelter didn’t look like a shelter at all.

The illusion distorted the appearance of the surrounding area, making the enormous settlement disappear beneath the image of an ordinary hill covered in vegetation. Anyone passing through the region would see nothing more than a natural formation surrounded by trees and overgrown ruins.

It was one of the reasons Codebreakers had been able to expand so rapidly without immediately attracting the attention of nearby settlements. Even the merchants with strange protection against A.I. Army’s detection failed to notice it...
However, the illusion wasn’t perfect.
At least, not against everything.
A strange machine had wandered into the area.
It wasn’t part of the ordinary patrols of the A.I. Army, nor did it resemble any of the machines that the Codebreakers had encountered before.
The machine had simply appeared from the wilderness and moved through the surrounding area without any obvious objective.
At first, none of the Sentinels or guards stationed around the shelter considered it particularly dangerous.
After all, the machine didn’t immediately attack and it simply walked silently...
Then, as it passed near the concealed settlement, something unexpected happened.
The machine suddenly stopped.
Its head slowly turned toward the enormous hill...
Clank... Clank...
For a moment, nothing happened.
Then the air around the hill began to distort.
The machine’s sensors had somehow detected something!
It released a strange echo, and for a moment, the illusion wavered!
It happened just for an instant, but that single moment was enough.
The image of an ordinary hill briefly disappeared, revealing something beneath it.
It saw a massive wall!
The machine stood completely still.
Then it turned around and it didn’t attack.
It didn’t even approach the hidden settlement.
Instead, the strange machine simply continued walking away, disappearing into the wilderness as if it had never been there.
Unfortunately for the A.I. Unit, however, it had already been seen.
Ralph happened to be stationed at one of the outer watchtowers when he noticed the almost invisible machine!
His Eagle Eye immediately activated.
The skill allowed him to perceive details that ordinary survivors would have overlooked, and the moment his gaze settled on the retreating machine, his expression changed.
[ Target Identified. ]
[ Nightmare Unit. ]
[ Classification: A-Grade ]
Ralph’s eyes widened.
"A-Grade? Shit..."
He immediately contacted the shelter’s command center.
The information spread quickly.
By the time the machine had completely disappeared from sight, Wallace and the others had already been informed.
No one knew what the Nightmare Unit was capable of and that was the problem.
The Codebreakers had never encountered such a machine before.
The only thing they knew was that it was powerful enough to be classified as an A-Grade unit.
It had detected the illusion and that alone was deeply concerning.
The shelter immediately increased its alert level.
The Sentinels stationed around the perimeter were ordered to remain vigilant, while the surveillance network began monitoring the surrounding wilderness more carefully.
Everyone expected that the Nightmare Unit might return, but no one expected what happened next.
Several minutes later, the first alarm suddenly sounded.
"Diggers! They’re coming from underground!"
Indeed! It didn’t come from the watchtowers... Instead, it came from underground.
The entire shelter immediately reacted.
The underground detection system had identified movement beneath the settlement. Without a doubt, something was digging.
"Underground breach detected!"
The warning echoed throughout the shelter as the ground beneath the settlement began to tremble.
However, the Codebreakers Shelter had been built with more than just walls and watchtowers.
The moment the underground sensors detected the approaching movement, the shelter’s defensive systems activated.
Explosive charges buried beneath the outer perimeter detonated in rapid succession.
BOOM!
The ground violently shook.
The underground tunnel created by the approaching machines collapsed under the force of the explosions, burying the passage beneath tons of earth and shattered rock.
The Diggers had no choice but to change their approach!
Well, they couldn’t continue digging forward.
At the same time, they couldn’t simply emerge beneath the settlement since the Advanced Barrier was still active.
Soon, the first Digger finally emerged from the ground a few meters away from the shelter as the barrier prevented the Diggers from breaking through directly into the shelter’s interior...
CRASH!
Soil and debris were thrown into the air as the machine forced its way toward the surface.
Then another appeared... and another.
Soon, dozens of Diggers emerged from the ground... This time, the illusion was already useless, so it had been disabled.
It was at this point that the shelter’s Sentinel opened fire!
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Clang! Clang! Clang!
Still, the Diggers were not ordinary A.I. units.
Their massive drill-like heads had been specifically designed to penetrate defenses and endure heavy artillery!
Their powerful bodies alone were capable of damaging even structures that would have been impossible for ordinary machines to destroy.
Just like that, the Diggers ignored the incoming bullets!
Their armored bodies continued moving forward as they turned to their objective!
Apparently, the Diggers turned their massive drills toward the Advanced Barrier.
Then they attacked!
BOOM!
The impact shook the entire defensive field as the barrier rippled violently.
Then, the next Digger struck.
BOOM!
Another impact followed as the Advanced Barrier trembled.
Soon, the people inside the shelter realized something was wrong.
The Diggers were actually damaging it!
"Those things can break the barrier?!"
Someone shouted.
The answer became obvious when the third impact struck as cracks of energy began spreading across the surface of the barrier.
The Advanced Barrier was holding... but it wouldn’t hold forever.
The Diggers had succeeded in doing something that few enemies had ever managed to accomplish.
They had found a way to threaten the Codebreakers Shelter’s strongest defensive system.
And then, suddenly, the Diggers stopped...
It was quite weird, but soon, everyone realized what was happenin... a Sentinel made of black steel came out of the gates of the shelter.
Atom had come out!

chapters.title: Chapter 360: Atom
paragraphs: The Diggers suddenly stopped attacking.
For several seconds, the battlefield became strangely quiet.

The Sentinels stationed along the walls continued aiming their weapons at the machines, while the survivors inside the shelter watched in confusion as the massive mechanical creatures stood motionless before the Advanced Barrier.
Their drill-shaped heads were still spinning, throwing up clouds of dust and debris, but none of them attempted another attack.
Then the main gates of the Codebreakers Shelter slowly opened.
A figure emerged from within...
Atom had arrived.
The S-Grade Sentinel walked forward without any hesitation, leaving the shelter’s gates behind him as the Advanced Barrier continued to protect the place...
Atom did not carry a firearm, nor did it possess any visible weapon in its hands. Its body alone was the weapon.

Although Kai was not currently inside the Codebreakers Shelter, Atom remained under his command. However, Kai had already established a hierarchy of authority that allowed several trusted individuals to issue orders in his absence, and Althea was one of them.
"Eliminate the Diggers," she said. "Do not allow them to damage the barrier any further."
Atom then turned its attention back toward the battlefield.
At the same time, the Diggers finally began moving again. This time, however, the machines had stopped attacking the barrier...
They had already identified Atom as a hostile target, and they immediately redirected themselves toward him.
The first one swiftly charged.
Its drill-shaped head began spinning at an incredible speed as its mechanical legs pushed its heavy body forward.
Whoosh~
The ground shook as the machine accelerated rapidly despite its massive size.
However, Atom did not move.
The Digger continued charging until it was only a few meters away!
Then Atom raised one hand.
The Digger’s drill slammed into his palm.
CLANG!
The sound was so loud that everyone nearby instinctively flinched.
For a moment, the machine appeared to have succeeded.
Its enormous drill continued spinning violently against Atom’s hand!
Everyone was shocked as they saw sparks flying in every direction as the weapon attempted to tear through the black metal of its body.
Atom, however, remained completely motionless.
The Digger’s entire body was pushed forward by the force of its own attack, yet Atom didn’t take even a single step backward.
The difference between them became obvious almost immediately.
The Digger was a B-Grade unit... while Atom was an S-Grade Sentinel.
There was simply too much of a gap between them.
Atom’s fingers slowly closed around the rotating drill.
The mechanical weapon suddenly stopped.
The Digger’s entire body continued pushing forward, its internal engines roaring as they attempted to generate enough power to free the drill from Atom’s grip.
It was useless!
Atom tightened his hand and then...
CRACK!
A metallic fracture appeared across the Digger’s drill.
The machine immediately attempted to retreat, but Atom had already taken hold of its massive body.
Then, he lifted the B-Grade machine from the ground!
The Digger weighed several tons, but Atom didn’t seem to care.
He swung the machine sideways and slammed it into the ground.
BOOM!
The impact shook the surrounding area.
The Digger’s armored body bounced once before crashing into the dirt, leaving a deep crater beneath it. Its mechanical limbs twitched violently as its internal systems attempted to recover.
The people watching from the shelter were stunned.
The B-Grade Diggers had been powerful enough to damage the Advanced Barrier.
Yet in front of Atom, one of them had been defeated in a matter of seconds.
"That’s Atom..."
Wallace stared at the battlefield.
He had seen Atom in action before, but seeing the S-Grade Sentinel fight without a weapon was an entirely different experience.
The other Diggers seemed to reach the same conclusion.
They immediately changed their strategy.
Instead of attacking individually, the remaining machines spread out.
Several of them rushed toward Atom from different directions, while the others continued attacking the Advanced Barrier.
Apparently, their objective had not changed.
They wanted to destroy the shelter.
Atom’s head turned slightly... It had already calculated the situation.
Five Diggers were moving toward him.
The remaining machines were continuing their assault on the barrier.
[ Target priority updated. ]
Atom suddenly disappeared.
Several Sentinels watching from the walls widened their eyes.
They had not even seen him move.
A moment later, one of the Diggers attacking the barrier suddenly stopped.
Atom had appeared directly behind it.
The S-Grade Sentinel reached forward and grabbed the machine by the back of its armored body before violently pulling it away from the barrier.
Bam!
The Digger immediately responded.
Its drill spun rapidly as it attempted to turn around and attack Atom.
However, Atom simply moved its head to the side.
The drill passed harmlessly beside him and just like that, Atom’s fist struck the Digger’s body.
BOOM!
The sound was closer to an explosion than a punch.
The Digger was sent flying across the battlefield with its armored body rolling several times before crashing into another machine.
Crash!
The two B-Grade units collided violently.
Nonetheless, Atom was already moving again... Another Digger attempted to intercept him.
But this time, Atom didn’t dodge as it saw the drill coming...
Thud!
The drill struck his black armor.
But to everyone’s surprise, the Digger’s weapon stopped.
Atom didn’t even get a scratch as it grabbed the Digger’s drill with both hands.
The Digger’s mechanical body immediately began struggling.
But soon, the machine’s entire front section was ripped apart!
Soon, all the remaining Diggers moved as they surrounded
Even though they knew Atom was an S-Grade Sentinel, the Diggers were still B-Grade machines, and there were dozens of them surrounding the shelter.
If they attacked together, even a powerful enemy could potentially be overwhelmed.
Atom, however, did not appear concerned...
The S-Grade Sentinel showed the difference in their strength!
Atom alone destroyed any Diggers that were surfacing on the ground.
However, as the battle continued, the Diggers started behaving strangely.
They were no longer trying to destroy the barrier.
They had stopped attacking the shelter entirely.
Instead, they were spreading out around Atom.
"What are they doing?" Wallace asked.
Althea didn’t answer immediately as she watched the machines carefully.
Something was wrong.
Then, Althea’s expression changed.
"Everyone, retreat!"

The impact shook the surrounding area.
The Digger’s armored body bounced once before crashing into the dirt, leaving a deep crater beneath it.
Its mechanical limbs twitched violently as its internal systems attempted to recover.
The people watching from the shelter were stunned.
The B-Grade Diggers had been powerful enough to damage the Advanced Barrier.
Yet in front of Atom, one of them had been defeated in a matter of seconds.
"That’s Atom..."
Wallace stared at the battlefield.
He had seen Atom in action before, but seeing the S-Grade Sentinel fight without a weapon was an entirely different experience.
The other Diggers seemed to reach the same conclusion.
They immediately changed their strategy.
Instead of attacking individually, the remaining machines spread out.
Several of them rushed toward Atom from different directions, while the others continued attacking the Advanced Barrier.
Apparently, their objective had not changed.
They wanted to destroy the shelter.
Atom’s head turned slightly...
It had already calculated the situation.
Five Diggers were moving toward him.
The remaining machines were continuing their assault on the barrier.
[ Target priority updated. ]
Atom suddenly disappeared.
Several Sentinels watching from the walls widened their eyes.
They had not even seen him move.
A moment later, one of the Diggers attacking the barrier suddenly stopped.
Atom had appeared directly behind it.
The S-Grade Sentinel reached forward and grabbed the machine by the back of its armored body before violently pulling it away from the barrier.
Bam!
The Digger immediately responded.
Its drill spun rapidly as it attempted to turn around and attack Atom.
However, Atom simply moved its head to the side.
The drill passed harmlessly beside him and just like that, Atom’s fist struck the Digger’s body.
BOOM!
The sound was closer to an explosion than a punch.
The Digger was sent flying across the battlefield with its armored body rolling several times before crashing into another machine.
Crash!
The two B-Grade units collided violently.
Nonetheless, Atom was already moving again...
Another Digger attempted to intercept him.
But this time, Atom didn’t dodge as it saw the drill coming...
Thud!
The drill struck his black armor.
But to everyone’s surprise, the Digger’s weapon stopped.
Atom didn’t even get a scratch as it grabbed the Digger’s drill with both hands.
The Digger’s mechanical body immediately began struggling.
But soon, the machine’s entire front section was ripped apart!
Soon, all the remaining Diggers moved as they surrounded
Even though they knew Atom was an S-Grade Sentinel, the Diggers were still B-Grade machines, and there were dozens of them surrounding the shelter.
If they attacked together, even a powerful enemy could potentially be overwhelmed.
Atom, however, did not appear concerned...
The S-Grade Sentinel showed the difference in their strength!
Atom alone destroyed any Diggers that were surfacing on the ground.
However, as the battle continued, the Diggers started behaving strangely.
They were no longer trying to destroy the barrier.
They had stopped attacking the shelter entirely.
Instead, they were spreading out around Atom.
"What are they doing?" Wallace asked.
Althea didn’t answer immediately as she watched the machines carefully.
Something was wrong.
Then, Althea’s expression changed.
"Everyone, retreat!"

chapters.title: Chapter 361: Atom’s Might
paragraphs: "Everyone, retreat!"

Althea’s voice was calm, yet urgent enough that everyone nearby reacted almost instinctively. The Sentinels positioned outside immediately disengaged, while Atom abandoned its pursuit and leaped backward with astonishing speed. Even the soldiers stationed on the walls stepped away from the edge as they hurried to follow the order.
Wallace frowned.
"What is it?"
"The formation."
Althea’s eyes never left the battlefield.
"They’re surrounding Atom."
Only then did Wallace notice it as well.

The Diggers were no longer attacking randomly. Each machine had stopped at a specific distance from Atom, forming a rough circle around the S-Grade Sentinel. There was no hesitation in their movements, nor any attempt to break through the barrier again. It was as though every one of them had received the exact same command at the exact same moment.
That wasn’t normal.
These machines had acted aggressively from the moment they surfaced, but now they had suddenly become disciplined.
A bad feeling settled in Althea’s chest.
"Atom!" she shouted. "Move away from them!"
The black Sentinel reacted immediately.
Its legs pushed against the ground, and the several-ton machine shot backward like a cannonball, crossing dozens of meters in the blink of an eye.
It was just in time.
The first Digger suddenly opened the armored plates around its drill-shaped head.
Instead of releasing the familiar Bomber Swarmers that Codebreakers had encountered before, a thick stream of dark green gas burst out under tremendous pressure.
PSSSSHHH—
The poisonous cloud spread across the battlefield with frightening speed.
Then the second Digger activated.
Another torrent of green gas erupted into the air.
The third.
The fourth.

Within only a few seconds, every Digger surrounding the area released the same substance. Thick clouds rolled across the ground before rapidly rising higher, merging together into a massive poisonous fog that swallowed the battlefield.
"What the hell is that?"
Wallace instinctively covered his nose despite standing safely behind the barrier.
No one answered.
They simply watched as the green cloud continued expanding until it completely concealed every D-Grade machines, every crater, and every trace of the battlefield beneath a sea of poisonous mist.
The visibility outside the shelter dropped to almost nothing.
Even the Sentinels’ optical sensors began reporting interference as the dense gas distorted thermal signatures and reduced their effective detection range.
"It’s blocking vision..." Victor muttered.
"No..." Althea replied quietly.
"It isn’t just smoke."
She watched as the poisonous cloud drifted toward the Advanced Barrier.
The moment it touched the shimmering wall of energy, faint ripples spread across the barrier’s surface.
One ripple.
Then another.
Then dozens.
Wallace’s expression stiffened.
"The poison is affecting the barrier?"
Before anyone could answer, the barrier’s energy level suddenly dropped by a fraction of a percent.
It wasn’t much, but it was still happening...
Everyone monitoring the defensive systems noticed it immediately.
The poison wasn’t merely toxic... it was corrosive.
It was eating away at the Advanced Barrier itself.
Silence fell across the command center.
Only now did they understand the true purpose of the Diggers.
Destroying the barrier with their drills had never been the real objective.
The drills had merely been meant to keep everyone’s attention focused on a direct assault.
Their actual weapon was the poisonous gas now slowly blanketing the battlefield.

The poisonous or corrosive fog continued spreading across the battlefield, growing denser with every passing second until the entire area outside the shelter had been swallowed by the dark green cloud.
Nothing could be seen anymore.
The Diggers had completely disappeared inside the poisonous mist.
Only the constant hissing of escaping gas and the rumbling of heavy machinery could be heard from within, making it impossible to tell where the enemy was hiding.
Even the Sentinels stationed along the walls began reporting errors.
Their optical sensors were struggling to penetrate the dense cloud, while thermal imaging became increasingly unreliable as the poisonous substance interfered with their readings.
The battlefield had effectively become blind.
"Can Atom still fight in there?" Wallace asked, unable to hide the concern in his voice.
Before anyone could answer, Althea calmly looked toward one of the operators monitoring Atom’s status.
It was Victor himself, with his special eyes that could quickly examine mechanical objects using his skill.
"Atom’s systems are functioning normally."
"What about the poison?"
"No corrosion detected."
Several people inside the shelter were impressed.
No corrosion?
The poisonous gas was slowly consuming the Advanced Barrier, yet it couldn’t even damage Atom’s outer armor?
Victor couldn’t help but smile.
"Of course..."
"That armor wasn’t built with ordinary alloys. That’s Aetherium for you..."
Everyone inside the shelter remained focused on the battlefield.
Then...
A violent shockwave suddenly erupted from inside the poisonous cloud.
BOOOOM!
The thick mist was momentarily blown away as a massive mechanical body burst out of it like a cannonball.
One of the Diggers was thrown uncontrollably through the air before crashing into the ground nearly fifty meters away.
The machine bounced several times before finally sliding to a stop.
Its drill-shaped head had been completely crushed!
The armor protecting its front half had caved inward, exposing shattered gears, broken hydraulic lines, and sparks dancing wildly from torn circuits.
It didn’t move again.
Silence filled the watchtowers.
No one had actually seen what happened.
All they knew was that a B-Grade Digger had entered the poisonous cloud...
...and had been thrown back out as nothing more than scrap metal.
Another explosion echoed from inside the mist.
BOOM!
This time, a second Digger flew into the air.
Then a third.
The massive machines, each weighing several tons, were being launched from the poisonous cloud one after another as though some gigantic monster was throwing toys aside.
Crash!
Boom!
Crunch!
Every impact shook the surrounding ground.
Some Diggers lost their drills entirely.
Others had their armored bodies twisted beyond recognition.
One unfortunate machine struck another midair, causing both to explode into a rain of burning metal before they even reached the ground.
The soldiers standing atop the walls could only stare blankly.
"...is Atom throwing them?"

chapters.title: Chapter 362: Soul Enhancement
paragraphs: "Atom is just throwing them around..."
Everyone realized just how strong this Sentinel was...
Another Digger came flying out of the poisonous fog with its massive body tumbling through the air before crashing into the ground...
Boom!
It slid several meters across the dirt, leaving a deep trail behind it, and then finally stopped moving.
After that, there was nothing.
The battlefield fell strangely quiet.

The poisonous fog still covered the area, but the sounds of the Diggers had disappeared. There were no more drills grinding against metal, no more mechanical engines running beneath the earth, and no more impacts against the Advanced Barrier.
Victor smiled as he activated his eye’s ability again.
He carefully scanned through the thick fog, searching for any remaining signs of movement.
A few seconds later, his expression relaxed.
"All of them are down."
"You’re certain?" Wallace asked
Victor nodded.
"Every Digger has been destroyed."
Only then did the soldiers on the walls finally lower their weapons.
Dozens of B-Grade machines had appeared beneath their shelter, and for a brief moment, it had seemed as though they had discovered a method of destroying the Codebreakers’ strongest defense.
Yet none of them had managed to survive.
Atom had simply walked into the poison and destroyed every last one.
"The poison is still affecting the barrier," one of the operators suddenly reported. "But the corrosion has stopped spreading."
Althea looked toward the battlefield.
"Then keep monitoring it. Once the concentration drops, send the cleanup team."
"Understood."

Not long after, the dark green fog began to thin as the wind carried it away from the shelter. The wreckage of the Diggers gradually became visible again, scattered across the battlefield like discarded pieces of metal.
Then a black figure emerged from the remaining mist.
Atom walked back toward the shelter.
There wasn’t a scratch on its Aetherium armor.
Althea watched as it approached the gates and smiled...
She wanted to pat Atom’s shoulder but realized that there were still corrosive matter on its body...
"You need to wash up for a bit..."
She then turned to Wallace and shouted.
"Wallace, can you wash Atom? There’s still some poison residue or something on its body."
"Got it!"
Just like that, the immediate crisis was over, but she didn’t allow herself to relax completely.
Her thoughts returned to the strange machine that had appeared earlier.
The Nightmare Unit had discovered their shelter despite Claire’s illusion. Only a few minutes later, the Diggers had emerged from underground.
"Increase the surveillance range," she ordered. "I want every unusual movement around the shelter reported immediately. That Nightmare Unit must be eliminated."
The operators acknowledged the order, as they swiftly arranged a few people to watch over...
But as Althea looked beyond the ruined battlefield toward the distant wilderness, she couldn’t shake the feeling that this attack had been more than a simple raid.
Something had found them.
And sooner or later, she suspected that something would come back.
In the meantime, Kai became almost completely absorbed in Perfect World.
Although he had originally entered the virtual world to search for clues regarding the Divine Gene, he had never forgotten the other reason he was here.
His breakthrough.

In the real world, Kai had already reached Level 39 and accumulated enough experience to reach the maximum limit of the level. However, the system had made it clear that he could not advance any further until he completed the special requirements of his breakthrough quest.
[ Quest: Forge Your Legacy ]
[ Requirement 1: Strengthen your foundation further. ]
[ Progress: 8/8 ]
[ Requirement 2: Possess at least 5 Fused Gene Skills created through Skill Fusion. ]
[Progress: 5/5 ]
[ Requirement 3: Consume a Soul Enhancement Serum to unlock higher compatibility with advanced systems. ]
[ Progress: 0/1 ]
Kai stared at the final requirement for several seconds.
Everything else had already been completed.
Over the past several weeks, he had deliberately strengthened his Gene Skills and created additional fused abilities, gradually pushing himself toward the requirement that had once seemed distant.
Only the Soul Enhancement Serum remained.
Fortunately, even that problem had already been solved.
He had already spent 20,000 Credit Points to purchase it and Cornelio Aries had finally fulfilled his side of the transaction.
The Soul Enhancement Serum had been handed over through Farrah, allowing Kai to finally obtain the item he had been waiting for.
Soon, Kai looked at the small transparent vial in his hand.
The liquid inside was strangely clear, almost colorless, yet there seemed to be something moving beneath its surface whenever he tilted the container.
Kai carefully examined it using his Appraisal.
[ You have discovered Soul Enhancement Serum ]
[ Grade: Special ]
[ Description: A rare serum capable of enhancing the compatibility between a living soul and advanced evolutionary systems.
Effect: Upon consumption, the Soul Enhancement Serum will strengthen the user’s soul and establish the foundation required for higher-level evolutionary progression. ]
[ System Compatibility: Increased ]
[ Soul Compatibility: Increased ]
[ Advanced System Access: Unlocked ]
[ Warning:
The enhancement process will directly affect the user’s soul.
Individuals with insufficient Soul Resistance may experience severe mental strain, soul instability, temporary loss of consciousness, or other unforeseen complications during the enhancement process.
The effects of Soul Enhancement cannot be completely reversed once the process begins. ]
[ Special Requirement Detected ]
The user has fulfilled all other requirements for the Level 39 Breakthrough Quest.
Consumption of this item will fulfill the remaining requirement.
[ Level 39 → Level 40 Breakthrough: Available ]
"Incredible..."
Unlike ordinary Gene Stimulants, there was no familiar information describing simple physical enhancement. The Soul Enhancement Serum affected something much deeper.
It was meant to improve compatibility with advanced systems.
That alone made Kai cautious.
Anything capable of affecting the soul was unlikely to be completely harmless.
For a brief moment, he considered putting it away and waiting until he had gathered more information.
But he quickly dismissed the thought.
There was no point in obtaining the serum if he was too afraid to use it.
More importantly, he had already reached the limit of what Level 39 could provide.
His experience was capped and his breakthrough requirements were complete.
The only thing standing between him and the next stage was this final step.
Kai slowly uncorked the vial.
"If there’s a problem, I’ll deal with it."
He raised the serum to his lips and drank it...
Soon, the liquid entered his body and for several seconds, nothing happened.
Kai frowned.
Then his expression suddenly changed.
A strange sensation spread through his body.
It wasn’t pain... at least, not yet.
It felt as though something had suddenly entered the deepest part of his consciousness and begun searching through it.
His vision blurred as the room around him seemed to disappear for an instant, replaced by countless unfamiliar images.
Kai’s breathing became heavier.
The Soul Enhancement Serum wasn’t simply strengthening his body... it was changing something within him.
His spiritual energy began fluctuating violently, while the system interface in front of him blinked a few times...
[ Warning: Soul compatibility adjustment detected. ]
[ Warning: The process cannot be interrupted. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 363: Zodiacs ( Part 1 )
paragraphs: Kai gritted his teeth as he saw the two warnings just now.
So this was the danger Cornelio had mentioned.
He could feel something being altered inside him, and although the sensation wasn’t unbearable, there was an unmistakable feeling that he was crossing a boundary that could not easily be undone.
The system continued.
[ Analyzing Survivor’s soul structure... ]
[ Adjusting compatibility... ]
[ Compatibility adjustment in progress... ]
Kai remained still.
He had no idea what the final result would be, but there was no turning back now.
After what felt like several minutes, the strange sensation finally began to fade.
The pressure inside his mind gradually disappeared, and his surroundings slowly returned to normal.
Kai took a deep breath.
Then the notification appeared.
[ Requirements have been completed.]
[ Forge Your Legacy: Complete. ]
For a moment, Kai simply stared at the words.
Then another notification appeared.
[ Breakthrough Requirement fulfilled. ]
[ Level 39 restriction has been removed. ]
[ Reward: Evolutionary Ascension. ]
[ Veteran Physique Evolution unlocked. ]
[ Advanced stat growth, increased resilience against environmental hazards, and improved compatibility with higher-tier Gene Skills and Zodiac Enhancement.]
[ Title upgraded. ]
[ Expert Survivor to Veteran of Humanity. ]
Kai smiled as he saw it...
He had finally done it.
For so long, Level 39 had been an invisible wall.
He had accumulated enough experience to advance long ago, but no matter how much he hunted monsters, completed missions, or participated in battles, his level remained fixed.
Now that restriction was gone.
Kai slowly clenched his fist.
"Finally."
He had completed his breakthrough requirements... But there was one more thing left...
Kai’s smile slowly faded as another notification appeared before him.
It was different from the previous notifications.
This time, the system interface occupied almost his entire field of vision.
[ You have leveled up! ]
[ New Evolutionary Path detected. ]
[ Zodiac Trait System unlocked. ]
"Zodiac Trait System... It’s finally here."
He was already aware of the Twelve Zodiac Factions before and was aware that he would be part of it as well.
The system continued.
[ The Survivor has reached Level 40 and fulfilled the conditions required to select a Zodiac Trait. ]
[ Twelve Zodiac Traits are available. ]
[ Each Survivor may select only ONE Zodiac Trait. ]
[ Warning: Once selected, the Zodiac Trait cannot be changed through ordinary means. ]
Kai became serious.
’One trait.’
That meant this wasn’t something he could casually choose.
The system then displayed the available options.
[ Aries: Reverb Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Active Gene Skill Enhancement ]
[ Effect: Active Gene Skills can be repeated once within 3 seconds after activation without consuming additional Spirit. ]
[ Taurus: Anchor Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Defensive / Strength Enhancement ]
[ Effect: When using defensive or strength-based skills, gain temporary immunity to knockback and stagger for 5 seconds. ]
[ Gemini: Mirror Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Adaptive Support ]
[ Effect: Every 60 seconds, copy the last Active Gene Skill used by a target and cast it at 70% efficiency. ]
Kai was already somewhat aware of the Aries’ traits because of Cornelio and the others...
This was the same with Taurus’s trait after he had seen them in the previous raid in Citadel-09...
However, the Gemini’s trait came as a surprise...
"Copy another person’s skill?"
This one was different.
Unlike Aries and Taurus, Gemini didn’t strengthen a particular style of combat.
Instead, its usefulness depended on the opponent or ally he was fighting.
If he encountered someone with an exceptionally powerful Active Gene Skill, Mirror could potentially allow him to use that ability himself.
The 70% efficiency was a limitation, but it was still extremely useful.
Kai stared at the description for several seconds.
If he understood it correctly, this meant the stronger his opponent was, the more valuable Gemini could become.
Of course, there was also a sixty-second interval between uses.
Unlike Reverb, which immediately provided additional offensive power, Mirror required him to wait for the right opportunity.
In any case, he continued checking the other traits.
[ Cancer: Shell Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Defensive Enhancement ]
[ Effect: Defensive skills automatically trigger a special and additional barrier at 50% strength for 10 seconds. ]
[ Leo: Radiance Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Offensive Enhancement ]
[ Effect: The first offensive skill used in combat deals 30% additional damage and briefly silences the enemies within range. ]
[ Virgo: Precision Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Offensive Enhancement ]
[ Effect: The first strike of an offensive Active Gene Skill is guaranteed to become a critical hit. ]
"W-whoa~"
Kai couldn’t help but pause for a moment as he felt like it was getting really difficult to choose which Zodiac he should take!
He had originally expected the choice to be relatively simple. After all, each Zodiac represented a different combat style, and he could simply choose the one that best suited him.
But after seeing the traits in detail, Kai realized that each one had a completely different kind of value.
His gaze returned to the three traits that had caught his attention the most.
Kai immediately began imagining how useful they could be in an actual battle.
The first one he considered was Cancer’s Shell Trait.
An additional barrier would automatically appear whenever he activated a defensive skill, although it would only have 50% of the original skill’s strength and would last for ten seconds.
Kai thought about it for a moment but shook his head...
It was certainly useful...

If his original defensive skill was broken by a powerful attack, the additional barrier would still remain afterward. That could give him enough time to recover, reposition himself, or launch a counterattack.
More importantly, the additional barrier would activate automatically. He wouldn’t need to spend more Spirit or activate another skill just to gain the extra protection.
However, it wouldn’t suit him at all...
Kai then moved on to Leo’s Radiance Trait.
The first offensive skill he used in combat would deal 30% additional damage and briefly silence enemies within range.
Kai’s expression immediately became more interested.
"Thirty percent additional damage... and silencing them. Wait, does it mean that I’m stopping them from using any Survivor Skills? "
Without a doubt, the silence effect was what made the trait even more attractive.
He could potentially gain control of the battle from the very beginning with this ability!

chapters.title: Chapter 364: Zodiacs ( Part 2 )
paragraphs: Kai imagined himself facing a powerful opponent and launching his fastest attack before they could properly react...
This Radiance Trait was just too incredible. Still, it was quite the same with Virgo’s Precision Trait!
After all, it was a guaranteed Critical Hit!
"Both of them are perfect for Survivor Skills that move fast to hit the target..."
After taking a deep breath, Kai continued checking the others...
[ Libra: Balance Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Sustained Combat Enhancement ]
[ Effect: Casting a skill restores 5% of missing Health or Spirit, whichever is lower. ]
[ Scorpio: Venom Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Offensive Debuff ]

[ Effect: Offensive skills inflict Venom on the target, dealing 2% of the target’s maximum Health as damage every second for 6 seconds. Venom can stack up to 5 times, with each stack increasing the damage by an additional 2%. ]
[ Sagittarius: Pierce Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Ranged Combat Enhancement ]
[ Effect: Ranged skills ignore 25% of enemy armor, including barriers. ]
Kai’s attention settled on Libra’s Balance Trait first...
"Five percent of my missing Health or Spirit..."
He thought about it for a moment. At first, the recovery didn’t seem particularly impressive, but the fact that it activated whenever he cast a skill made it much more interesting...
It was definitely the best recovery ability out there!

If he continued using his skills throughout a battle, the recovery could gradually add up. More importantly, it wasn’t limited to Health. If his Spirit was running low, the trait would restore Spirit instead.
"That’s actually pretty useful."

Kai could already imagine himself fighting a powerful opponent for an extended period. As long as he continued using his skills, he would constantly recover a small portion of his missing resources. It wouldn’t allow him to instantly recover from serious injuries, but it could significantly improve his endurance.
"This would be really good for prolonged battles."
Kai nodded and moved on to the next trait, Scorpio’s Venom Trait.
"Reducing the enemy’s defenses..."
His expression immediately became more interested.
Unlike Leo and Virgo, which focused on strengthening his own attacks, Scorpio weakened the opponent instead. The fact that the effect could stack made it even more appealing.
"If I keep attacking the same target, their health will just continue to drop unless they have something to remove debuffs..."

Kai immediately imagined himself fighting a powerful monster with extremely high defenses. His first attack would apply the debuff, and his next attack would add another stack. If he continued attacking without giving the enemy enough time to recover, the effect could gradually turn a difficult opponent into an increasingly vulnerable target.
"That could become terrifying in a long fight."
The six-second duration was also important. As long as Kai continued attacking within that period, he could potentially maintain the debuff instead of allowing it to disappear.

However, compared with Leo and Virgo, Scorpio required more time to show its full potential. Leo could immediately increase the power of his first attack, while Virgo could immediately guarantee a critical hit. Scorpio needed Kai to keep attacking.
"Still, if the enemy is strong enough, this might actually be better."
Kai continued thinking about it.
A powerful opponent would naturally have stronger defenses, and the stronger their defenses were, the more valuable it would be to continuously reduce them.
Still, he wasn’t sure if this would be effective against machines...
After all, the main enemy here was still the A.I. Civilization, Anima...
In any case, his gaze then moved toward Sagittarius.
"Ignoring twenty-five percent of their armor..."
This one was different from Scorpio. Instead of gradually weakening the enemy, Sagittarius allowed his ranged attacks to bypass a portion of their defenses from the beginning.
"Even barriers?"
That was the part Kai was interesting.

A powerful barrier could completely change the outcome of a battle. If an enemy relied heavily on defensive barriers, being able to ignore twenty-five percent of them could give Kai a significant advantage.
He imagined himself standing at a distance and firing a powerful ranged Survivor Skill at an enemy protected by a massive barrier.
Normally, the barrier would absorb part of the attack.
But with Pierce...
"Twenty-five percent of it wouldn’t matter."
Kai couldn’t help but smile.
"This would be really useful against defensive-type Survivors."
There was, however, an obvious limitation.
It only worked with ranged skills.
If he was fighting at close range, the trait wouldn’t provide him with any benefit...
Perhaps this would be better with Ralph, who had Sharpshooter Talent and others.
Kai wryly smiled as he began comparing the traits in his mind...
"Why are all of these so good?"
Kai couldn’t help but sigh.
The more traits he examined, the harder the choice became.
In any case, he checked the last batch...
[ Capricorn: Endure Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Survival Enhancement ]
[ Effect: Once every 60 seconds, survive a fatal attack with 1 HP and instantly recover 20% Spirit. ]
[ Aquarius: Flow Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Movement Enhancement ]
[ Effect: Movement-based skills recover their cooldowns 90% faster. ]
[ Pisces: Tidal Shift Trait ]
[ Trait Type: Evasion Enhancement ]

[ Effect: Once every 30 seconds, when the user is struck by an attack, they can automatically shift their body with the force of the impact, reducing the damage received by 50% and moving 5 meters away from the attacker. ]
"Endure... Flow... and Tidal Shift..."
Kai stared at the three options and sighed...
He didn’t immediately know what he wanted.
Every trait was useful... More importantly, none of them were simply stronger versions of the others.
They represented completely different specialties...
Aries, Leo, Virgo, and Scorpio leaned toward offense, while Taurus, Cancer, and Capricorn focused on survival and defense.
Meanwhile, Gemini offered versatility as Libra emphasized sustained combat, and Sagittarius specialized in ranged attacks.
Then, Aquarius focused on mobility, while Pisces belonged to a more evasive and reactive style.
Kai slowly rubbed his chin.
"This isn’t an easy choice."
The system then displayed one final notification.
[ Zodiac Trait Selection ]
[ Please select ONE Zodiac Trait. ]
[ Selected trait will become permanently bound to the Survivor. ]
[ Current Selection: None ]
Kai looked at the twelve traits again.
This wasn’t merely a reward for reaching Level 40.
It was a choice that could influence the way he fought from this point onward.
And with the number of powerful Gene Skills he had already accumulated, choosing the right trait could make a significant difference.
"I need to think carefully."
He wasn’t going to choose simply because one trait looked powerful.
He needed to find the one that suited him best...

chapters.title: Chapter 365: Zodiacs ( Part 3 )
paragraphs: Kai checked his current Status as he pondered which zodiac he should choose.
[ Name: Kai ]
[ Title: Veteran of Humanity, Trailblazer, Stronghold Defender, Guardian, Strongest One ]
[ Guild: Codebreakers ]
[ Level: 40 ]
[ Physique Rating: B ]
[ Talent: Infinite Gift Pack (SSS) ]
[ Active Skills: Fast Appraisal Lv7, Spirit Dominion [F] Lv7, Titan Step [F] Lv7, High Jump Lv1, Spirit Lance Lv1, Shadow Dash Lv1, Neural Acceleration [F] Lv7 ]
[ Passive Skills: Bio-Adaptive Constitution Lv9, Great Protection [F] Lv7, Slayer’s Flow [F] Lv7, Solid Balance Lv1, Blood Regeneration Lv1, Enhanced Physique Lv1, Fast Spirit Recovery Lv7 ]
[ Skill Points: 0 ]
[ Reputation Points: 40 ]
[ Inventory Slots: 9 ]
Kai briefly looked through his updated status before his attention returned to the skills he had acquired in Perfect World.

During his time in the virtual world, he had completed several quests that rewarded him with new Gene Skills and Skill Points. The most notable was Neural Acceleration, which he had created through Skill Fusion by combining Mental Acceleration and Neural Enhancement. The two abilities had similar effects, but their combination produced a much stronger skill that temporarily accelerated his neural processing speed, allowing him to react and think faster during combat.

He had also obtained Spirit Lance and Shadow Dash after completing several combat and exploration quests. Although none of them were particularly powerful on their own, they greatly expanded the options available to him in battle.

The additional Skill Points he had earned from completing those quests had also allowed him to strengthen several of his Gene Skills. By the time he finished the requirements for his breakthrough, he had managed to bring five of his Gene Skills to Level 7 and create another fused ability.
Kai couldn’t help but smile.
His current skill set was already considerably more complete than before.
However, that only made his decision more difficult.
He looked back at the twelve Zodiac Traits displayed before him.
With his current abilities, almost every one of them could be useful.
The question was no longer whether a Zodiac Trait was strong.
It was which one could bring out the greatest potential of the skills he already possessed.
Kai first considered Virgo’s Precision Trait.
A guaranteed critical hit on the first strike of an offensive Active Gene Skill was extremely tempting.

With his current skills, he could make excellent use of it, especially when combined with Shadow Dash or Neural Acceleration. If he could close the distance before his opponent reacted, his first Gene Skill Attack, Spirit Lance, could potentially deal devastating damage.
However, Kai eventually shook his head.
"Only the first strike..."
It was powerful, but it was limited to the opening attack of a battle. Once that attack was used, the trait would no longer provide any additional benefit until the next considered battle.
His gaze then moved to Leo’s Radiance Trait.

Thirty percent additional damage on his first offensive skill was already impressive, but the brief silence effect made it even more valuable. Being able to prevent an enemy from using their Survivor Skills at the beginning of a battle could give him an enormous advantage.
Kai considered it for a while before slowly narrowing his eyes.
"Very powerful, but it’s not really the best against A.I. Soldiers..."
Though he acknowledged that there were also many human enemies, he must also acknowledge that the main enemy of this apocalypse was the machine civilization.
However, there was still something he didn’t particularly like about it.

Like Virgo, Leo’s greatest advantage was concentrated into a single opening attack. If his first attack failed to end the battle or create a decisive advantage, much of the trait’s value would disappear.
Finally, Kai’s attention returned to Aries.
Reverb was much simpler.
It didn’t strengthen only his first attack, nor did it depend on a specific type of enemy.
It simply gave him another use of an Active Gene Skill without requiring additional Spirit Points, and as far as he remembered, even the cooldown was ignored.
Of course, there would be more details about the Zodiac Trait once he selected but for now, he felt that it could be the best option for him...
Neural Acceleration could improve his reaction speed and decision-making...
Shadow Dash could help him reposition quickly, while Titan Step gave him another powerful movement-based option. Spirit Lance might also become one of his go-to Gene Skills because of this...
Most importantly, Reverb would continue to be useful even after the opening exchange.
"If I can use it properly, I won’t just get one extra attack."
Kai smiled.
"I’ll get another opportunity to use whichever skill I need at that moment."
That was what finally convinced him.
Kai looked at the three traits one last time...
"Chamber... What do you think is the best for me? I think Aries is the best..."
Just like that, he consulted this A.I. Assistant and explained his options...
Soon, Chamber also gave its conclusion...
[ Based on your current abilities, Aries has the highest compatibility with your combat style. ]
"Why?"

[ Your current skill set contains multiple offensive Active Gene Skills, including fused Gene Skills with significantly higher combat potential. Reverb allows you to immediately repeat one of these abilities without waiting for its normal cooldown, which greatly increases your burst damage. ]
"Fine... We made the same choice, so I’ll choose Aries."
The moment he spoke, the system immediately responded.
[ Zodiac Trait Selection confirmed. ]
[ Selected Zodiac: Aries ]
[ Aries Trait: Reverb ]
[ Trait Type: Active Gene Skill Enhancement ]
[ Effect: Active Gene Skills can be repeated once within 3 seconds after activation without consuming additional Spirit or triggering their normal cooldown. ]

[ Drawback: After an Active Gene Skill is repeated through Reverb, that skill enters a cooldown period twice as long as its normal cooldown. This increased cooldown applies only to the immediate cooldown following the repeated activation. Subsequent activations return to the skill’s normal cooldown. ]
[ Zodiac Trait successfully integrated. ]
’So that’s the drawback, huh... It’s still acceptable.’
Kai then suddenly felt a strange sensation spreading through his body.
It wasn’t painful.
Instead, it felt as though something had connected itself to his Gene Skills, creating a new layer of compatibility between them and his body.
Then several more notifications appeared.
[ Gene structure adaptation detected. ]
[ Aries Trait has successfully synchronized with the Survivor’s Gene System. ]
[ Active Gene Skill compatibility increased. ]
[ Reverb Trait has been permanently bound to the Survivor. ]
[ Warning: Zodiac Trait cannot be changed through ordinary means. ]
Kai stared at the notifications for several seconds before slowly clenching his fist.
He had finally chosen his path.
’I hope I made the right choice...’
Kai thought to himself as he decided to go outside to test his new Trait.
