chapters.title: Chapter 378: Opening the Gifts
paragraphs: Kai stared at the list of Legendary Gift Packs for a while before his expression slowly became serious.
There was one thing that he wanted more than anything else.
The improvement of his Infinite Gift Pack Talent.
The Talent had already provided him with countless useful items, and it was the reason he had been able to develop so quickly after the apocalypse began.
However, there was still a limit.
His current Talent could only infinitely produce Basic, Enhanced, and Superior Grade Gift Packs.
These Legendary Gift Packs were different.
They were rewards from the System itself, and Kai couldn’t produce them endlessly with his Talent.
That thought made him feel slightly dissatisfied.
"I really need to upgrade my Talent."
Kai knew that if he could raise the grade of his Infinite Gift Pack Talent to Legendary, then everything would change.
Basic, Enhanced, Superior, Legendary... That would be really perfect.
’Soon...’ Kai thought.
These Legendary Gift Packs were basically a glimpse of what his Infinite Gift Pack Talent could eventually produce.
They were like a teaser of the things waiting for him at the next stage.
"Talent Upgrade Crystals..."
Kai muttered. That was what he needed.
Unfortunately, Talent Upgrade Crystals were extremely rare, and he had no idea when he would find another one.
Furthermore, he knew that he didn’t just need one of them. He wouldn’t be surprised if he had to find a dozen of them.
Still, after seeing the contents of the Legendary Gift Packs, his desire to upgrade his Talent had increased considerably.
"I definitely need to find more."
Kai shook his head and looked at the gift packs again.
For now, there was another problem... He couldn’t open most of them inside his room.
The Transport Gift Pack alone contained several large vehicles.
The Shelter Gift Pack contained an armored mobile bunker.
The Energy Gift Pack contained a fusion reactor.
Even some of the other packs contained equipment that was far too large to simply appear inside his small room.
"If I open those here, I’ll probably get crushed before I even get to enjoy the rewards."
Kai chuckled.
That left him with only a few reasonable choices...
The Weapon Gift Pack was one of them.
Well, most of its contents were relatively compact, so he could safely open it here.
Kai selected the Weapon Gift Pack.
"Let’s start with this one."
Ding!
[ Weapon Gift Pack (Legendary) selected. ]
[ Would you like to open it? ]
"Open."
The moment Kai confirmed, the gift pack suddenly released a brilliant golden light.
A few seconds later, the light disappeared.
Several objects had appeared throughout the room.
Kai immediately stood up and looked around.
A large, dark-colored weapon was resting against the wall.
Beside it was a strange-looking pistol, a long combat blade, a set of heavy armor, several small grenades, and a compact machine that looked somewhat like a toolbox.
Kai’s eyes immediately focused on the largest weapon.
"Is that the railgun?"
He walked over and carefully inspected it.
The weapon was considerably larger than a normal rifle, with a long barrel and several metallic components running along its frame.
Kai used Fast Appraisal.
Ding!
[ You have discovered Electromagnetic Railgun! ]
[ Grade: Legendary ]
[ Type: Electromagnetic Heavy Weapon ]

[ Description: A high-powered electromagnetic weapon that accelerates metal projectiles to extreme velocities using electromagnetic propulsion. Designed to penetrate heavily armored targets and fortified structures. Its internal energy system allows repeated firing without conventional ammunition, but each shot consumes a significant amount of stored energy. ]
"So it doesn’t even need normal bullets?"
He carefully examined the weapon.
The concept was similar to the advanced weapons he had seen from the machine civilization, although this weapon was clearly designed for human use.
"If this can really penetrate fortified structures, it could be extremely useful against those machines."
Kai placed it down before turning toward the next item.
The pistol looked much more ordinary at first glance.
However, its metallic surface had a strange blue glow running through the frame.
Kai raised his hand and appraised it.
Ding!
[ You have discovered Plasma Pistol! ]
[ Grade: Legendary ]
[ Type: Energy Pistol ]

[ Description: A compact energy weapon that generates and fires superheated plasma bolts. Each shot produces intense thermal energy capable of burning through heavy armor and mechanical components. The weapon contains an integrated energy cell that automatically recovers a small amount of charge over time. ]
"A plasma pistol... It looks really cool..."
He turned it over in his hand.
Compared to the railgun, this weapon was much easier to carry.

He immediately used Fast Appraisal.
Ding!
[ You have discovered Monomolecular Combat Blade! ]
[ Grade: Legendary ]
[ Type: Monomolecular Cutting Weapon ]

[ Description: A perfect blade with an edge sharpened to an extremely thin molecular scale. Its cutting surface can slice through many conventional metals, armor plates, and materials with minimal resistance. The blade is extremely durable but requires careful handling due to its exceptional sharpness. ]

"Monomolecular..."
He carefully moved his finger near the edge without actually touching it.
"Yeah, I’m definitely not going to test its sharpness on myself."
Kai couldn’t help but smile.
The blade was simple compared to the railgun, but its ability to cut through armor made it extremely dangerous.

However, several mechanical components were built into the armor itself.
Kai immediately became interested.
Ding!
[ You have discovered Powered Combat Armor! ]
[ Grade: Legendary ]
[ Type: Powered Combat Armor ]

[ Description: A full-body combat armor equipped with an internal power-assistance system. The Talent had already provided him with countless useful items, and it was the reason he had been able to develop so quickly after the apocalypse began.
However, there was still a limit.
His current Talent could only infinitely produce Basic, Enhanced, and Superior Grade Gift Packs.
These Legendary Gift Packs were different.
They were rewards from the System itself, and Kai couldn’t produce them endlessly with his Talent.
That thought made him feel slightly dissatisfied.
"I really need to upgrade my Talent."

"Talent Upgrade Crystals..."
Kai muttered.
That was what he needed.
Unfortunately, Talent Upgrade Crystals were extremely rare, and he had no idea when he would find another one.
Furthermore, he knew that he didn’t just need one of them.
He wouldn’t be surprised if he had to find a dozen of them.

chapters.title: Chapter 379: The New Items and the Replacement
paragraphs: "If the system really increases physical strength and movement speed, this could make an already strong awakened fighter even more dangerous."
Kai looked at the armor for a moment before glancing down at himself.
Fortunately, it wasn’t too large for him. The moment he put it on, the armor automatically adjusted to fit his body perfectly, almost as if it had been made specifically for him.

The armor had a simple and streamlined appearance, with smooth gray outer plates covering his chest, shoulders, arms, and legs. There were no unnecessary decorations or complicated designs on its surface, making it look more like advanced combat equipment than ordinary armor.
Several small mechanical components were built into the joints, allowing the armor to move naturally with his body. Despite its heavy appearance, Kai could barely feel its weight after putting it on.
He clenched his fist and moved his arms a few times.
"Not bad."
The armor responded smoothly to every movement, without restricting him in the slightest.
Kai took a few steps around the room before stopping.
"It really does feel like I’m not wearing anything heavy."
Considering his current strength and physique, wearing the armor wasn’t a problem at all.
In fact, Kai could already imagine how much stronger he would become once the armor’s power-assistance system was activated.
After feeling satisfied, Kai finally put them off and continued looking at the other items.
There were still several small objects remaining.
Kai picked one of them up.
It was a small metallic sphere with several tiny lights around its surface.
He used Fast Appraisal again.
Ding!
[ You have discovered Smart Grenade! ]
[ Grade: Legendary Grade Consumable ]
[ Type: Programmable Explosive ]

[ Description: An advanced programmable grenade capable of automatically detecting nearby targets and adjusting its detonation timing. The user can configure the grenade to detonate on impact, after a set delay, or when a designated target enters its detection range. Each grenade contains a compact high-yield explosive core and a directional fragmentation system. ]
Kai’s expression became slightly strange.
"Smart grenades..."
He looked at the remaining ones.
"There are six of them."
That was quite a terrifying amount of firepower to carry around.
Kai carefully placed them back down before turning toward the final item.
Unlike the other weapons, this one looked more like a compact industrial machine.
It had a small control panel on the front and several mechanical components folded inside its rectangular body.
He glanced at his Spirit Points and seeing that he hadn’t spent much, he used Fast Appraisal once again.
Ding!
[ You have discovered Portable Ammunition Fabricator! ]
[ Grade: Legendary Grade Utility Equipment ]
[ Type: Automated Ammunition Fabrication Device ]

[ Description: A compact fabrication machine capable of producing compatible ammunition by processing suitable metal, chemical, and energy-based materials. The device can manufacture conventional ammunition, electromagnetic projectiles, explosive rounds, and several specialized ammunition types after receiving the necessary material and production data. ]
Kai stared at it.
Then his eyes slowly widened.
"Wait."
He looked at the machine again.
"It can really manufacture ammunition?"
Kai immediately understood how valuable this thing was.
Ammunition had always been a problem in the apocalypse. Even if he could produce it by opening a lot of Weapon Gift Packs, that would also mean that he would have a lot of items that he couldn’t use!
However, with this almost-magical Fabricator, he would actually have fewer worries now!
After all, even if someone possessed powerful weapons, they couldn’t keep using them forever if their ammunition ran out.
But this machine could potentially solve that problem.
As long as he had the necessary materials and the required production data, he could manufacture more ammunition whenever he needed it.
Kai walked around the machine and carefully examined it.
"This is actually much more useful than I expected."
He looked at all the items scattered throughout his room.
The electromagnetic railgun.
The plasma pistol... The monomolecular combat blade... The powered combat armor... The smart grenades... and the ammunition fabricator.
Kai couldn’t help but smile.
Every single item was something that would have been considered priceless before the apocalypse.
And this was only one of the ten Legendary Gift Packs.
He still had nine more waiting for him.
Kai looked toward the remaining gift packs in his inventory.
"I definitely need to find a bigger place before opening the others."
He paused for a moment.
Then his eyes narrowed with excitement.
"Especially the Technology Chest."
That reward was different from everything else.
It came directly from the machine civilization.
And after everything he had witnessed inside the Floating Citadel, Kai couldn’t help but wonder what kind of technology it contained...
Unlike the Legendary Gift Packs, he had no clue what this chest would contain aside from the fact that it was a Technology.
The System had never given him anything like this before.
"It came directly from the hidden quest..."
Kai’s expression became serious.
It was specifically related to the machine civilization.
And Kai had already seen how terrifying their technology was.

The Floating Citadel alone had been enough to overwhelm an entire human city. Its defensive systems, energy weapons, machines, and internal network were far beyond anything humanity currently possessed.
If this chest contained even a fraction of that technology, its value would be difficult to estimate.
"Hopefully, it’s something useful."
Kai thought about it for a moment before deciding not to open it yet.
His room was already filled with the items from the Weapon Gift Pack.
If something enormous appeared from the Technology Chest, he didn’t want to find himself trapped underneath it.
"I’ll open it after I find a bigger place."
Kai stored the thought in the back of his mind. Then, he recalled the Anima Civilization... He knew that whatever technology it was, he would be happy to obtain it.
"If I can obtain their technology and understand how it works..."
His voice trailed off as the possibilities he had in mind were already enough to excite him.
The ability to reproduce even a small portion of the machine civilization’s technology could completely change the development of human settlements.
"Right... I should go back to the shelter first."
Kai thought about it as he recalled that Renji should be arriving soon to take over for Farrah, whose level had stagnated for weeks because she had been stuck running the shop.

chapters.title: Chapter 380: Troublesome Customers
paragraphs: Several days later, a young man quietly entered Cameron City.
He didn’t attract much attention.

Compared to the countless survivors entering and leaving the city every day, there was nothing particularly unusual about him. He wore a simple set of combat clothes, carried a backpack, and had two androids following him from a short distance behind.
The young man was Renji, a newer member of the Codebreakers Guild.
He had been sent here to take over for Farrah at Kai’s Shop.
However, instead of immediately going to the shop, Renji decided to spend a few days exploring Cameron City first.
It was his first time visiting the city.
And there was something else he really wanted to learn more about...
The Zodiac Factions.
He just learned through the Guild Chat that the Zodiac Factions had become much more prominent. Even someone who wasn’t particularly interested in politics couldn’t ignore their influence.
Among them, the Aries Faction had attracted the most attention recently.
The faction had suddenly begun protecting a certain shop in the city, and rumors about the shop’s owner had spread throughout the city.
Renji naturally wanted to know more.
He had heard about the Aries Faction from other members of the Codebreakers Guild, but hearing about something and seeing it with his own eyes were two different things.
So, instead of immediately reporting to Kai’s Shop, Renji spent the next few days walking around Cameron City.
He visited several busy streets, watched the members of different factions, listened to conversations between survivors, and quietly observed how the city operated.
The more he explored, the more interested he became.
Cameron City was far more developed than he had expected.
There were shops selling equipment, players gathering in groups before leaving the city, merchants exchanging supplies, and various factions establishing their own areas of influence.
It was completely different from other places Renji had visited before.
And then there was the Aries Faction.
Renji quickly noticed that the faction’s members were particularly active around a certain area.
The reason wasn’t difficult to guess.
They were protecting Kai’s Shop.
Renji had already heard about it before coming here, but he hadn’t expected the security to be this obvious.
Several powerful awakened fighters could often be seen nearby, and ordinary Survuvirs rarely caused trouble around the shop.
After observing everything for several days, Renji finally decided that he had learned enough.
It was time to report to the shop.
When he finally arrived, Farrah was standing behind the counter.
She was organizing several items when she noticed someone approaching.
Her eyes immediately landed on the unfamiliar young man.
"Can I help you?"
Renji smiled politely.
"Are you Farrah?"
Farrah nodded.
"Yes. Who are you?"
"I’m Renji. I’m from the Codebreakers Guild."
Farrah paused.
She looked at him for a moment before her expression changed slightly.
"That Renji? The one in the Top 10 Rankings?"
"Yes."
"I’ve heard about you."
Farrah had never met Renji before. He was a newer recruit and had joined the Codebreakers Guild after she had already started working at the shop.
Still, the guild members had mentioned him before.
Apparently, he was a fairly capable Survivor and had two androids that usually accompanied him.
Farrah looked behind Renji.
Then she frowned.
"Where are your androids?"
Renji immediately understood what she was asking.
"Oh, I left them somewhere... I can’t have them always following me around."
Farrah blinked.
"You came all the way here without them?"
"I wanted to explore the city myself."
Renji shrugged.
"They tend to attract a little too much attention, so I left them behind. I figured they could stay at the shelter and help with some tasks while I was here."
Farrah nodded.
"That makes sense."
She had already seen enough unusual things in the apocalypse that two androids no longer surprised her very much.
"So you’ve been here for a few days?"
"Yes."
Farrah stared at him.
"And you only decided to come here now?"
Renji gave an embarrassed smile.
"I wanted to look around first. I’ve never been to Cameron City before."
Renji glanced outside the shop.
"And I wanted to learn more about the Zodiac Factions."
Farrah’s expression became slightly more interested.
"Did you learn something?"
Renji nodded. He had already spent several days observing them, so he had a fairly good idea of how much influence they had around this area.
"They are all powerful."
"Hahaha! They’re definitely powerful. I don’t know everything about them, but they’ve helped protect the shop several times."
Renji nodded thoughtfully.
"That’s what I wanted to learn more about."
Farrah looked at him for a moment before smiling.
"Well, you can worry about the Zodiac Factions later."
She pointed toward the shelves behind her.
"If you’re taking over for me, you have a lot to learn first."
Renji followed her finger and immediately became serious.
"The shop?"
Farrah smiled.
"Kai expects us to handle it properly, so I’m going to teach you everything before I leave."
Renji nodded.
"Understood."
Just like that, Farrah began explaining how the shop operated.
She taught him how to organize the items, how to check inventory, how to deal with customers, and which products needed to be kept in specific areas.
She also explained how Kai preferred the shop to be managed.
"Don’t randomly change the prices."
"I won’t."
"If someone asks about an item you don’t understand, don’t make something up. Just tell them that you’ll need to check first."
"Understood."
"And don’t let people cause trouble inside the shop."
Renji nodded seriously.
"What if they’re members of a powerful faction?"
Farrah glanced at him.
"Especially then."
Renji couldn’t help but smile.
"Got it."
Farrah continued teaching him for several hours.
At first, Renji simply listened.
But as time passed, he began asking more questions.
He was surprisingly quick to learn.
Farrah soon realized that she wouldn’t have to worry too much about leaving the shop in his hands.
"He learns fast."
She couldn’t help but feel relieved.
She had been stuck managing the shop for weeks, and although she didn’t hate the job, she had been eager to return to leveling.
Now that Renji had finally arrived, she could finally return to hunting and improving her strength.
After finishing another explanation, Farrah looked toward him.
"I think that’s enough for today."
Renji nodded.
"Thank you for teaching me."
"No problem... Tomorrow, I’ll teach you how to deal with the more troublesome customers."
Renji’s expression became slightly serious.
"There are troublesome customers?"
Farrah stared at him.
"Of course."
She sighed.
"You’ll understand soon."

"The shop?"
Farrah smiled.
"Kai expects us to handle it properly, so I’m going to teach you everything before I leave."
Renji nodded.
"Understood."
Just like that, Farrah began explaining how the shop operated.
She taught him how to organize the items, how to check inventory, how to deal with customers, and which products needed to be kept in specific areas.
She also explained how Kai preferred the shop to be managed.
"Don’t randomly change the prices."
"I won’t."
"If someone asks about an item you don’t understand, don’t make something up.
Just tell them that you’ll need to check first."
"Understood."
"And don’t let people cause trouble inside the shop."
Renji nodded seriously.
"What if they’re members of a powerful faction?"
Farrah glanced at him.
"Especially then."
Renji couldn’t help but smile.
"Got it."
Farrah continued teaching him for several hours.
At first, Renji simply listened.
But as time passed, he began asking more questions.
He was surprisingly quick to learn.
Farrah soon realized that she wouldn’t have to worry too much about leaving the shop in his hands.
"He learns fast."
She couldn’t help but feel relieved.
She had been stuck managing the shop for weeks, and although she didn’t hate the job, she had been eager to return to leveling.
Now that Renji had finally arrived, she could finally return to hunting and improving her strength.
After finishing another explanation, Farrah looked toward him.
"I think that’s enough for today."
Renji nodded.
"Thank you for teaching me."
"No problem...
Tomorrow, I’ll teach you how to deal with the more troublesome customers."
Renji’s expression became slightly serious.
"There are troublesome customers?"
Farrah stared at him.
"Of course."
She sighed.
"You’ll understand soon."

chapters.title: Chapter 381: Leaving the City
paragraphs: Later that day, Kai finally finished checking most of his Legendary Gift Packs...
He had originally planned to stay away for a little longer, but after dealing with the Floating Citadel, there were several things he needed to take care of.
More importantly, he had heard that Renji had already arrived at the shop.
When Kai entered Kai’s Shop, he immediately noticed the young man standing behind the counter.
Renji also noticed him.
For a moment, neither of them said anything.
Then Renji’s eyes widened slightly.
"Sir Kai..."
Kai nodded.
"Yes."
Renji looked at him for a few seconds before smiling.
"I’ve heard a lot about you."
Kai couldn’t help but smile as well.
"I’ve heard about you too."
Of course, Kai already knew who Renji was.
As one of the newer members of the Codebreakers Guild, Renji’s name had already appeared in the guild’s information. More importantly, he was currently among the Top 10 Rankings.
That alone was enough to make Kai pay attention.
Seeing him in person was still somewhat impressive.
The Top 10 survivors were the strongest people humanity had produced so far, at least according to the ranking system.
However, they were all still below level 40...
In fact, none of the other Top 10 survivors had reached Level 40 yet.
That meant none of them had received a Zodiac.
Kai was currently the only one who had obtained a Zodiac, due to the strict requirements
In any case, he had already received the Aries Trait and understood just how powerful a Zodiac could become.
Because of that, Kai couldn’t help but feel that there was now a clear difference between himself and the other high-ranking survivors.
They were strong... But they had yet to reach the same stage he had reached.
Still, Kai wasn’t arrogant enough to underestimate them.
Reaching the Top 10 while still below Level 40 was already an impressive achievement.
"So you’re the one who will be running the shop while Farrah was away?"
"Yes. Farrah has been teaching me everything since yesterday."
Kai glanced toward Farrah.
"How is he doing?"
Farrah smiled.
"He’s learning quickly. I don’t think there will be any problems leaving the shop to him."
Kai nodded in satisfaction.
"That’s good."
He then looked toward Renji.
"By the way, where are your androids?"
Renji chuckled.
"They’re here. They’ve actually been following me this entire time."
Kai looked around the shop.
He couldn’t see anything unusual.
"Following you?"
"Yes."
Renji smiled.
"They’re just really good at staying out of sight."
Kai’s expression became slightly interested.
He had assumed that Renji had simply left his androids behind at the Codebreakers Shelter.
Apparently, that wasn’t entirely true.
Renji chuckled and finally summoned the two invisible androids who had been following him secretly all this time.
At first, nothing seemed to happen.
Then two figures slowly appeared inside the shop.
Kai’s eyes widened slightly.
"Those are..."
Two young-looking figures were standing behind Renji.
At first glance, they looked completely human.
They had natural-looking skin, human facial features, and were wearing ordinary human clothes. There was nothing obviously mechanical about them.
If Kai hadn’t already known that they were androids, he would have assumed they were simply two ordinary survivors.
One was a young man, while the other was a young woman.
The two androids quietly stood beside Renji, looking around the shop with calm expressions.
"These are my androids."
Renji gestured toward them.
"They’ve been with me for quite some time."
Kai stared at them for a moment.
"That’s quite impressive."
He had already seen the machines used by the machine civilization, but these two were completely different.
They looked like ordinary humans.
Even their movements were natural.
Kai then asked Chamber and quietly examined them.
The A.I. immediately displayed several lines of information.
[ Target detected. ]
[ Type: Advanced Humanoid Android ]
[ Threat Level: Low ]
[ Functions: Combat Support, Intelligence Gathering, Household Assistance, Infiltration ]
Kai smiled as he saw it... "So they’re designed for infiltration as well."
Renji nodded.
"Among other things."
He glanced at the two androids.
"They’re capable of blending into human settlements, so most people don’t realize they’re androids unless they already know."
Kai nodded thoughtfully.
That explained why he hadn’t noticed them earlier.
"If that’s the case, they could be useful here. They can work here with you."
"That’s what I thought..."
Kai looked toward Farrah.
"Yes... Farrah is going back to leveling, and you’re taking over the shop. Having two additional people here would make things easier."
"That’s perfect."
"They don’t need to do anything complicated. They can help organize the inventory, assist customers, watch the shop, and handle other simple tasks."
The two androids nodded silently.
Kai looked at them again.
"Can they communicate normally?"
"Yes."
One of the androids immediately stepped forward.
"Of course."
Kai paused.
The voice sounded completely natural.
He couldn’t help but glance at Renji again.
"That’s convenient."
Renji laughed.
"They’re better at acting human than I am. I bought some modules I found in the reputation store to upgrade them. To be honest, all my RPs were used to fix these two."
Kai shook his head with a smile.
With the two androids staying at the shop, Kai wouldn’t have to worry about leaving everything to Renji alone.
At that moment, two small figures who had been listening nearby finally reacted.
"Really? We’re going back to the shelter?"
Xinyi’s eyes immediately lit up.
She had been quietly listening to their conversation, but the moment she heard that they would be returning to the Codebreakers Shelter, she could no longer hide her excitement.
Xian was also smiling.
"Does that mean we can see your shelter?"
Kai nodded.
"Yes."
The two siblings exchanged excited looks.

They had spent quite some time around the shop, and although they had gotten used to the place, the Codebreakers Shelter was like a mystical place to them... After all, they heard a lot about that place from Farrah...
Xinyi instinctively touched her mechanical arm before smiling brightly.
"I want to visit your home, Sir Kai..."
Xian nodded several times.
"Me too!"
Seeing their reactions, Kai couldn’t help but smile.
"Then we’ll leave soon."
"Okay!"
The two siblings immediately became excited, already looking forward to returning to the shelter.

chapters.title: Chapter 382: The Family
paragraphs: Before leaving Cameron City, Kai decided that there was one more thing they needed to take care of.
The two children needed new clothes.

Xian and Xinyi had been wearing the same few outfits for quite some time, and although their clothes were still usable, Kai felt that there was no reason to let them continue wearing worn-out clothing now that they were returning to the Codebreakers Shelter.
"We should get them some new clothes first," Farrah suggested after seeing Kai looking at their clothes.
Kai nodded in agreement. "Let’s buy several sets for each of them."
The two children immediately became interested when they heard that.
"New clothes?" Xinyi asked, her eyes lighting up.
"Yes," Kai replied with a smile. "You can choose some of them yourself."
That was enough to make Xinyi excited.

The group soon found a clothing store that still had plenty of children’s clothes available. Although the store was nowhere near as luxurious as the shops that had existed before the apocalypse, there was still a decent selection of shirts, pants, dresses, jackets, shoes, and other basic clothing.
Farrah immediately took Xinyi with her while Kai stayed with Xian.
"Come on, Xinyi. Let’s see what fits you."
Xinyi happily followed Farrah between the shelves while Kai looked through the clothes for Xian.
After a few minutes, Kai picked up a dark jacket and held it in front of the boy.
"How about this?"
Xian looked at the jacket carefully before nodding. "I like it."
"Then we’ll take it."
Kai placed it into the shopping basket before looking for something else.
However, before he could pick another piece of clothing, Farrah appeared beside him with several outfits in her arms.
"That’s not enough."
Kai looked at the clothes she was carrying.
"How many outfits do they need?"
Farrah stared at him.
"They’re children, Kai. They need more than one set of clothes."
Kai scratched his cheek awkwardly.
"I’ve never really had to shop for children before."
"I can tell."
Farrah gave him an amused look before returning to Xinyi.
Kai could only smile helplessly and continue following her suggestions.

Over the next hour, the simple shopping trip turned into something much larger. Farrah carefully picked out several outfits for Xinyi, while Kai did the same for Xian. Whenever one of the children found something they liked, they would show it to Kai or Farrah and wait for their approval.
At one point, Xinyi came out wearing a simple dress that Farrah had chosen for her. She looked at herself in the mirror for a moment before turning toward Kai.
"Sir Kai, does this look good?"
Kai looked at her and nodded.
"It looks great."
Xinyi immediately smiled.
"Then I want this one!"
Farrah smiled as well. "See? You have good taste."
Kai glanced at Farrah before smiling teasingly.
"You sound like a mother."
Farrah froze for a moment before turning toward him.
"What did you say?"
"Nothing."
"You definitely said something."
Kai quickly looked away.
"I said the dress looks good."
Farrah narrowed her eyes at him, clearly unconvinced, but eventually she simply shook her head and returned to helping Xinyi.

Meanwhile, Xian had found a few shirts and pants that he liked. Kai bought all of them without hesitation, along with several pairs of shoes, socks, jackets, and other necessities. Farrah also picked out two small backpacks for the siblings, insisting that they would need them once they returned to the shelter.
By the time they finished shopping, Kai was carrying several bags in both hands.
He looked at the amount of clothing they had bought and couldn’t help but laugh.
"Did we really buy this much?"
Farrah looked at him as if the answer were obvious.
"Of course. They’re going to need everything eventually."
Kai nodded.
"Then we’ll just buy more when they need it."
Xinyi hugged her new backpack tightly while Xian stood beside her with a smile.
"Thank you, Sir Kai," Xinyi said happily.
"Thank you," Xian added.
Kai smiled at the two children.
"There’s no need to thank me. You two can just enjoy your new clothes."
Farrah watched the interaction quietly for a moment.

There was something strangely peaceful about the scene. Kai was carrying their bags, the children were excited about their new clothes, and she had spent nearly an hour helping Xinyi choose what she liked.
For a moment, it almost felt as though they were an ordinary family out shopping together.
Farrah couldn’t help but think about it.
"We really look like a family right now."
Kai glanced at her and froze for a moment...
"You think so?"
Farrah immediately realized what she had said and her face became slightly red.
"I didn’t mean it like that!"
Kai smiled.
"Then what did you mean?"
"Just forget it."
Xinyi, who had been listening to them, suddenly looked up at Farrah.
"Are you and Sir Kai married?"
Farrah’s expression instantly changed.
"What?! No!"
Xian also looked toward the two adults with curiosity.
Kai, on the other hand, couldn’t stop himself from laughing.
Xinyi tilted her head innocently.
"Then why do you act like a family?"
Farrah was completely speechless.
Kai looked at her with an amused smile.
"That’s actually a good question."
"Don’t encourage her!"
Farrah lightly hit his arm, causing the two children to burst into laughter.

After finishing their shopping, they finally headed toward the transportation area. Kai had already prepared two hoverboards for the journey back to the Codebreakers Shelter, and there was no need for them to use a vehicle when the hoverboards could easily carry them through the damaged roads outside the city.
Soon, they got the clearance to get out of the city...
Kai stepped onto one of them and looked toward Xian.
"Come here. You’ll ride with me."
Xian immediately walked over.
"I’ve never ridden one before."
"Don’t worry. I’ll carry you. Just hold on tightly."
Kai then picked up the boy and placed him in front of himself before activating the hoverboard.
Farrah did the same with Xinyi, allowing the little girl to sit in front of her while holding onto her.
"Ready?" Kai asked.
Xian nodded excitedly.
"Ready!"
Xinyi also laughed.
"I’m ready too!"
The hoverboards slowly rose from the ground before accelerating forward!
However, before they could completely get out of the city’s vicinity, Kai immediately sensed danger!

chapters.title: Chapter 383: Humans
paragraphs: Kai immediately slowed down the hoverboard.
Farrah noticed his reaction and looked at him with concern.
"What is it?"
Kai didn’t answer immediately. Instead, he looked toward the ruins of several buildings in the distance.
Something was there.
He could sense multiple presences hiding among the damaged structures, and judging from their movements, they were not ordinary enemies...
They could be other Survivors or perhaps a new set of A.I. Soldiers.
Kai thought for a moment before revealing what he had sensed.
"Someone is watching us."
Farrah immediately became cautious.
"Survivors? Maybe the scouts outside the city..."
"I don’t think so."
Kai focused his senses in a certain direction.
A few seconds later, several figures slowly appeared from behind the ruined buildings outside the main city...
Farrah’s expression changed.
"What are those?"
They were humans.
At least, they had once been human.

One of them had four arms and four eyes, with its distorted body covered in scars and patches of hardened flesh. Another had an abnormally long tongue that hung from its mouth and nearly reached its chest.
There were others with strangely shaped bodies.
One had two elbows on each arm, making its limbs look unnaturally long and flexible. Another had a long, stretched neck that allowed its head to rise far above the others.
Their appearances were disturbing enough that Farrah instinctively moved closer to Xinyi.
They were familiar beings... They were closer to the ones protecting the Gene Traders.
Kai, however, didn’t immediately attack.
He continued observing them from a distance.
There were more of them than he had initially noticed.
Dozens of mutated humans were scattered around the ruined buildings, and some were even hiding behind broken vehicles and collapsed walls.
They had apparently been watching Cameron City from the outskirts.
Kai didn’t have any good encounters with such mutated humans before, except for the Superhuman Guild that was under Grim’s lead.

Nonetheless, he couldn’t forget his experience with mutants protecting the Gene Traders... They were extremely aggressive. Once they noticed humans, they would usually rush toward them without hesitation and attempt to kill them.
That was why Kai had initially assumed these mutated humans were preparing to attack.
But something felt different this time... They weren’t approaching.
They weren’t growling...
They weren’t charging toward the city or toward Kai’s group.
They were simply watching, so Kai continued observing them carefully.
"They don’t seem aggressive."
Farrah looked surprised.
"Are you sure?"
Kai nodded.
"At least for now."
One of the mutated humans slowly stepped out from behind a ruined building.
It was a particularly strange-looking creature. It had four eyes arranged unevenly across its face, and two of its arms were much longer than the others.
It stared toward Cameron City.
Kai followed its gaze.
The mutated human didn’t seem interested in them at all.
It was looking at the city.
Several others were doing the same.
Kai remained silent as he watched them.
For some reason, the scene felt strangely pitiful.
These creatures were no longer truly human, yet there was something about the way they stood outside the city that made Kai feel as though they were longing for something.
Perhaps they wanted to enter...
Perhaps they remembered that the place had once been their home.
But they couldn’t.
The humans inside the city would never allow creatures like them to enter.
And if they approached too closely, the city’s defenders would probably attack them immediately.
Kai couldn’t help but feel conflicted.
"They’ve been watching the city for a while," he finally said.
Farrah looked at him.
"You think they used to live there?"
"It’s possible."
Kai didn’t know what had happened to these people or how much of their humanity remained.
Perhaps they were still capable of thinking... perhaps they weren’t.
There was simply no way for him to know.
One of the mutated humans suddenly turned its head toward Kai.
Its four eyes stared directly at him while he remained still.
For several seconds, neither side moved.
Then the mutated human slowly turned away and the others followed.
Instead of approaching them, the mutated humans began moving in another direction, disappearing among the ruins.
Kai watched them leave.
"They’re avoiding us."
Farrah looked at the disappearing figures.
"Maybe they’re smarter than we thought."
"Maybe."
Kai glanced toward Cameron City one last time.
He couldn’t do anything about the mutated humans.
Even if they were still capable of feeling emotions or remembering their former lives, Kai couldn’t simply bring them into the city.
Even if he could, it was too dangerous.
If even one of them suddenly lost control, innocent people could die.
For now, Kai turned the hoverboard toward the road leading away from Cameron City.
"Let’s go."
Farrah nodded.
She adjusted her grip around Xinyi while Kai made sure Xian was holding onto him securely.
The two hoverboards soon accelerated across the ruined road.
Behind them, the mutated humans remained at the edge of the city, quietly watching the place they could no longer return to.
Kai didn’t look back again.
He simply continued forward, carrying Xian toward the Codebreakers Shelter.

They continued along the ruined road, with the two hoverboards moving steadily toward the Codebreakers Shelter. Kai remained alert as they traveled, occasionally scanning the surrounding area for any signs of danger.
After about four hours, however, he suddenly noticed something ahead.
A large caravan was traveling along the same road.

There were nearly ten heavy trucks moving together in a long formation, surrounded by several A.I. Soldiers. Kai immediately recognized some of them as Sentinels, while others were Spyders moving quickly around the convoy and scouting the surrounding area.
Kai slowed down the hoverboard.
Farrah noticed the change and looked ahead.
"That’s quite a large group."
Kai nodded.
"Yes."
Something about the caravan bothered him.
The A.I. army was clearly protecting the trucks, but Kai couldn’t understand why they were using ordinary vehicles.
The machine civilization possessed anti-gravity ships and various flying aircraft. They had already demonstrated their ability to move large numbers of machines through the air.
So why were they transporting something with trucks?
It was suspicious.
Kai narrowed his eyes as he observed the convoy from a distance.
"Chamber, can you scan those trucks?"
There was a brief pause before his A.I. assistant responded.
[ Scanning the caravan. ]
Kai waited patiently.
Then Chamber’s voice suddenly became more serious.
[ Analysis complete. ]
[ Biological lifeforms detected inside the trucks. ]
Kai’s expression changed.
"Humans?"
[ Confirmed. The trucks contain multiple human life signs. ]
Farrah immediately looked at him.
"Humans?"
Kai nodded slowly.
His bad feeling became even stronger.

chapters.title: Chapter 384: Targeted
paragraphs: Kai didn’t immediately move as he saw it...
His eyes remained fixed on the convoy in the distance as the heavy trucks continued along the road, surrounded by dozens of A.I. Soldiers.
He already knew what was happening.

The machine civilization had been capturing humans for a long time. Sometimes, they used them as living shields during battles, forcing human survivors to hesitate before firing their weapons. Other times, the captured humans were taken away for experiments.
And the experiments had produced those mutants, aside from the side effects of Gene Enhancement Serums.
Kai couldn’t help but think about the strange creatures they had encountered earlier.
Four arms... Four eyes... Distorted bodies... and abnormally long limbs.
Those weren’t simply monsters that had appeared after the apocalypse.
Without a doubt, they had been normal humans once.
They were probably failed experiments too...
After all, the machine civilization had been searching for something through those experiments.
The Divine Gene.
For some reason, the Anima Civilization was also searching for the same mysterious gene that humanity was trying to discover.
The difference was that humans were searching for it inside the VR World known as Perfect World, a place where the A.I.s couldn’t enter.
The machines had no such limitation here.
They could experiment directly on human bodies...
Kai’s expression became darker.
He looked at the convoy again.
There were too many A.I. Soldiers.
Several Sentinels surrounded the trucks, while numerous Spyders moved through the surrounding ruins. There were also several larger combat machines mixed into the formation.
Kai quickly estimated their strength.
Then he glanced toward his own group.
Only two people here could actually fight.
Himself and Farrah.
Xian and Xinyi were with them, but they obviously couldn’t participate in a battle like this.
Kai sighed as he considered his options.
Even if he used all his strength, protecting the children while fighting such a large group of machines would be extremely difficult.
And the humans inside those trucks made things even worse.
If the machines were using them as shields, Kai couldn’t simply unleash powerful attacks against the convoy.
One mistake could kill the very people he was trying to save.
Kai slowly clenched his fist.
He didn’t like this feeling... Not at all.
For a moment, he considered simply leaving.
It was painful to admit, but there was nothing he could realistically do with only himself and Farrah.
If he attacked, they might die.
If he tried to rescue the prisoners, the machines could use them as hostages.
And if the convoy reached its destination, Kai didn’t even know where the prisoners would be taken.
He remained silent for several seconds.
Farrah noticed his expression.
"Kai?"
Kai didn’t answer as he continued staring at the convoy.
He hated this... He had the strength to destroy countless machines, yet there were still situations where he couldn’t save everyone.
Just as Kai was about to turn around, he suddenly sensed something approaching from behind.
His expression changed.
A powerful presence was moving rapidly toward them.
Kai immediately turned around and Farrah also looked in the same direction.
Soon, a humanoid figure emerged from the ruins.
It was nearly seven feet tall, with a heavily reinforced mechanical body and a familiar silver-colored frame.
Kai’s eyes widened.
"Atom?"
The S-Grade Sentinel stopped several meters away from them.
Its mechanical eyes briefly scanned Kai, Farrah, Xian, and Xinyi.
Then it spoke in its usual mechanical voice.
[ Target group located. ]
Kai stared at it in disbelief. This S-Grade Sentinel really talks now... It seemed that it cad i[
"What are you doing here?"
Atom didn’t answer immediately.
Instead, it continued scanning the surrounding area.
[ Escort mission confirmed. ]
Kai’s eyebrows rose.
"Escort mission?"
Atom nodded.
[ Confirmed. ]
Kai was genuinely confused.
He hadn’t summoned Atom.
More importantly, he hadn’t given it any orders.
The S-Grade Sentinel was one of the strongest defensive units at the Codebreakers Shelter. Sending it away from the shelter was not something Kai would normally do without a good reason.
Someone must have ordered it.
Kai immediately thought of the people managing the shelter.
Claire... Althea... or perhaps Sera.
One of them must have realized that Kai and the others were traveling back from Cameron City and decided to send Atom to escort them.
Kai couldn’t help but feel slightly worried.
Sending an S-Grade Sentinel this far away meant the shelter had lost one of its strongest combat units, even if only temporarily.
Still, Kai wasn’t going to complain.
Because the situation in front of him had just changed completely.
He looked back toward the convoy... Then he looked at Atom.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"Well..."
Kai reached toward his waist.
He pulled out the Plasma Pistol he had obtained from the Legendary Weapon Gift Pack.
The compact weapon immediately attracted Farrah’s attention.
She had seen Kai receive several powerful items recently, but she hadn’t actually seen him use this one yet.
Kai checked the weapon for a moment before pointing it toward the distant convoy.
The integrated energy cell hummed softly.
He then reached toward his other side and drew the Monomolecular Combat Blade.
The blade looked surprisingly simple.
There was no complicated design or excessive decoration.
Yet Kai knew exactly how dangerous it was.
Its cutting edge had been refined to an extremely thin molecular scale, allowing it to slice through conventional metals and armor with astonishing ease.
Kai carefully held the handle.
He wasn’t going to test the edge with his fingers.
He had no intention of accidentally cutting himself apart with his own weapon.
Farrah glanced at the two weapons.
"You got new equipment?"
"From the Legendary Gift Pack."
"W-what? There’s another gift pack? Amazing..."
Kai looked at the plasma pistol again.
"I haven’t had a chance to properly test them yet."
He slowly raised the weapon.
The distant machines were still protecting the trucks.
There were far too many enemies for Kai and Farrah alone, but now they had Atom.
And that changed everything.
An S-Grade Sentinel was not just another combat machine.
Atom was a powerful humanoid unit capable of fighting against extremely dangerous enemies while also providing protection.
Kai looked at the convoy once more...
Seeing their strength, his previous hesitation had disappeared.
He still didn’t know how many humans were inside those trucks and he certainly didn’t know whether he could save everyone.
But at least now, he had a chance.
Kai smiled slightly.
"Chamber."
[ Yes? ]
"Keep scanning the convoy."
[ Understood. ]
"Find out which truck contains the largest number of prisoners."
[ Analyzing. ]
Kai tightened his grip around the plasma pistol.
"Then we’ll rescue them."
Farrah immediately stepped forward.
"I’m ready."
Atom’s mechanical body shifted as its combat systems activated.
[ Combat support ready. ]
Kai looked at the enormous Sentinel beside him.
"Atom... Let’s see what these machines are transporting."

chapters.title: Chapter 385: The Ambush
paragraphs: The convoy continued moving through the uneven road, completely unaware that its route would soon become a battlefield.

Kai remained behind the broken concrete barrier, watching the machines through the scope of his rifle. The closer the convoy came, the more clearly he could see its formation. Several Sentinels surrounded the trucks while dozens of Spyders moved through the nearby ruins, constantly scanning the area. The trucks themselves were heavily reinforced, their metal bodies covered in additional plating.
Whatever was inside them, the machines clearly considered it valuable.
"Chamber," Kai said quietly. "Give me the prisoner count."
[ Scanning. ]
A few seconds later, the answer appeared.
[ Thirty-seven human life signatures detected. ]
Kai’s expression immediately became serious.
Thirty-seven.
At least thirty-seven people were being transported by the machines.
"How is their condition? It’s not too late to save them right?"
[ I can’t tell. However, several subjects are suffering from severe biological deterioration. Multiple unstable mutations have been detected.]
Kai’s grip tightened around his rifle.
So they really were transporting experimental subjects.
He glanced toward Farrah, who was already crouching beside Xian and Xinyi.
"Farrah."
She looked toward him.
"I’ll handle the machines. Keep the children behind you and don’t let anything get close."
Farrah nodded without hesitation.
"I understand."
Kai turned back toward the convoy.
He took one final look at Atom.
The S-Grade Sentinel was standing several meters away, completely motionless as it waited for his command. Its mechanical eyes remained fixed on the approaching machines.
Kai thought for a moment before making a plan.
He wasn’t going to fight beside Atom at close range.
Atom was too powerful and too fast. Its entire combat system had been designed around close-quarters warfare, and Kai knew that trying to move alongside it would only interfere with its movements.
Instead, he would support it from a distance.
"Atom."
The Sentinel’s head turned toward him.
"Go."
Atom immediately disappeared from its position.

The ground beneath its feet cracked as the machine accelerated forward. It crossed the distance between them and the convoy in only a few seconds, moving so quickly that several of the machines didn’t even have time to react.
The first Sentinel raised its weapon.
However, Atom reached it before it could fire.
Boom!
Its fist slammed into the machine’s chest with enough force to send it flying through the air.
Thud... Thud...
The Sentinel crashed into the ruins beside the road, tearing through a concrete wall before finally coming to a stop.
The convoy was immediately put into chaos...
Warning signals flashed across the machines.
The Spyders spread out while the remaining Sentinels opened fire.
Hundreds of rounds tore through the ruins.
Kai immediately lowered himself behind the concrete barrier as the first wave of machines opened fire.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Bullets tore through the abandoned buildings around him, sending fragments of concrete and rusted metal flying through the air.
The sound of gunfire was deafening, but Kai remained surprisingly calm.
He reached toward his inventory.
A moment later, the Electromagnetic Railgun from the Legendary Gift Pack appeared in his hands.
The weapon was considerably larger than an ordinary rifle, its dark metallic frame surrounded by several electromagnetic components that hummed softly as its internal energy system came online.
It was designed for one purpose... overwhelming penetration.
Kai had received the weapon just recently, but he had barely found an opportunity to use it.
This seemed like the perfect test.
"Chamber, identify priority targets."
[ Scanning battlefield. ]
The A.I. Assistant immediately began marking targets within Kai’s field of vision.
Several Sentinels appeared first.
Then the heavier combat machines.
"Give me the most heavily armored target."
[ Target acquired. ]
A large modified Sentinel had just moved into position behind the convoy. Its body was covered in thick armor plating, and the weapon mounted on its shoulder was already charging.
Kai steadied the Railgun against the concrete barrier.
The weapon then began gathering energy.
Soon, a low electromagnetic hum filled the air as the machine suddenly turned toward him.
"Eat this..."
Kai pulled the trigger.
Click!
There was no ordinary gunshot.
Instead, the Railgun released a thunderous electromagnetic discharge.
BOOOOM!
The projectile crossed the battlefield almost instantaneously.
It punched straight through the combat machine’s chest armor, continued through its internal frame, and exited from the opposite side before the machine even had time to react.
The massive machine froze.
Then it collapsed.
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Armored Sentinel (A) ]
[ Experience Points distributed among all participants. ]
[ +500 Experience Points ]
Kai stared for a moment.
"...That’s powerful."
He had known the weapon was Legendary-grade, but actually seeing its penetration capability was something else entirely.
He immediately shifted his aim.
Another Sentinel was attempting to move around Atom’s flank.
Kai aimed and fired.
Boom!
The projectile struck its weapon arm and completely tore through the limb.
Before the Sentinel could recover, Atom appeared beside it and drove a powerful punch into its chest.
The machine was sent flying across the road.
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Armored Sentinel (A) ]
Kai smiled faintly.
He understood the battlefield now...
He didn’t need to fight alongside Atom. He just needed to control everything around it.

Whenever a machine tried to attack Atom from a blind spot, Kai would eliminate it. Whenever one attempted to approach the trucks, he would stop it. And if something particularly heavily armored appeared, the Railgun would deal with it.
Atom could focus entirely on destroying whatever stood directly in front of it.
The combination was devastating.
Another group of Spyders rushed toward Atom.
Kai fired again.
The electromagnetic projectile passed through the first machine and continued into the second, destroying both.
Atom didn’t even slow down.
It grabbed another Sentinel by the arm and swung it into an abandoned building. The machine crashed through the wall before Atom charged after it.
Bam!
Meanwhile, several Spyders attempted to circle around the battlefield.
Kai switched targets and, needless to say, the machines fell one after another.
"Whoa... This railgun is a bit too good." Kai muttered.
Still, he could tell that if not for his level and other bonus stats, it would be impossible for him to use his railgun several times.
If someone other than him used this weapon, they might already be injured.
Well, it wasn’t really that surprising considering the firepower it had...
"I really needed more Talent Upgrade Crystals..."

The S-Grade Sentinel was standing several meters away, completely motionless as it waited for his command.
Its mechanical eyes remained fixed on the approaching machines.
Kai thought for a moment before making a plan.
He wasn’t going to fight beside Atom at close range.
Atom was too powerful and too fast.
Its entire combat system had been designed around close-quarters warfare, and Kai knew that trying to move alongside it would only interfere with its movements.
Instead, he would support it from a distance.
"Atom."
The Sentinel’s head turned toward him.
"Go."
Atom immediately disappeared from its position.
The ground beneath its feet cracked as the machine accelerated forward.
It crossed the distance between them and the convoy in only a few seconds, moving so quickly that several of the machines didn’t even have time to react.
The first Sentinel raised its weapon.
However, Atom reached it before it could fire.
Boom!
Its fist slammed into the machine’s chest with enough force to send it flying through the air.
Thud...
Thud...
The Sentinel crashed into the ruins beside the road, tearing through a concrete wall before finally coming to a stop.
The convoy was immediately put into chaos...
Warning signals flashed across the machines.
The Spyders spread out while the remaining Sentinels opened fire.
Hundreds of rounds tore through the ruins.
Kai immediately lowered himself behind the concrete barrier as the first wave of machines opened fire.
Bang!
Bang!
Bang!
Bullets tore through the abandoned buildings around him, sending fragments of concrete and rusted metal flying through the air.
The sound of gunfire was deafening, but Kai remained surprisingly calm.
He reached toward his inventory.
A moment later, the Electromagnetic Railgun from the Legendary Gift Pack appeared in his hands.
The weapon was considerably larger than an ordinary rifle, its dark metallic frame surrounded by several electromagnetic components that hummed softly as its internal energy system came online.
It was designed for one purpose... overwhelming penetration.
Kai had received the weapon just recently, but he had barely found an opportunity to use it.
This seemed like the perfect test.
"Chamber, identify priority targets."
[ Scanning battlefield. ]
The A.I.
Assistant immediately began marking targets within Kai’s field of vision.
Several Sentinels appeared first.
Then the heavier combat machines.
"Give me the most heavily armored target."
[ Target acquired. ]
A large modified Sentinel had just moved into position behind the convoy.
Its body was covered in thick armor plating, and the weapon mounted on its shoulder was already charging.
Kai steadied the Railgun against the concrete barrier.
The weapon then began gathering energy.
Soon, a low electromagnetic hum filled the air as the machine suddenly turned toward him.
"Eat this..."
Kai pulled the trigger.
Click!
There was no ordinary gunshot.
Instead, the Railgun released a thunderous electromagnetic discharge.
BOOOOM!
The projectile crossed the battlefield almost instantaneously.
It punched straight through the combat machine’s chest armor, continued through its internal frame, and exited from the opposite side before the machine even had time to react.
The massive machine froze.
Then it collapsed.
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Armored Sentinel (A) ]
[ Experience Points distributed among all participants. ]
[ +500 Experience Points ]
Kai stared for a moment.
"...That’s powerful."
He had known the weapon was Legendary-grade, but actually seeing its penetration capability was something else entirely.
He immediately shifted his aim.
Another Sentinel was attempting to move around Atom’s flank.
Kai aimed and fired.
Boom!
The projectile struck its weapon arm and completely tore through the limb.
Before the Sentinel could recover, Atom appeared beside it and drove a powerful punch into its chest.
The machine was sent flying across the road.
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Armored Sentinel (A) ]
Kai smiled faintly.
He understood the battlefield now...
He didn’t need to fight alongside Atom.
He just needed to control everything around it.
Whenever a machine tried to attack Atom from a blind spot, Kai would eliminate it.
Whenever one attempted to approach the trucks, he would stop it.
And if something particularly heavily armored appeared, the Railgun would deal with it.
Atom could focus entirely on destroying whatever stood directly in front of it.
The combination was devastating.
Another group of Spyders rushed toward Atom.
Kai fired again.
The electromagnetic projectile passed through the first machine and continued into the second, destroying both.
Atom didn’t even slow down.
It grabbed another Sentinel by the arm and swung it into an abandoned building.
The machine crashed through the wall before Atom charged after it.
Bam!
Meanwhile, several Spyders attempted to circle around the battlefield.
Kai switched targets and, needless to say, the machines fell one after another.
"Whoa...
This railgun is a bit too good." Kai muttered.
Still, he could tell that if not for his level and other bonus stats, it would be impossible for him to use his railgun several times.
If someone other than him used this weapon, they might already be injured.
Well, it wasn’t really that surprising considering the firepower it had...
"I really needed more Talent Upgrade Crystals..."

chapters.title: Chapter 386: The Truck
paragraphs: Kai had some with him, but he needed multiple of them since he had already used a few of them before...

In any case, he wasn’t wasting ammunition because the Railgun didn’t use conventional ammunition in the first place. Its internal energy system allowed it to repeatedly launch projectiles, although Kai could already see the energy reserve decreasing with every shot.
That meant he couldn’t simply fire endlessly.
He would have to make every shot count.
"Chamber, can you monitor the Railgun’s energy for me?"
[ Understood. Current energy reserve: 66%.]
"That’s plenty."
Kai looked toward the battlefield again.
Farrah was still protecting Xian and Xinyi.
Several Spyders had noticed the children and were attempting to reach them.
Farrah immediately positioned herself between the machines and the children.
She intercepted the first Spyder wielding an energy blade before it could attack, striking it hard enough to send its mechanical body crashing against an abandoned vehicle.
Boom!
"I can take care of them, Kai! Just help Atom... He might get overwhelmed."
Kai heard this, but he didn’t listen. He could monitor Atom’s movement anyway.
Just like that, he watched as another came from the side of Farrah...
Of course, she easily turned and destroyed it with her. She was a Spirit Knight after all!
However, a third machine attempted to circle around her, and it was too fast!
This time, Kai raised the Railgun, and without hesitation, he fired!
Boom!
The machine disappeared beneath the weapon’s next electromagnetic discharge.
Farrah would’ve probably survived without his help if she used her own Gene Skills or using her hidden Gene Weapon, but she still appreciated the assistance and glanced toward him.
"Thanks!"
Kai nodded.
"Keep them behind you."
"I will."
The battle continued around them.
The machines were becoming increasingly desperate.
Some attempted to overwhelm Atom with numbers. Others tried to reach the trucks. A few even abandoned their weapons and attempted to retreat with the convoy.
Kai didn’t let them.
The Railgun fired again and again, each shot tearing through armor that would have taken ordinary weapons dozens of rounds to penetrate.
At one point, three Sentinels advanced together.
"Easy..."
Kai waited until they aligned... Then he fired.
The projectile pierced through the first Sentinel’s torso, continued through the second, and struck the third in its shoulder.
The first two collapsed immediately and the third was already heavily damaged.
"Nice..."
Atom reached it a moment later.
Its mechanical hand seized the damaged Sentinel by the neck.
The machine struggled desperately, but Atom simply took its core from its chest!
Thud!
Seeing this, Kai knew what Atom wanted to do...
He then slowly lowered the Railgun as he knew that this was already done...
"Yeah... I definitely like this weapon." He muttered as he kissed the railgun.
Then something caught his attention.
One of the remaining Sentinels wasn’t attacking Atom.
Instead, it had broken away from the battle and was heading toward the trucks.
Kai immediately recognized what it was doing.
"Chamber."
[ Yes? ]
"Monitor that Sentinel."
The machine was highlighted in his vision.
It was moving toward the rear of the convoy.
"It’s going for the prisoners." He raised the Railgun.
The weapon hummed as energy gathered, but Kai hesitated.
The truck was directly behind the Sentinel.
A Railgun shot could easily penetrate the machine and continue into the vehicle.
He couldn’t risk it.
With that in mind, Kai switched weapons.
The Railgun disappeared from his hands and was replaced by the Plasma Pistol.
He aimed carefully and soon, the weapon released a concentrated bolt of superheated plasma.
ZAP!
The shot struck the Sentinel’s knee joint.
Its leg melted beneath the intense heat and, just like that, the machine crashed onto the road.
Before it could recover, Atom arrived.
The massive S-Grade Sentinel grabbed the damaged machine and lifted it from the ground.
With a single motion, Atom took its mechanical core once again as it disappeared from its hands!
Without a doubt, Atom was absorbing it once again...
Still, Kai finally relaxed.
The battlefield had fallen silent as the last remaining machines had been destroyed.
Scattered across the highway were the wrecks of Sentinels, Spyders, and larger combat machines. Smoke rose from the ruined convoy while small sparks continued to flicker across the damaged metal.
Kai looked at Atom.
The S-Grade Sentinel was still standing, and there wasn’t even a significant mark on its armor.
Kai couldn’t help but shake his head.
"Having you around really makes things easier."
Atom simply turned toward the convoy and Kai chuckled before he followed.
They had won the battle.
But the real reason they had fought was still waiting inside those trucks.
Atom approached the nearest vehicle while Kai examined the tightly shut doors.
There was a complicated locking mechanism built into the side.
Before Kai could even attempt to figure it out, Atom reached forward.
Its mechanical fingers pierced directly into the locking system.
Metal twisted... and soon, the lock shattered.
Atom pulled the door open.
Clank! Clank!
As soon as he saw what was inside, Kai’s expression immediately darkened.
There were humans inside... Dozens of them.
Men and women were packed tightly together, many of them too weak to even stand. Several were unconscious, while others stared at Kai with hollow, frightened eyes.
Some had scars covering their bodies, while others had obvious physical abnormalities.
Kai’s gaze lingered on one man whose arms were unnaturally long.
He remembered the mutants they had encountered earlier.
Four arms... Four eyes... Distorted bodies... Abnormally long limbs.
Those creatures hadn’t simply appeared because of the apocalypse.
They had once been human.
And now Kai was looking at the people who had been subjected to the same experiments before they became monsters.
One of the prisoners slowly raised his head.
"Please..."
His voice trembled... and Kai could feel something in his chest.
"Don’t let them take us back."
Kai took a deep breath as he remained silent for a moment.
Then he stepped forward.
"We’re not taking you anywhere."
He looked around the truck.
"We’re getting you out."
The prisoners stared at him, and for several seconds, nobody moved.
Then, one woman began crying.
Just like that, another survivor lowered his head and covered his face with both hands.
Farrah immediately stepped forward and began helping the weakest prisoners out of the truck.
"Careful. Take your time."
Xian and Xinyi stayed close behind her.
Kai turned toward the remaining vehicles.
There were still more trucks.
"Atom."
The S-Grade Sentinel turned toward him.
"Open all of them."

chapters.title: Chapter 388: Saved
paragraphs: Wilson remained where he was, staring at Farrah’s outstretched hand.

For so long, he had been treated as something less than human that he had almost forgotten what it felt like to be treated normally. The simple kindness in her voice was almost harder for him to accept than the experiments he had endured.
He eventually reached out and grabbed her hand.
Farrah pulled him out of the truck.
The moment his feet touched the ground, Wilson instinctively lowered his head. He was still embarrassed by his appearance, and he didn’t want to see the reactions of the people around him.
However, nobody laughed.
Nobody screamed.
Nobody even moved away from him.
Farrah simply released his hand and turned toward the other prisoners.
"Come out slowly. There’s no need to rush."
The survivors began climbing out of the trucks one after another.

There were far more than Wilson had expected. Some were so weak that they needed help just to stand, while others could barely walk after spending so long inside the cramped vehicles. Their bodies had been changed in different ways, and some looked just as unnatural as Wilson did.
Yet despite their appearances, there was one thing they all had in common.
They were starving.
At first, Kai thought they might need medical attention before anything else, but the moment one of the survivors was given a bottle of water, he emptied it almost instantly.
Another survivor saw the bottle and immediately asked for one as well.
Then another.
It didn’t take long for Kai to understand just how hungry and thirsty they were.
"When was the last time you were properly fed?" he asked.
The survivors exchanged uncertain looks.
Some couldn’t remember.
Others said it had been days.
A few admitted that they had been given only enough food to prevent them from dying.
Kai frowned.
He didn’t ask any more questions.
There was no point.
He opened his inventory and began taking out Gift Packs.
Several Enhanced Food Gift Packs appeared on the ground.
The moment Kai opened them, vacuum-sealed rations, canned goods, dried fruits and nuts, instant soup packs, coffee sachets, and portable cooking stoves appeared among the supplies.
The survivors stared at the food.
"You can have them all..."
For a moment, nobody moved.
Then one of them slowly reached for a ration.
He tore open the package and took a bite!
His expression changed immediately and he began eating faster.
That seemed to break the hesitation among the others.
Soon, the survivors were surrounding the supplies and eating whatever they could get their hands on.
Kai had expected them to be hungry, but he hadn’t expected their appetite to be this enormous.
One ration disappeared... Then another.
Several survivors finished entire cans of food within minutes and immediately reached for more.
Wilson was no different.

He had spent so long eating only enough to keep his altered body alive that he had forgotten what real hunger felt like. Now that food was actually available, his body seemed to demand everything it could get.
He finished one ration and reached for another.
Then another.
Even after eating several portions, he still felt hungry.
Wilson eventually looked down at the empty packages around him and realized how much he had eaten.
His face reddened.
"I’m sorry."
Farrah, who was helping another survivor open a can, looked at him in confusion.
"For what?"
"I’ve eaten too much."
He knew that finding food at this time wasn’t easy.
Still, Farrah just glanced at the enormous pile of supplies beside them before looking back at him.
"There’s plenty. You don’t need to worry about that."
Wilson hesitated before slowly reaching for another ration.
Kai watched the survivors for a moment as he continued opening more Gift Packs.

Their appetite should have been concerning if they were ordinary humans. The amount of food they were consuming would have left most people feeling sick, but their bodies had been changed by years of genetic experimentation.
Their metabolism had been altered and their organs had been modified.
Even their ability to process energy was no longer comparable to that of an ordinary human.
The machines had changed them so extensively that their bodies could handle enormous amounts of food without any apparent problems.
If anything, the food seemed to be helping them recover.
Their faces gradually gained color, and some of those who had barely been able to stand earlier were already moving around more easily.
Kai didn’t find it difficult to understand why.
Their bodies had been kept alive through countless experiments, and now that they finally had access to enough food, they could actually begin recovering.
He opened several Enhanced Water Gift Packs next.
Water gallons, filled bottles, collapsible buckets, purification tablets, hydration packs, insulated canteens, and advanced water filters appeared among the supplies.
The survivors immediately began drinking again.
This time, Farrah made sure they didn’t drink too quickly.
"Slow down. There’s enough for everyone."
The survivors listened, although several of them still kept glancing toward the remaining water as if afraid that it might disappear.
Kai couldn’t blame them.
After being deprived of food and water for so long, it was probably difficult for them to believe that they no longer had to fight for every mouthful.
Once everyone had eaten and drunk enough, Kai opened several Superior Survival Tools Gift Packs.
He had specifically chosen the Superior Grade packs because they contained better survival equipment, including proper survival clothing.
The packs produced multi-tools, digging equipment, fire-starting kits, portable fishing equipment, navigation tools, communication radios, emergency repair kits, and even a portable drone scout.
But the clothing was the most important thing here...
The survivors had spent years wearing whatever the machines gave them, and some of their clothes were barely recognizable as clothing anymore.
Kai distributed the new survival clothing sets among them.
"Take these."
The survivors accepted them carefully.
Some immediately began changing.
Others simply held the clothes against their bodies, staring at them as if they couldn’t believe they were actually being given something new.
Wilson was one of the latter.
He looked down at the clean clothing in his hands.
A simple set of survival clothes shouldn’t have meant much.
Yet to him, it was almost overwhelming.
He couldn’t remember the last time someone had given him something simply because they wanted him to be comfortable!
"T-thank you for saving me... I will do anything to pay this debt!"
