chapters.title: Chapter 389: Savior Kai
paragraphs: Eventually, Wilson found a place away from the others and changed.
He also used one of the buckets from Kai’s Water Gift Packs to wash himself.
The first touch of clean water against his skin made him close his eyes.
He washed slowly, allowing the dirt and dried blood that had accumulated over years to finally disappear.
When he finished, he changed into the new clothes and looked down at himself.
He still looked nothing like the man he had once been...
His arms remained unnaturally long, and his body was covered in scars.
Mechanical components were still embedded in his flesh, and there were mutations he knew would never disappear.
But at least he was clean...
After that, Wilson returned to the others.
Nobody treated him differently.
Farrah was still helping the weaker survivors, while Kai continued opening more Gift Packs whenever the supplies began to run low.
There was no shortage.
Soon, the other rescued people also realized that Kai seemed to be capable of producing unlimited resources!
’How is he doing that? Is he a god of supplies?’
It was very weird... and it was difficult to explain...
Everything they needed to survive was appearing in front of them.
Just like that, Wilson realized that he was no longer waiting for the next experiment... He wasn’t waiting for another machine to approach him...
He wasn’t waiting for pain anymore!
He was simply sitting beside other survivors, eating food and wearing clean clothes beneath the open sky.
Wilson then lowered his head and quietly took another bite of food.
It tasted ordinary.
Yet to him, it was the best meal he had eaten in his entire life.
Among the rescued survivors was a young woman named Hanabi.
Unlike most of the others, she remained inside the truck even after everyone else had begun getting out.
Well, she couldn’t...
Hanabi had no legs.
Both of them had been removed during one of the experiments, and for a long time, she had relied on a special mechanical device that allowed her to move around.
It wasn’t a perfect replacement, but at least it allowed her to stand and walk.
However, when the machines transported them to another facility, the device had been taken away.
Hanabi had no idea why...
Perhaps they had wanted to use it for another prisoner... Perhaps it had simply been damaged and discarded.
She never found out.
Since then, she had been forced to crawl whenever she needed to move.
Now that the machines were gone, Hanabi looked down at her missing legs and quietly sighed.
She had no idea where she could find another device.
Even before the apocalypse, advanced prosthetics were expensive... Furthermore, most people like him,
Now, with civilization collapsing and machines controlling most of the advanced technology, finding one was practically impossible.
She lowered her head as perhaps she would simply have to accept it.
At least she was alive.
That was already more than she had expected.
"Hanabi?"
She looked up.
Kai was standing in front of her.
He had noticed that she hadn’t left the truck.
"I heard you lost your legs."
Hanabi nodded. She wasn’t surprised that he knew her name since she was quite well known in the group... After all, she was the only one who had no legs.
"The machines gave me a device before, but they took it away during transportation." She replied.
"...I don’t know where it is now."
There was no anger in her voice... Only resignation.
"I suppose I’ll just have to find another one someday."
Kai stared at her for a moment... Then he opened his inventory.
A strange metallic capsule appeared in his hands.
Hanabi looked at it curiously.
"What is that?"
"A Limb Reconstruction Capsule."
Kai placed it in front of her.

[ Limb Reconstruction Capsule: A highly advanced medical device capable of completely reconstructing a missing limb. Once activated, the capsule stimulates accelerated tissue regeneration, rebuilding bones, muscles, nerves, blood vessels, and skin until the missing limb is fully restored.
The reconstructed limb will initially be weak and may cause significant pain as the body adapts to it. The recovery period varies depending on the user’s physique and overall condition. ]
"It can regrow missing limbs."
Hanabi froze as she heard this. She had never heard of such a technology.
She stared at the capsule.
Then she looked at Kai.
"Regrow... my legs?"
"Yes."
For several seconds, Hanabi couldn’t respond.
She had heard of advanced medical technology before the apocalypse, but even then, completely regrowing a missing limb was something she had never personally seen.
After everything the machines had done to her, she had stopped believing that she would ever walk again.
"Are you serious?"
Kai nodded.
"I wouldn’t give it to you if it didn’t work."
Hanabi’s hands began trembling.
She reached out and touched the capsule as if she were afraid it might disappear.
"How much does it cost?"
"Don’t worry about that."
Kai shook his head.
"You need it more than I do. Well, I would be happy if you go work in my shelter from now on..."
Hanabi’s eyes slowly turned red.
She had spent years being treated as a test subject.
Whenever the machines gave her something, it was because they wanted something from her in return.
This was different...
Someone was simply giving her the chance to walk again!
Her voice broke.
Hanabi lowered her head and wiped her eyes.
"Thank you."
Kai simply nodded.
"You’ll probably experience some pain and weakness while your body adapts to the new limbs, so don’t push yourself too hard."
Hanabi nodded repeatedly.
"I understand."
She held the capsule tightly against her chest.
For the first time in years, Hanabi allowed herself to imagine something she had long since given up on...
Walking... Standing on her own or feeling the ground beneath her feet.
It was such a simple thing!
Yet to her, it felt like a miracle.
Still, before Kai left, he took out a crystal and asked her to touch...
"You just need to hold this for a few seconds..."
Kai said as he pulled out a Status Crystal...

chapters.title: Chapter 390: Recruitment
paragraphs: Kai held the Status Crystal toward Hanabi.
"You just need to hold this for a few seconds."
Hanabi looked at the strange crystal in his hand before carefully taking it.
The moment her fingers wrapped around it, the crystal began glowing.
A translucent screen appeared in front of her.
[ Name: Hanabi ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 6 ]
[ Health: 45 / 95 ]
[ Spirit: 85 / 85 ]
[ Physique Rating: D ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Adaptive Regeneration Lv1, Pain Resistance Lv2 ]
[ Adaptive Regeneration Lv1: Slightly accelerates the recovery of damaged tissues and improves the body’s ability to adapt to biological changes. ]
[ Pain Resistance Lv2: Significantly reduces the effects of physical pain and improves resistance to prolonged suffering. ]
[ Status: Bilateral Lower-Limb Loss. Extensive Genetic Modification. Body has undergone significant biological adaptation due to prolonged experimentation. ]
Hanabi stared at the information in disbelief.
"Level 6..."
She had never known.
She had never even realized that her body had become this strong despite everything that had been done to her.
Kai’s expression also changed slightly.
A Physique Rating of D wasn’t particularly high compared to the strongest Foreign Survivors, but for a native Survivor who had spent years being experimented on, it was impressive.
More importantly, her body had developed skills that were directly related to her experiences.
Adaptive Regeneration...
Pain Resistance...
She wasn’t useless. Not even close.
In fact, with proper resources, Hanabi’s potential might be considerably higher than her current strength suggested.
The Status Crystal’s light faded.
Hanabi slowly lowered it.
"I... didn’t know I had any of this."
"Most Survivors don’t."
Kai smiled.
"But now you know."
Hanabi looked at him before nodding. Just like that, Kai turned toward Wilson who was watching them outside the truck...
"You’re next."
Wilson hesitated before accepting the crystal.
The moment it activated, his expression changed.
[ Name: Wilson ]
[ Title: Mutated Survivor ]
[ Level: 8 ]
[ Spirit: 60 / 60 ]
[ Physique Rating: C- ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Enhanced Metabolism Lv2, Mutagenic Adaptation Lv2, Pain Resistance Lv3 ]
Similar to Hanabi, he only possessed Passive Skills! Still, these weren’t just skills but Genetic Abilities that could greatly improve in due time...
In any case, with the time remaining, Kai checked the skills as well.
[ Enhanced Metabolism Lv2: Greatly increases the body’s ability to process nutrients and convert consumed food into usable energy. ]
[ Mutagenic Adaptation Lv2: Allows the body to adapt to extensive genetic alterations, increasing tolerance toward biological mutations and foreign substances. ]
[ Pain Resistance Lv3: Greatly reduces physical pain and improves resistance to prolonged injuries and biological stress. ]
[ Status: Extensive Genetic Modification. Multiple Organ Replacements. Mechanical Implants. Severe Physical Mutation. ]
Wilson stared at his status for several seconds.
"A C- Physique..."
He almost laughed.
After everything that had happened to him, he had never imagined that his body could actually be considered strong.
Kai, however, was more interested in the abilities.
"Interesting..."
The machines had experimented on Wilson so extensively that his body had developed abilities specifically suited to surviving their modifications.
He had also reached Level 8.
That was already considerably higher than most ordinary Survivors.
Kai looked toward the other rescued prisoners.
"Let me check everyone else."
One after another, the survivors stepped forward.
Kai used the Status Crystal repeatedly.
Some had lower levels...
Others had strange passive skills.

One woman possessed a skill that increased resistance to extreme temperatures. Another had developed enhanced sensory perception after years of exposure to experimental energy. A man with heavily modified muscles possessed an unusually high Physique Rating despite his damaged body.
Some had completely useless abilities.
Others had skills that Kai immediately recognized as valuable.
But there was one thing they all had in common.
None of them were ordinary.
Their bodies had been pushed beyond their natural limits through years of cruel experimentation.
The machines had failed to create what they wanted.
Yet in the process, they had accidentally created Survivors with unusual abilities and powerful adaptive traits.
Then, there was another interesting Survivor among the crowd.
[ Name: Kennedy ]
[ Title: Mutated Survivor ]
[ Level: 9 ]
[ Spirit: 90 / 90 ]
[ Physique Rating: C- ]
[ Active Skills: Overdrive Mutation Lv2 ]
[ Passive Skills: Enhanced Muscle Density Lv2, Rapid Recovery Lv1 ]

[ Overdrive Mutation Lv2: Temporarily stimulates the user’s mutated tissues, greatly increasing physical strength, movement speed, and reaction speed. The user’s mutations become more pronounced while the skill is active, but the increased strain can cause temporary weakness after the effect ends.
Spirit Cost: 30
Duration: 60 seconds
Cooldown: 120 seconds ]
[ Enhanced Muscle Density Lv2: Significantly increases muscle strength and physical durability. ]
[ Rapid Recovery Lv1: Slightly accelerates the recovery of damaged tissues and reduces recovery time from physical injuries. ]
"Overdrive Mutation... Interesting Skill..."
Kai slowly lowered the Status Crystal as he checked that there were only a few charges left...
A faint smile appeared on his face.
He had initially intended to rescue these people because they were victims.
Now he realized something else. They had potential... a lot of potential.
"If I bring all of them to the Codebreakers Shelter..."
Kai glanced at the survivors.
He began imagining what they could become after receiving proper food, equipment, training, and medical treatment.
Their current conditions were terrible.
But that could change.
He could give them better Gene Serums. Then, if he wanted them to fight, he could provide high-grade weapons, give them armor, or even find ways to help stabilize their mutations.
And resources?
Kai almost laughed.
He had the Infinite Gift Pack Talent.
As long as he had enough time, resources were hardly his biggest problem.
Food... water... medicine... weapons... serums... and equipment.
He could obtain all of them through Gift Packs.
Why would he leave these people behind?
Kai looked toward Farrah.
"They’re coming with us."
Farrah smiled.
"I was wondering when you’d say that."
Wilson immediately looked toward him.
"You... want us to join your shelter?"
"Yes."
Kai nodded.
"If you’re willing to work for the shelter, you’re welcome to stay."
The survivors exchanged glances.
Some looked shocked while others looked uncertain.
They had spent so long being treated as experiments that the idea of actually being accepted somewhere felt almost unreal.
Hanabi quietly held the Limb Reconstruction Capsule against her chest.
Wilson looked down at his mutated hands.
They could feel that despite being failed experiments, they were still survivors.
And perhaps, with Kai’s help, they could become something more.
Kai looked at the group before turning toward the damaged vehicles...
"If there’s no one against it... Then, I’ll fix these trucks so we can use them."

chapters.title: Chapter 392: Visitors
paragraphs: Kai turned his attention toward the black mechanical figure and couldn’t help but remember the massive upgrade Atom had undergone in the past.

After absorbing fifty Aetherium Ores, Atom had evolved from an A-Grade Sentinel into an S-Grade Sentinel. His durability had increased tremendously, his barrier generation had become far more efficient, and his operating duration had been greatly extended. He had also gained several new functions, including an Adaptive Energy Shield, a Self-Repair Protocol, and an Overdrive Mode that could temporarily increase his combat output by 200% when Spirit Energy was channeled into his core.
The Aetherium had even changed his appearance.
Atom’s previous metallic body had been replaced by a much darker black surface that almost seemed to absorb the surrounding light.
However, there was still something that hadn’t changed.
Atom couldn’t speak.

Even after becoming an S-Grade Sentinel, he still wasn’t capable of communicating through words. Kai had originally wondered whether the evolution would somehow unlock a proper communication system, but that clearly hadn’t happened.
So when Atom suddenly began walking toward him, Kai couldn’t help but become curious.
"What are you doing?"
As expected, Atom didn’t answer.
Instead, the S-Grade Sentinel simply walked past Kai and continued toward the second truck.
Kai turned around and followed him with his eyes.
"Atom?"
Atom stopped beside the vehicle before reaching out and placing one of his black mechanical hands against its metal exterior.
Kai frowned.
For a moment, nothing happened.
Then a faint glow suddenly appeared beneath Atom’s palm.
Kai immediately became alert.
"Chamber, scan it."
[ Scanning. ]
The result appeared almost immediately.
[ Aetherium detected. ]
Kai’s eyes widened.
"Aetherium?"
He quickly stepped closer.

The faint glow beneath Atom’s hand became brighter as something inside the truck began moving toward him. A few seconds later, a small amount of dark metallic material emerged from within the truck’s structure before disappearing directly into Atom’s hand.
Kai stared at the scene.
Apparently, the truck had been constructed with Aetherium integrated into some of its internal components.
He hadn’t noticed it.
Even Chamber hadn’t detected it during the initial inspection, but Atom had somehow sensed it.
The black Sentinel remained completely silent as the last traces of Aetherium disappeared into his body.
[ Atom’s aetherium absorption complete. ]
Kai looked at Atom.
"You found Aetherium inside the truck?"
Atom simply stood there and Kai couldn’t help but sigh.
"Right. You can’t answer me."

Still, Kai couldn’t help wondering whether Atom needed more Aetherium after his evolution. If the material had been responsible for his advancement once, perhaps absorbing more of it could provide additional benefits.
Unfortunately, asking Atom wouldn’t help.
Before Kai could ask Chamber to perform another scan, Atom suddenly turned and walked toward the next vehicle.
Kai followed him.
The same thing happened again.
Atom placed his hand against the truck, and after a brief moment, the hidden Aetherium inside the vehicle began flowing toward him.
Kai’s expression gradually became stranger.
"How many of these trucks have Aetherium inside them?"
Chamber immediately scanned the remaining vehicles.
[ Scanning for Aetherium. ]
A few seconds later, the results appeared.
[ Aetherium detected in Truck One. ]
[ Aetherium detected in Truck Three. ]
[ Aetherium detected in Truck Five. ]
Kai stared at the notifications.
"So they all have it?"
[ Correct. ]

Atom continued moving from one truck to another, silently absorbing the hidden Aetherium from each vehicle. There was no explosion or dramatic reaction. He simply touched the metal and absorbed the material directly into his core.
By the time he finished, all of the hidden Aetherium had been consumed.
Kai looked at him with curiosity.
"Does your core need more?... Never mind, there’s no point asking you."
Still, he wasn’t complaining. If there was more Aetherium available, he certainly wasn’t going to stop Atom from absorbing it.
Kai was about to ask Chamber to inspect Atom again when he suddenly heard the distant sound of engines.
He couldn’t help but frown at it...
Vroom!
Another engine roared in the distance, followed by several more.
Kai turned toward the road ahead...
Several pairs of headlights were approaching them. They were motorbikes!

Then, the rescued survivors noticed them as well, and the relaxed atmosphere around the trucks immediately disappeared. People who had been sitting around their coffee cups quickly stood up, while some of the stronger survivors instinctively moved closer to the others.
Well, they had picked up the various guns used by the Sentinels and Spyders a while ago, so they had something to use to protect themselves.
Meanwhile, Farrah also prepared her weapons and looked toward the approaching vehicles.
"Guys... Stay calm. Don’t shoot until we confirm if they’re hostile." Farrah reminded the nervous survivors.
She was worried that they would preemptively shoot the bikers and cause more trouble for them.
Soon, the sound of the engines grew louder as the group came closer.
There were more than a dozen motorcycles, and most of them carried two people. The riders were armed with rifles, swords, and various modified weapons.
Kai immediately understood what had happened.
The fires, lights, and movement around their temporary camp had probably attracted their attention.
The motorcycles slowed down as they approached the trucks before stopping several dozen meters away.
A man riding at the front raised his weapon.
"Stop right there!"
Kai remained where he was.
The leader looked past him and examined the trucks. His eyes then moved toward the group of survivors gathered around them.
His expression changed.
"You’ve got quite a few people with you."
Kai didn’t respond.
The man glanced at the supplies scattered around the camp before looking at the trucks again.
"Hand over your supplies and we’ll leave you alone."
Some of the rescued survivors immediately became nervous.
After everything they had experienced, the last thing they wanted was another group of armed people taking them away.
Kai, however, remained calm. These guys were actually so stupid, thinking that they could do whatever they wanted without properly assessing their strength.
"You should leave."
The leader laughed after hearing Kai’s warning...
But then, his eyes moved toward the unmoving Atom.
"What the hell is that thing?"
Atom stood silently beside Kai, his black body reflecting the faint light from the nearby fires.
The leader seemed uncertain for a moment, but the number of people behind him gave him confidence.
He raised his weapon that seemed to have been stolen from a Spyder Unit...
"Take the supplies."
Several motorcycles immediately accelerated... And Kai couldn’t help but sigh at their stupidity...
Apparently, the apocalypse hadn’t changed human nature as much as he had hoped.
He then activated Neural Acceleration.
The world around him seemed to slow as the motorcycles rushed toward them. Kai could clearly see the riders raising their weapons and spreading out in an attempt to surround the trucks.
At the same time, Atom finally moved.
The black S-Grade Sentinel accelerated forward and reached the first motorcycle before its rider could react!

Atom’s previous metallic body had been replaced by a much darker black surface that almost seemed to absorb the surrounding light.
However, there was still something that hadn’t changed.
Atom couldn’t speak.
Even after becoming an S-Grade Sentinel, he still wasn’t capable of communicating through words.
Kai had originally wondered whether the evolution would somehow unlock a proper communication system, but that clearly hadn’t happened.
So when Atom suddenly began walking toward him, Kai couldn’t help but become curious.
"What are you doing?"
As expected, Atom didn’t answer.
Instead, the S-Grade Sentinel simply walked past Kai and continued toward the second truck.
Kai turned around and followed him with his eyes.
"Atom?"
Atom stopped beside the vehicle before reaching out and placing one of his black mechanical hands against its metal exterior.
Kai frowned.
For a moment, nothing happened.
Then a faint glow suddenly appeared beneath Atom’s palm.
Kai immediately became alert.
"Chamber, scan it."
[ Scanning. ]
The result appeared almost immediately.
[ Aetherium detected. ]
Kai’s eyes widened.
"Aetherium?"
He quickly stepped closer.
The faint glow beneath Atom’s hand became brighter as something inside the truck began moving toward him.
A few seconds later, a small amount of dark metallic material emerged from within the truck’s structure before disappearing directly into Atom’s hand.
Kai stared at the scene.
Apparently, the truck had been constructed with Aetherium integrated into some of its internal components.
He hadn’t noticed it.
Even Chamber hadn’t detected it during the initial inspection, but Atom had somehow sensed it.
The black Sentinel remained completely silent as the last traces of Aetherium disappeared into his body.
[ Atom’s aetherium absorption complete. ]
Kai looked at Atom.
"You found Aetherium inside the truck?"
Atom simply stood there and Kai couldn’t help but sigh.
"Right.
You can’t answer me."
Still, Kai couldn’t help wondering whether Atom needed more Aetherium after his evolution.
If the material had been responsible for his advancement once, perhaps absorbing more of it could provide additional benefits.
Unfortunately, asking Atom wouldn’t help.
Before Kai could ask Chamber to perform another scan, Atom suddenly turned and walked toward the next vehicle.
Kai followed him.
The same thing happened again.
Atom placed his hand against the truck, and after a brief moment, the hidden Aetherium inside the vehicle began flowing toward him.
Kai’s expression gradually became stranger.
"How many of these trucks have Aetherium inside them?"
Chamber immediately scanned the remaining vehicles.
[ Scanning for Aetherium. ]
A few seconds later, the results appeared.
[ Aetherium detected in Truck One. ]
[ Aetherium detected in Truck Three. ]
[ Aetherium detected in Truck Five. ]
Kai stared at the notifications.
"So they all have it?"
[ Correct. ]
Atom continued moving from one truck to another, silently absorbing the hidden Aetherium from each vehicle.
There was no explosion or dramatic reaction.
He simply touched the metal and absorbed the material directly into his core.
By the time he finished, all of the hidden Aetherium had been consumed.
Kai looked at him with curiosity.
"Does your core need more?...
Never mind, there’s no point asking you."
Still, he wasn’t complaining.
If there was more Aetherium available, he certainly wasn’t going to stop Atom from absorbing it.
Kai was about to ask Chamber to inspect Atom again when he suddenly heard the distant sound of engines.
He couldn’t help but frown at it...
Vroom!
Another engine roared in the distance, followed by several more.
Kai turned toward the road ahead...
Several pairs of headlights were approaching them.
They were motorbikes!
Then, the rescued survivors noticed them as well, and the relaxed atmosphere around the trucks immediately disappeared.
People who had been sitting around their coffee cups quickly stood up, while some of the stronger survivors instinctively moved closer to the others.
Well, they had picked up the various guns used by the Sentinels and Spyders a while ago, so they had something to use to protect themselves.
Meanwhile, Farrah also prepared her weapons and looked toward the approaching vehicles.
"Guys...
Stay calm.
Don’t shoot until we confirm if they’re hostile." Farrah reminded the nervous survivors.
She was worried that they would preemptively shoot the bikers and cause more trouble for them.
Soon, the sound of the engines grew louder as the group came closer.
There were more than a dozen motorcycles, and most of them carried two people.
The riders were armed with rifles, swords, and various modified weapons.
Kai immediately understood what had happened.
The fires, lights, and movement around their temporary camp had probably attracted their attention.
The motorcycles slowed down as they approached the trucks before stopping several dozen meters away.
A man riding at the front raised his weapon.
"Stop right there!"
Kai remained where he was.
The leader looked past him and examined the trucks.
His eyes then moved toward the group of survivors gathered around them.
His expression changed.
"You’ve got quite a few people with you."
Kai didn’t respond.
The man glanced at the supplies scattered around the camp before looking at the trucks again.
"Hand over your supplies and we’ll leave you alone."
Some of the rescued survivors immediately became nervous.
After everything they had experienced, the last thing they wanted was another group of armed people taking them away.
Kai, however, remained calm.
These guys were actually so stupid, thinking that they could do whatever they wanted without properly assessing their strength.
"You should leave."
The leader laughed after hearing Kai’s warning...
But then, his eyes moved toward the unmoving Atom.
"What the hell is that thing?"
Atom stood silently beside Kai, his black body reflecting the faint light from the nearby fires.
The leader seemed uncertain for a moment, but the number of people behind him gave him confidence.
He raised his weapon that seemed to have been stolen from a Spyder Unit...
"Take the supplies."
Several motorcycles immediately accelerated...
And Kai couldn’t help but sigh at their stupidity...
Apparently, the apocalypse hadn’t changed human nature as much as he had hoped.
He then activated Neural Acceleration.
The world around him seemed to slow as the motorcycles rushed toward them.
Kai could clearly see the riders raising their weapons and spreading out in an attempt to surround the trucks.
At the same time, Atom finally moved.
The black S-Grade Sentinel accelerated forward and reached the first motorcycle before its rider could react!

chapters.title: Chapter 394: Return to the Shelter
paragraphs: Farrah’s curiosity grew when she heard the name.
"Stable Gene Enhancement Serum?"
She stepped closer and looked at the vial in Kai’s hand.
"Isn’t that different from the other Gene Enhancement Serums we’ve found?"
Kai nodded.
"That’s what I was thinking."
They had encountered several different types of Gene Enhancement Serums during the apocalypse.
There was the Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum, which provided balanced improvements to overall stats and offered a small chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
There was the Warrior Gene Enhancement Serum, which focused heavily on improving Physique.
The Super Gene Enhancement Serum provided smaller improvements but had a much higher chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Then there was the Mutagenic Gene Enhancement Serum.
That one was particularly dangerous because although it could provide massive improvements, it could also cause unpredictable mutations and severe drawbacks.
They had even encountered the Prime Gene Enhancement Serum, another powerful serum that focused on greatly improving Physique while providing a chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
However, the serum in Kai’s hand was different.
Stable.
That single word immediately caught Farrah’s attention.
"So what exactly makes it stable?" she asked.
Kai looked at the vial again. He read the description, but it wasn’t really that detailed.
"Well... It can reduce the risks caused by previous genetic modifications? That’s what it says."
Farrah immediately looked toward the rescued survivors.
The importance of the serum became obvious.
Many of them had undergone years of experimentation.

Their bodies had been injected with different substances, had their genes altered, and had even been implanted with mechanical components. Some had developed extreme mutations, while others had barely retained their original human appearance.
For ordinary survivors, a serum like this would already be valuable.
For them, it could be even more important.
"Then this might be exactly what they need," Farrah said.
Kai nodded.
"Maybe."
He wasn’t going to immediately give the serum to anyone.

The fact that it reduced genetic instability didn’t mean there were no risks at all. Their bodies had undergone extreme modifications, and Kai wanted to understand the serum properly before allowing anyone to consume it.
Of course, with an Alchemist waiting for them in the shelter, it would be better store this item for a while.
After all, if it could stabilize the bodies of the rescued survivors, they might finally have a chance to develop their abilities without constantly worrying about their mutations becoming worse.
Kai carefully stored the vials inside his Inventory.
"We’ll give them to Vera in the shelter..."
Farrah nodded.
"That’s probably for the best... She’s our only Alchemist."
Kai then looked at the pile of equipment they had collected from the attackers.

The weapons were nothing compared to his own equipment, but they were still useful. The Codebreakers Shelter had hundreds of survivors, and not everyone could be equipped with the advanced weapons Kai possessed.
Even damaged weapons and machine components could potentially be repaired or studied.
And now they had several Gene Enhancement Serums as well.
Kai made sure everything had been collected before returning to the trucks.
The rescued survivors were already preparing to leave.

The two repaired trucks were loaded with supplies, medical equipment, food, water, spare parts, weapons, and everything else they had gathered because of the excess from the gift pack and also from other trucks.
Kai also stored the remaining useful equipment inside his Inventory.
There was no reason to leave anything valuable behind.
After everything was ready, Wilson climbed into one of the trucks and carefully inspected the repaired engine one last time.
"It should hold," he said. "The repairs won’t last forever, but it should be enough to get us back."
Kai nodded.
"Good."
Wilson smiled faintly.
Hanabi was also helped into the truck, while the other survivors found places to sit.
Some were still weak, and several needed assistance simply to move around, but their condition was already much better than when Kai had first found them.
Farrah climbed onto one of the motorcycles they had taken from the attackers.
Kai looked at the road ahead.
The night had become colder, and the ruins around them were almost completely silent.
Somewhere beyond the darkness was the Codebreakers Shelter.
A place where these people could finally rest.
"Everyone ready?"
The survivors nodded.
Kai climbed onto his own vehicle and looked toward the two trucks.
"Then let’s go."
The engines roared to life.
One by one, the vehicles began moving down the road.
Kai stayed near the front while Farrah and Atom remained around the trucks, making sure nothing approached them from the sides.
Behind them were the fifty-eight rescued survivors, while Xian and Xinyi were in the front of the truck...
"I hope we get there already," Xinyi muttered as she really wanted to be within the protection of a safe shelter.
Being outside the city was already putting pressure on her.
Xian understood his sister and held her hands... "Don’t worry... Did you not see that black armored guy? He came from the Codebreakers Shelter, and he’s super strong, right? I think we’re safe now."
Xinyi’s eyes lit up...
"Right! I heard Sir Kai call him Atom!"
"Yes. Let’s greet Uncle Atom later."
"I will!"
In the meantime, within the Codebreakers Shelter, Maris received the news that Kai would be returning with a bunch of rescued people.
Needless to say, Kai had also requested some roasted chicken!

"Oh... Then this is going to be luxurious. I guess Kai wants those guys to stay with us. I don’t blame him. We need more manpower," Maris muttered as she looked at the two hundred or so chickens on the farm.
Only about 150 of them were hens, which meant they were the ones capable of laying eggs. Removing some of the others for meat wouldn’t be a huge problem at all.
Maris quickly began making preparations.

The shelter already had enough experience handling large groups of people, but sixty new survivors arriving at once was still a significant addition. They would need food, water, clothes, sleeping arrangements, and probably medical attention.
Fortunately, Kai had sent a message ahead of time, so they had some time to prepare before the group arrived.
Maris was only assigned to one thing...
Roasted chicken...
Soon, she walked toward the farm and looked at the chickens again.
"Alright, let’s see..."
She counted them for a moment before pointing toward several of the larger chickens.
"These ones should be enough."
As she said this, she noticed someone casually entering her space carrying a sculpture of a chicken...
"Eh?"

chapters.title: Chapter 395: Problem
paragraphs: Maris stared at the strange figure in Glen’s hands.
The man carrying it was none other than Glen, one of the survivors who had awakened a Rare-Grade Talent.

His Sculptor Talent allowed him to shape wood and stone with remarkable precision. Ordinary materials that would normally require hours of carving could be transformed within minutes, while his enhanced control over the material allowed him to create surprisingly detailed structures.
At first, Maris had thought the Talent would only be useful for making decorations.
However, Glen had already proven that it could be quite useful inside the shelter.

He had helped repair damaged walls, reinforce wooden structures, and create various tools and components whenever the shelter needed them. With enough materials, he could even reproduce complicated shapes with a level of precision that ordinary craftsmen would struggle to achieve.
But the thing he was carrying now was clearly different.
Glen carefully placed the sculpture on the ground.
"Maris! Look at this!"
Maris blinked.
It was a sculpture of a chicken.
But it wasn’t an ordinary wooden carving.

The body had been made primarily from carefully shaped wood, while several smaller sections had been reinforced with metal. The feathers had been carved individually, giving the sculpture an almost lifelike appearance. Even the eyes had been made from polished pieces of metal that reflected the surrounding light.
Maris stared at it for several seconds.
"It looks... surprisingly realistic."
Glen immediately puffed out his chest.
"Of course it does!"
He looked incredibly proud.
"This is my magnum opus!"
"Your what?"
"My greatest creation!"
Glen walked around the sculpture, admiring his own work.
"I spent an entire week working on it. I used different types of wood for the body, reinforced the internal structure with metal, and carefully carved every feather."
Maris looked at the sculpture again.
"Why a chicken?"
Glen’s expression became even more serious.
"Because chickens are important!"
Maris stared at him.
That was certainly one way to answer.
Glen then pointed toward the chickens wandering around the farm.
"But that’s not even the best part."
He placed his hand against the sculpture.
"This isn’t just decoration. I used my Talent to imbue the sculpture with a special effect."
Maris’s expression changed.
"What kind of effect?"
Glen smiled.
"It can enhance the chickens."
"Enhance them? Like iron feathers? Or maybe they can fly high now or something?"
"Exactly."
He proudly explained that the sculpture could subtly influence the chickens within its range, improving their biological efficiency and increasing their egg production.
"Under normal conditions, they can produce one egg."
Glen raised a finger.
"But with my sculpture nearby, they’ll be able to produce twice as many!"
Maris’s eyes widened.
"Twice as many?"
Glen nodded enthusiastically.
"Twice as many eggs!"
Maris immediately looked toward the chickens.
The shelter already had around two hundred chickens, and approximately 150 of them were hens.
If every hen could produce twice as many eggs, the increase in food production would be enormous.
She suddenly looked at the sculpture differently.
This wasn’t decoration.
It was an agricultural treasure.
"Glen."
"Yes?"
"I take back what I said about your Talent only being useful for repairs."
Glen laughed proudly.
"I told you my Talent was amazing!"
Maris couldn’t help but smile.
"You’re right. This is actually extremely useful."
With the shelter’s population continuing to grow, anything that increased their food production was valuable.
Eggs could be eaten directly, used for cooking, or even used to raise more chickens.
A simple increase in production could have a significant effect on the shelter’s long-term food supply.
Maris looked at the sculpture again.
"How long will this effect last?"
"As long as the sculpture remains intact and the chickens stay within its effective range."
"Then we’ll make sure nothing happens to it."
Glen nodded seriously.
"Don’t worry. I’ll protect my magnum opus with my life."
Maris almost laughed.
"Good. Then I’ll leave the chickens to you."
She glanced toward the farm before remembering something.
"Actually, I need your help with something else."
Glen looked at her curiously.
"What is it?"
"We’re preparing roasted chicken for tonight."
Maris pointed toward the larger chickens she had selected earlier.
"I want twenty of them prepared."
Glen’s expression immediately became serious.
"Twenty?"
"Yes. And I don’t want anything wasted."
Maris then looked toward the shelter.
"Go find Leron, Randel, and Emiru. Tell them I need their help cleaning the chickens."
Glen nodded.
"Got it."
"And make sure they keep everything."
"The feathers too?"
"Especially the feathers."
Maris smiled.
"We can use them for other things later. There’s no reason to throw away useful materials."
The shelter had already learned that even seemingly worthless materials could become valuable after the apocalypse.
The meat would become tonight’s meal.
The bones could be used for broth.
The organs could be cooked as well.
Even the fat could be rendered and stored for cooking.
Nothing needed to be wasted.
As for the feathers, Maris already had several ideas for how they could be used, whether for stuffing, insulation, or other practical purposes.
Glen nodded before carefully picking up his precious chicken sculpture.
"I’ll get them."
He turned around and started walking away.
Then he suddenly stopped.
"Maris."
"What?"
"Can you make sure nobody touches my chicken while I’m gone?"
Maris sighed.
"Yes, Glen. I’ll protect your precious chicken."
Glen smiled in satisfaction before finally leaving to find Leron, Randel, and Emiru.
Maris watched him disappear before turning back toward the farm.
She looked at the chickens... Then at the sculpture.
A smile slowly appeared on her face.
With this thing producing twice as many eggs, the shelter’s food supply was about to become even more ridiculous.
Not long after, Leron, Randel, and Emiru arrived at the farm.
The three immediately got to work. They began by butchering the twenty chickens Maris had selected, carefully draining the blood before plucking and processing the birds.
Nothing was wasted.

The meat would be used for the evening meal, while the organs and bones could also be prepared as food. Even the feathers were collected separately because Glen had already mentioned that they could be useful for other purposes.
With three people working together, they were able to process all twenty chickens surprisingly quickly.
After a while, Maris finally left...
Her next stop was the kitchen area, where Mila was already preparing for Kai’s return.
She soon found Mila in the kitchen, where she was checking on the preparations for tonight’s meal.
The kitchen was already bustling with activity.

Several people were preparing vegetables and other ingredients, while others were getting the cooking equipment ready. It seemed Kai had already informed them about the large group of survivors he was bringing back.
"How are things?" Maris asked.
Mila looked around the busy kitchen.
"Everything is going smoothly. We’re just waiting for the chickens. Once they’re ready, we can start roasting them. Though... I think we have a problem."

I’ll protect your precious chicken."
Glen smiled in satisfaction before finally leaving to find Leron, Randel, and Emiru.
Maris watched him disappear before turning back toward the farm.
She looked at the chickens...
Then at the sculpture.
A smile slowly appeared on her face.
With this thing producing twice as many eggs, the shelter’s food supply was about to become even more ridiculous.
Not long after, Leron, Randel, and Emiru arrived at the farm.
The three immediately got to work.
They began by butchering the twenty chickens Maris had selected, carefully draining the blood before plucking and processing the birds.
Nothing was wasted.
The meat would be used for the evening meal, while the organs and bones could also be prepared as food.
Even the feathers were collected separately because Glen had already mentioned that they could be useful for other purposes.
With three people working together, they were able to process all twenty chickens surprisingly quickly.
After a while, Maris finally left...
Her next stop was the kitchen area, where Mila was already preparing for Kai’s return.
She soon found Mila in the kitchen, where she was checking on the preparations for tonight’s meal.
The kitchen was already bustling with activity.
Several people were preparing vegetables and other ingredients, while others were getting the cooking equipment ready.
It seemed Kai had already informed them about the large group of survivors he was bringing back.
"How are things?" Maris asked.
Mila looked around the busy kitchen.
"Everything is going smoothly.
We’re just waiting for the chickens.
Once they’re ready, we can start roasting them.
Though...
I think we have a problem."

chapters.title: Chapter 396: New Item
paragraphs: "What problem?" Maris asked.
Mila pointed toward the large cooking area.
"We don’t have enough ovens."
Maris blinked.
"What?"
"We can prepare twenty chickens, but roasting all of them is another matter."
Mila gestured toward the kitchen.

"The shelter’s cooking equipment was originally set up for our existing population. We have enough pots, pans, and stoves to prepare ordinary meals, but roasting twenty whole chickens at once would take much longer than you think."
Maris looked toward the single large oven.
It suddenly seemed much smaller than before.
"Can’t we just roast them in batches?"
"We can."
Mila sighed.
"But then the first batch will be finished long before the last one. By the time everything is ready, Kai and the new survivors might already be starving."
Maris couldn’t help but laugh.
"Of all the problems we could have tonight, we ran out of ovens."
Mila looked completely serious.
"And considering how much Kai likes giving people ridiculous amounts of food, I have a feeling this won’t be the last time."
Maris was about to respond when she suddenly remembered something.
"Kai’s Gift Packs."
Mila’s eyes widened slightly.
"Do you think he has something that can help?"
Maris smiled.
"With Kai? There’s a good chance. We should ask Sera about it..."
Sera was one of the trusted people guarding the vault where Kai’s Gift Packs were stored. If they informed her of their predicament, they were sure that she’d be willing to assist them.
However, before either of them could say anything else, hurried footsteps suddenly came from outside the kitchen.
Someone was running toward them.
"Everyone!"
She turned around.
A messenger rushed into the kitchen, breathing heavily.
"We found a Gene Trader!"
Maris’s expression immediately changed.
"A Gene Trader?"
"Yes! One of the patrol groups discovered him nearby. He’s not too far from the outer checkpoint! If you have Survivor Medals, you can visit it and trade something!"
Mila looked at Maris.
Maris looked back at her.
The kitchen problem was suddenly forgotten.
A Gene Trader had appeared near the shelter at almost exactly the same time Kai was returning with fifty-eight rescued survivors.
That was far more interesting than twenty chickens.
"Nice! I have 15 Survivor Medals here! I want another batch of Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum!"
"Me too..."
"Not everyone can go! Just let a couple of people purchase what you want!"
Just like that, Maris immediately left the area as she took out her 15 Survivor Medals!
Maris soon followed several other survivors from the Codebreakers Shelter as they made their way toward the location where the Gene Trader had been discovered.
The patrol that found the mysterious merchant had marked the route carefully, and it did not take long before Maris and the others reached the outskirts of the area.
An abandoned building stood ahead of them.

Most of its windows had been shattered, and weeds had already grown through cracks in the walls. The surrounding streets were eerily quiet, with only the occasional sound of wind passing through the ruins.
However, there was something strange about the area.
Several people had gathered around the building, but none of the ordinary residents of this world were approaching it.
Well, the Gene Trader’s unique nature made it impossible for native survivors to freely approach him.
Whenever a native resident came too close, mutated creatures would eventually be attracted to the area.
Because of this, only Foreign Survivors were allowed to approach the Gene Trader safely.
People who had come from Earth and been brought into this world by the System could enter without triggering the same reaction.
Maris was one of them.
She looked around and quickly recognized several familiar faces from the Codebreakers Shelter.
Wallace was standing near the entrance, discussing something with Victor.
Ralph was nearby, carefully counting the Survivor Medals in his hand, while Aurora and Elena were already looking through the available items displayed by the Gene Trader.
"So you’re thinking about buying the Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum too?" Victor asked.
Wallace nodded.
"Of course. Four Survivor Medals for something that can improve our physique and potentially awaken a Gene Skill is worth it."
"I agree," Ralph said. "But I’m actually considering the Gene Skill Crystal. If I get lucky, I might awaken something useful."
"How many medals do you have?" Aurora asked.
"Twenty-three."
"Then don’t waste them all," Elena immediately warned him. "The Gene Trader might have something even better later."
Ralph scratched his head.
"That’s exactly why I’m having trouble deciding."
Maris smiled faintly as she approached them.
"You all got here quickly."
Everyone turned toward her.
"Maris."
"You’re here too?"
"Did you bring your Survivor Medals?"
Maris nodded.
"Fifteen."
"I have the same amount," Wallace said. "I’m planning to buy three Alpha Gene Enhancement Serums."
"Me too," Maris replied. "I came here for the same reason."
The group continued discussing their choices while several other Foreign Survivors entered the abandoned building one after another.
Inside, the atmosphere was completely different from the outside.
The building was dark, with most of the sunlight blocked by pieces of cloth and broken wooden boards covering the windows.
At the center of the room sat a mysterious cloaked figure.
His face remained hidden beneath the hood, and several strange items were placed around him.
The moment Maris stepped closer, a familiar System interface appeared before her.
[ Gene Trader’s Store ]
[ Survivor Medal Items ]
Various items appeared on the display, and Maris immediately recognized many of them.
Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum.
Prime Gene Enhancement Serum.
Super Gene Enhancement Serum.
Gene Stabilization Pills.
Gene Skill Crystals.
Status Crystals.
Limb Reconstruction Capsules.
There were even several weapons and strange pieces of equipment.
Maris looked through the list carefully.
She had already decided what she wanted.
Three Alpha Gene Enhancement Serums.
That would cost her exactly twelve Survivor Medals, leaving her with three.
It was a simple choice.
The Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum had already proven itself valuable to the shelter, and with the number of survivors they had, strengthening more people could make a significant difference.
While Maris was preparing to make her purchase, she suddenly heard a surprised voice from deeper inside the building.
"Wait!"
Everyone turned toward the sound.
"What?"
"Did you see this?"
"What’s wrong?"
The voice came from one of the survivors standing closest to the Gene Trader.
The man stared at the System interface in disbelief.
"There is a new item!"

chapters.title: Chapter 397: More Items
paragraphs: "There is a new item!"
The survivor’s voice immediately attracted everyone’s attention.
"A new item?"
"What is it?"
"Show us!"
The survivor quickly moved aside so the others could see the newly added item on the System interface.
Maris looked at the description.
Her eyes widened slightly.
[ Owlwing Mutation Serum ]
[ Price: 40 Survivor Medals ]

[ Description: A highly specialized genetic serum that forces a guaranteed Owlwing mutation within the user’s body. The mutation will cause a pair of large owl-like wings to gradually develop from the user’s back, granting the ability to fly once the transformation is complete. ]

[ Mutation Progress: The wings will gradually form over approximately 7 days. During this period, the user’s back may experience severe pain, swelling, and abnormal tissue growth as the body develops the new organs. ]
[ Mutation Completion: Once the wings have completely formed, they will become fully functional and can be used for sustained flight. ]
[ Warning: The mutation is permanent. The resulting wings cannot be removed through ordinary medical treatment. ]
For several seconds, nobody spoke as they studied the new item.
Then someone finally broke the silence.
"Forty Survivor Medals?"
"That’s expensive."
"But... flying?"
A few survivors immediately became interested.
"If I could fly, I’d be able to scout entire areas without worrying about the roads."
"That would also be useful for escaping mutated creatures."
"Seven days of pain isn’t that bad if it really gives you the ability to fly."
"Not that bad?" Another survivor looked at him incredulously. "It says severe pain! Also, you have wings! How can you sleep with wings on your back!"
"It has feather... Maybe it’s comfy..."
"What if it’s not. You have to sleep face down forever!"
The first survivor immediately fell silent.
Maris continued reading the description as the mutation was guaranteed.
There was no chance of failure.
After seven days, the wings would completely form and become usable.
That alone made the item extremely valuable.
However, the price was also considerably higher than the ordinary Gene Enhancement Serums.
And unlike a normal Gene Skill, the wings would physically change the user’s body.
Only a handful of people seemed genuinely excited about the new item.
Most of the others were hesitant.
"Now that I think about it... I don’t think I want wings growing out of my back."
"Same."
"Just like what the other guy said... Imagine trying to sleep."
"Or wearing normal clothes."
"What if the wings get injured?"
The excitement quickly died down.
Maris couldn’t blame them.
The ability to fly was certainly tempting, but not everyone would be willing to undergo such a drastic and permanent mutation.
Still, the appearance of the Owlwing Mutation Serum proved that the Gene Trader’s inventory could change.
That realization made everyone much more interested.
"Keep looking," Wallace said.
"What?"
"If a new item appeared in the Survivor Medal section, there might be new items in the other sections too."
The others immediately began searching through the Gene Trader’s store.
They checked the different categories one after another.
After several moments, someone suddenly stopped.
"Wait."
"What did you find?"
"The Experience Points section."
Everyone gathered around again.
The Gene Trader had always offered a separate selection of items that could not be purchased with Survivor Medals.
Instead, they required Experience Points.

The previous Gene Trader’s inventory had mostly consisted of old-world supplies and equipment, including EMP Grenades, preserved spices, maps, gas masks, protective goggles, coffee, mechanical watches, old laptops, cameras, cooking utensils, and other relics from before the apocalypse.
But now...
There were several new items.
Maris stared at the list.
[ Experience Points Items ]
[ Items Sold for Experience Points ]
[ Portable Solar Generator ]
[ Price: 15,000 EXP ]

[ Description: A compact solar-powered generator capable of storing and supplying electrical energy. Can power small household appliances, lights, communication equipment, and other compatible devices. ]
[ Portable Water Purification Device ]
[ Price: 12,000 EXP ]
[ Description: A compact purification device capable of filtering contaminated water and removing most harmful bacteria, parasites, and common pollutants. Requires a power source to operate. ]
[ Medical Scanner ]
[ Price: 20,000 EXP ]
[ Description: Advanced medical scanning device capable of analyzing the user’s physical condition and detecting injuries, organ abnormalities, infections, and other biological problems. ]
[ Refrigeration Storage Box ]
[ Price: 8,000 EXP ]

[ Description: A portable insulated storage container equipped with a low-power cooling system. Maintains a stable internal temperature for extended periods, allowing food, medicine, and other temperature-sensitive supplies to be preserved. ]
[ Advanced Flashlight ]
[ Price: 3,000 EXP ]
[ Description: High-powered rechargeable flashlight capable of producing intense illumination over a large area. Includes adjustable brightness and emergency signaling functions. ]
[ Long-Range Communication Radio ]
[ Price: 10,000 EXP ]
[ Description: Advanced radio capable of transmitting and receiving signals over extremely long distances. Includes multiple communication channels and enhanced interference resistance. ]
[ Portable Cooking Station ]
[ Price: 7,000 EXP ]

[ Description: Compact cooking station equipped with an integrated heating system and multiple cooking surfaces. Designed for preparing meals in environments without access to conventional kitchens. ]
The room became noticeably quieter as everyone read through the list.
These items were completely different from the old-world relics.
They weren’t particularly powerful weapons.
They weren’t rare Gene Skills... but they were practical items.
Yet in the apocalypse, that made them incredibly valuable.
"They’re nice... But these things can be obtained from Kai’s Gift Packs, right?"
Wallace stared at the item.
"That’s true... But this shows that we can get more unique items here."
Victor nodded.
"It’s a good option for other Survivors for sure. But not if you’re with Kai..."
They all knew how difficult it was to accumulate Experience Points.
Unlike Survivor Medals, which could be obtained through certain System activities and rewards, Experience Points were primarily earned through combat and other actions that granted experience.
Spending tens of thousands of EXP on a single item was not something an ordinary survivor could casually afford.
Maris looked at the new inventory again.
The Gene Trader was becoming more mysterious by the minute.
Not only could he provide genetic enhancements and strange equipment, but his inventory was also expanding.
And if new items could suddenly appear without warning...
Then nobody knew what the Gene Trader might offer the next time he appeared.
"Wait..."
Someone suddenly pointed toward the bottom of the list.
"There are more."
